build: Yeti's one-file crack, WIZBALL    /YETI on the c64.com disk WWW.C64HQ.COM (with Impact's and Remember's cracks beside it); the game starts at $6389

exclude: title sprites $80-$8E; in play the score rows and landscape screen 0, drawn at run time
unused, and screen 0's sprite pointers, written by the play bands
landscape screen 1, drawn at run time
level-digit sprite $A0 and landscape screen 2, drawn at run time
text screen of the title, menus and get-ready screen; sprites and icon pointers in play
bottom band's sprite pointers, written every frame
star glyphs, cleared and plotted at run time
level glyphs, copied in for each level from the blocks at $0B42

comments.text: 6510 data-direction register. The traced code never writes it. Six self-modified calls carry $0000 as the placeholder operand that their real target replaces before they run: JMP $7316 (the icon handler, from $B549), JSR $7C9D (the raster band routine, from the display list), JSR $83D0 and JSR $83E1 (bounce handlers, from $B3BE), JSR $A6CB and JMP $A6DC (alien bounces, from $B28C). A flow trace that follows them marks zero page as code.

6510 processor port. The game's entry at $6389 writes $35 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000) and no other traced instruction, nor any byte pattern STA/STX/STY $01 in the image, writes it again.

Voice 1: index of its call and loop stack (addresses at $E4/$E9 + level, loop counts at $EE + level). load_tune sets 4, empty ($4820); a call ($48FF) or a repeat start ($4981) stores at the index and decrements it; a return ($4A09) or a finished repeat ($4A03) increments it. NMI watchdog. The NMI ($7C61) writes 0 here once a frame; band $8BBB sets it to the $D011 value at raster line $F7 in play, the title bands $936A-$93C5 increment it through INC $FFB0,X with X = $D5 (which wraps to $0085), and $B589 decrements it through DCP $FF97,X. The checks at $8B04 and $9287 (LAX $86, DCP $FF86,X, both in undocumented opcodes) pass only if the NMI has cleared it since, and otherwise crash the game through an unbalanced stack.

Holds $FF, written once by the initialisation at $EC4B. The watchdog checks at $8B04 and $9287 load it with LAX $86 and use it as the index of DCP $FF86,X, which wraps to $0085; any other value would send the check elsewhere.

Voice 3 live sound state byte 10 ($C1 + 10): ticks of pitch step 3 (arpeggio mode: the base note, which the note start replaces with note + transpose); used at $48EC, $5090, $50C8, $549F.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 11 ($C1 + 11): ticks of pitch step 4 (arpeggio mode: the first table index; the table is read from it down to 0, then again); used at $48E8, $508C, $5495.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 12 ($C1 + 12): ticks before the pitch steps begin (arpeggio mode: the current table index); used at $5088, $547C, $5480, $5491, $54A5.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 13 ($C1 + 13): pitch-effect mode, from template byte 13 (0 = no pitch update); used at $5082, $546F, $5482, $54FF.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 14 ($C1 + 14): pulse step 1 tick count, reloaded into byte 33 when the sweep repeats; used at $4878, $5078.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 15 ($C1 + 15): pulse step 2 tick count, reloaded into byte 34 when the sweep repeats; used at $487C, $507C.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 16 ($C1 + 16): pulse delay, counted down each tick; used at $5072, $5421, $5425.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 17 ($C1 + 17): pulse sweep mode, from template byte 17 (0 = no sweep); used at $5054, $541D, $5451.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 18 ($C1 + 18): pulse step 1, low byte; used at $506E, $5436.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 19 ($C1 + 19): pulse step 1, high byte; used at $506A, $543A.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 20 ($C1 + 20): pulse step 2, low byte; used at $5066, $5447.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 21 ($C1 + 21): pulse step 2, high byte; used at $5062, $544B.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 22 ($C1 + 22): pulse width at the note start, low byte (where a restarting sweep begins again); used at $4870, $5058.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 23 ($C1 + 23): pulse width at the note start, high byte; used at $4872, $505A.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 24 ($C1 + 24): the note's frequency, low byte (base of the pitch steps and of their restarts); used at $48E0, $5028.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 25 ($C1 + 25): the note's frequency, high byte; used at $48E2, $502A.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 26 ($C1 + 26): control register value as written at the note start; the gate-off clears bits 0 and 3; used at $5048, $53DB, $53EB, $53EF, $5416.

Voice 3 live sound state byte 27 ($C1 + 27): gate time, counted down to the gate-off (or compared with the note time left when control bit 3 is set); $FF holds; used at $50D3, $53E3, $53E9, $53F3, $540D, $5412.

Voice 3 live sound state byte 28 ($C1 + 28): release time, counted down after the gate-off; $FF holds; 0 = voice idle, the per-tick update returns at once; used at $47E5, $50D5, $53D7, $53F7, $53FC, $551F.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 29 ($C1 + 29): ticks left in pitch step 1; used at $48F6, $54B6, $54BA.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 30 ($C1 + 30): ticks left in pitch step 2; used at $48F2, $54C6, $54CA.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 31 ($C1 + 31): ticks left in pitch step 3; used at $48EE, $54D6, $54DA.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 32 ($C1 + 32): ticks left in pitch step 4; used at $48EA, $54E6, $54EA.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 33 ($C1 + 33): ticks left in pulse step 1; used at $487A, $507A, $542F, $5433.
Voice 3 live sound state byte 34 ($C1 + 34): ticks left in pulse step 2; used at $487E, $507E, $5440, $5444.

Voice 1 return addresses, low bytes, five levels $E4-$E8 (the index $0D runs from 4 down to 0 as the stack fills): a call ($4906) or a repeat start ($4988) stores the address to come back to at $E4 + level. This byte is level 0.
Voice 1 return address low bytes of levels 1-4 ($E5-$E8), read back by the repeat end ($49F8: LDY $E5,X with X = the index, one below the level pushed) and the return ($4A11).
Voice 1 return addresses, high bytes, level 0 ($E9-$ED hold levels 0-4; stored at $490C and $498E).
Voice 1 return address high bytes of levels 1-4 ($EA-$ED), read back at $49FA and $4A13.
Voice 1 loop counters, five bytes $EE-$F2, one per stack level: command $CC stores the repeat count at $EE + level ($4992). This byte is level 0.
Voice 1 loop counters of levels 1-4 ($EF-$F2), counted down by command $CE ($49F4: DEC $EF,X); the section repeats until the count reaches 0, so a count of 0 gives 256 passes.
Voice 2 return addresses, low bytes, five levels $F3-$F7 (index $0E): a call ($4A52) or a repeat start ($4AC1) stores at $F3 + level. This byte is level 0.
Voice 2 return address low bytes of levels 1-4 ($F4-$F7), read back by the repeat end ($4B19) and the return ($4B32).
Voice 2 return addresses, high bytes, level 0 ($F8-$FC hold levels 0-4; stored at $4A58 and $4AC7).
Voice 2 return address high bytes of levels 1-4 ($F9-$FC), read back at $4B1B and $4B34. The last three bytes of zero page, $FD-$FF, are referenced by no traced instruction.

Alien slots: six records of 42 bytes at $0200-$02FB, slot n at $0200 + 42n and drawn on sprite n + 2, run once a frame by update_aliens ($A204); create_alien ($9DA1) fills one from an alien template ($3ECF) or a bonus-stage template ($39DC). This label names byte $00 of slot 0, and the code reaches the other slots with X = 42n: the X position in 2-pixel units (sprite X is twice this plus the fraction's top bit).
Alien slot byte $01: the X position's fraction ($A3CB-$A3E1).
Alien slot byte $02: the line (sprite Y). 0 marks the slot empty, which every search for a free slot tests (LDA $0202,X / BEQ at $A223, $AA34, $A189, $9D44).
Alien slot byte $03: the line's fraction.
Alien slot byte $04: X speed, whole part (an acceleration in movement mode 3); reversed by the scenery bounces $A6DF and $A6E5.
Alien slot byte $05: X speed, fraction.
Alien slot byte $06: Y speed, whole part (an acceleration in mode 3); reversed by $A707 and $A70D.
Alien slot byte $07: Y speed, fraction.
Alien slot byte $08: movement mode for move_alien ($A386): 0 the Y speed grows by byte $09 a frame (falling), 1 it shrinks (rising), 2 steered by the pattern's direction bits, 3 accelerated by them.
Alien slot byte $09: the Y acceleration in modes 0 and 1 ($A395, $A3A7); for a colour-cycling alien, the cycle's frame counter ($A2CF).
Alien slot byte $0A: movement pattern pointer, low byte (read with byte $0B at $A3FA).
Alien slot byte $0B: movement pattern pointer, high byte.
Alien slot byte $0C: frames per movement pattern step ($A3ED).

Alien slot byte $0D: 0 passes through the scenery; 1 bounces off scenery and off the line limits $46-$C7 ($A665, $A678, $A688). 2 or more would skip the limits; no template uses it (and $A6B1 tests slot 0's byte, not the current slot's).
Alien slot byte $0E: firing mode for fire_alien_shots ($A541): 0 none, 1 aimed at the Wizball, 2 turning, 3 eight ways.
Alien slot byte $0F: frames between shots, compared exactly with the fire timer, byte $21 ($A547).

Alien slot byte $10: the sprite colour in the low bits ($10 there means colour cycling). Bit 5 set: a pearl whenever it is killed; bit 6: a hi-res sprite; bit 7: a police ship, which sounds the siren while alive.
Alien slot byte $11: animation mode for animate_alien ($A5B1): 0 one fixed frame, 1 the bounce wobble, 2 or more a frame list; while a droplet falls, its wobble index.
Alien slot byte $12: the fixed frame, wobble index or frame-list period; in states 2 to 4 (droplet, splash, explosion) the frame counter.
Alien slot byte $13: frame-list pointer, low byte; for colour cycling the cycle index, and the fade-in counter while byte $14 is 1.
Alien slot byte $14: frame-list pointer, high byte; 1 runs the fade-in ($A319).

Alien slot byte $15: the state a hit is dispatched on ($A830): 0 alien, 1 colour sphere, 2 droplet falling, 3 droplet splashing, 4 exploding, 5 pearl, 6 the Wiz lookalike of the bonus stage, 7 unused, $FF shrugs hits off (bonus template 7).
Alien slot byte $16: its value in tens of points, passed to add_score ($710B) at $A891 and $A941.
Alien slot byte $17: X velocity in movement mode 3, whole part ($A498-$A4CD).
Alien slot byte $18: X velocity in mode 3, fraction.
Alien slot byte $19: Y velocity in mode 3, whole part ($A4D6-$A50B).
Alien slot byte $1A: Y velocity in mode 3, fraction.
Alien slot byte $1B: index into the movement pattern ($A3F7, $A404).
Alien slot byte $1C: timer to the next pattern step ($A3E7).
Alien slot byte $1D: hit box, left edge (X - 3, set by set_alien_hitbox $A744). The shot collision test at $6FBE is unrolled and names every slot's box directly.
Alien slot byte $1E: hit box, right edge (X + 7).
Alien slot byte $1F: hit box, top (line - 3).
Alien slot byte $20: hit box, bottom (line + $13). Zeroing the top and bottom makes an alien untouchable ($A8A1, $A1D8, $7E85, $88D2).
Alien slot byte $21: frames since its last shot ($A541).
Alien slot byte $22: the direction of turning fire ($A56D).
Alien slot byte $23: the animation timer ($A5CD, $A61B).
Alien slot byte $24: the sprite shape, copied to the slot's sprite pointer by show_alien_sprite ($A2EF).

Alien slot byte $25: the hit flag, set by the shot collision test ($6FD4 for slot 0) and for every slot by the smart bomb ($7394), handled and cleared by run_hit_alien ($A7F2). Bytes $26 and $27 after it are used by no traced code.
Alien slot byte $28: the address of the slot's entry in the landscape's wave list, low byte ($AA6F), so that the entry can be marked or given back; 0, with byte $29, when there is none.
Alien slot byte $29: that address, high byte ($AA74, $A1DE, $A284). This label's span runs on over bytes $00-$1C of slot 1 ($022A-$0246), the same fields as above.
Alien slot 1 ($022A-$0253): hit box left edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 1 ($022A-$0253): hit box right edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 1 ($022A-$0253): hit box top, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 1 ($022A-$0253): hit box bottom, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.

Alien slot 1 ($022A): its hit flag, set by the unrolled shot collision test and by the smart bomb. Its span runs on over bytes $26-$29 of slot 1 and bytes $00-$1C of slot 2 ($0254-$0270), the fields described at $0200.
Alien slot 2 ($0254-$027D): hit box left edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 2 ($0254-$027D): hit box right edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 2 ($0254-$027D): hit box top, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 2 ($0254-$027D): hit box bottom, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.

Alien slot 2 ($0254): its hit flag, set by the unrolled shot collision test and by the smart bomb. Its span runs on over bytes $26-$29 of slot 2 and bytes $00-$1C of slot 3 ($027E-$029A), the fields described at $0200.
Alien slot 3 ($027E-$02A7): hit box left edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 3 ($027E-$02A7): hit box right edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 3 ($027E-$02A7): hit box top, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 3 ($027E-$02A7): hit box bottom, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.

Alien slot 3 ($027E): its hit flag, set by the unrolled shot collision test and by the smart bomb. Its span runs on over bytes $26-$29 of slot 3 and bytes $00-$1C of slot 4 ($02A8-$02C4), the fields described at $0200.
Alien slot 4 ($02A8-$02D1): hit box left edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 4 ($02A8-$02D1): hit box right edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 4 ($02A8-$02D1): hit box top, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 4 ($02A8-$02D1): hit box bottom, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.

Alien slot 4 ($02A8): its hit flag, set by the unrolled shot collision test and by the smart bomb. Its span runs on over bytes $26-$29 of slot 4 and bytes $00-$1C of slot 5 ($02D2-$02EE), the fields described at $0200.
Alien slot 5 ($02D2-$02FB): hit box left edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 5 ($02D2-$02FB): hit box right edge, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 5 ($02D2-$02FB): hit box top, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.
Alien slot 5 ($02D2-$02FB): hit box bottom, named directly by the unrolled shot collision test at $6FBE.

Alien slot 5 ($02D2): its hit flag, set by the unrolled shot collision test and by the smart bomb. Its span covers bytes $26-$29 of slot 5 and the four spare bytes $02FC-$02FF after the last slot, which nothing uses.

Alien bullets: sixteen records of 16 bytes at $0300-$03FF, handled by move_alien_bullets ($99BD), half of them each frame, and drawn as characters $5B-$6A over the landscape. This label names byte 0 of record 0: the screen column.
Alien bullet byte 1: the screen row.
Alien bullet byte 2: the position across the character cell, 0-31; with byte 3 it places the bullet, which is drawn as one of the 16 characters $5B-$6A, a dot at one of 16 places in the cell.
Alien bullet byte 3: the position down the character cell, 0-31.
Alien bullet byte 4: X speed, signed.
Alien bullet byte 5: Y speed, signed.
Alien bullet byte 6: the landscape character under the bullet, put back when it moves.
Alien bullet byte 7: its screen address, high byte.
Alien bullet byte 8: its screen address, low byte (also the colour RAM's low byte).
Alien bullet byte 9: its colour RAM page.
Alien bullet byte $0A: 0 free, 2 just fired, 1 flying.
Alien bullet byte $0B: the colour counter that makes it flash. Bytes $0C-$0F of each record are not used; this label's span covers them and records 1-3 ($0310-$034A).

Alien bullet records from byte $0B of record 4 to record 9 ($034B-$03A8), laid out as record 0 at $0300 and reached only through the index. In the hand-over image $034C-$0353 hold LDA $DD0D, CLD, SEI, JMP $6389: by their place and their jump to the game's entry, the end of the depacker that ran in pages 1-3. The initialisation's fill of pages 1-3 ($EC6F-$EC7F) overwrites it before the game uses the table.

False symbol: the operand of BIT $03A9 at $48FE, $4A4A and $4B6B in the music driver, where the bytes A9 03 are really LDA #$03 for code that enters one byte later (the skip idiom: LDA #$04 / BIT $03A9 loads 4 or, entered at the operand, 3). No code reads $03A9. The span from here to $03E7 lies inside alien bullet records 10-14.

False symbol: $03E8 is the placeholder operand of the self-modifying copy loops in build_scroll_buffer ($787A-$7883, operands rewritten at $7819-$7873) and at $7A78-$7A8A (rewritten at $7A55/$7A5A); the real addresses are screen rows. No code uses $03E8 itself. The span to $03FF lies inside alien bullet records 14 and 15.

Sound-effect slots: three of 32 bytes, $0400 for voice 1, $0420 voice 2, $0440 voice 3 (offsets from the table at $BA7B). start_sound_effect ($4553) copies an effect's record into the slot of the voice its byte 0 names ($45B1), and $B960 works a slot once a frame for each voice the music leaves free (from $B90C). The copy takes 25 bytes of a 24-byte record, so byte 24 is the next record's voice, which nothing reads; bytes 24-31 of a slot are unused. This label names byte 0: the voice, 1-3.
Effect slot byte 1: the priority, lower number wins: a new effect replaces the one playing only if its number is not higher ($459A), unless the slot counts as free (byte 2 at 0).

Effect slot byte 2: the first time counter, frames with the gate on, counted down at $BA64. start_sound_effect takes the slot as free when it is 0 ($4592), even while byte 3 still runs. $BAAD clears bytes 2 and 3 of all three slots (this one at $BAB7).
Effect slot byte 3: the second time counter, counted down once byte 2 is 0, the gate still on ($BA6F); when both are 0 the control register gets 0 ($BA77). Two counters make up to 510 frames.
Effect slot byte 4: the control register value (waveform), written with the gate bit set while either time counter runs ($BA72).
Effect slot byte 5: attack/decay, written to the voice's register every frame ($BA3B).

Effect slot byte 6: 0 in every record, so on a new effect's first frame $B960 writes 0 to the voice's control register, which takes the gate off so that the envelope starts again, and sets this to 1 ($B965).
Effect slot byte 7: the frequency, low byte, stepped up or down each frame ($B999-$B9BF) and written to the voice's frequency register ($BA47).
Effect slot byte 8: the frequency, high byte (stepped at $B9A5-$B9CE, written at $BA4D).
Effect slot byte 9: the frequency step, low byte, added while the sweep rises ($B99D) and subtracted while it falls ($B9BC).
Effect slot byte 10: the frequency step, high byte ($B9AC, $B9CB).
Effect slot byte 11: frames of rising frequency, loaded into the counter (byte 20) when the sweep turns upwards ($B977).
Effect slot byte 12: frames of falling frequency, loaded into the counter when the sweep turns downwards ($B989); a count of 0 gives 256 frames.
Effect slot byte 13: the pulse width, low byte, stepped each frame ($BA00-$BA26) and written to the voice's pulse register ($BA53).
Effect slot byte 14: the pulse width, high byte (stepped at $BA0C-$BA35, written at $BA59).
Effect slot byte 15: the pulse width step, low byte, added at $BA04 and subtracted at $BA23.
Effect slot byte 16: the pulse width step, high byte ($BA13, $BA32).
Effect slot byte 17: frames of widening pulse, loaded into the counter (byte 22) when the pulse sweep turns upwards ($B9DE).
Effect slot byte 18: frames of narrowing pulse, loaded when it turns downwards ($B9F0).
Effect slot byte 19: the frequency sweep's direction, 1 rising, 0 falling; it turns when the counter, byte 20, is found at 0 ($B96D-$B991).
Effect slot byte 20: frames left in the frequency sweep's current direction, counted down every frame ($B996, $B9B5).
Effect slot byte 21: the pulse sweep's direction, 1 widening, 0 narrowing ($B9D4-$B9F8).
Effect slot byte 22: frames left in the pulse sweep's current direction ($B9FD, $BA1C).

Effect slot byte 23: sustain/release, written to the voice's register every frame ($BA41). This label's span runs over the unused bytes 24-31 ($0418-$041F) and bytes 0 and 1 of voice 2's slot ($0420, $0421).

Voice 2's effect slot ($0420-$043F), byte 2: its first time counter, cleared by $BAAD at $BABD and tested directly by $7DF7 and $AAA6, which start effect $18 (the background sound) whenever it is 0, and on every 256th pass anyway (the counter $7DF3).
Voice 2's effect slot, byte 3: its second time counter, cleared at $BAC0. This label's span covers the rest of that slot and bytes 0 and 1 of voice 3's ($0440, $0441).
Voice 3's effect slot ($0440-$045F), byte 2: its first time counter, cleared at $BAC3.
Voice 3's effect slot, byte 3: its second time counter, cleared at $BAC6. This label's span runs to the end of the slot, $045F.
Landscape map row addresses, low bytes, rows 0-15 (row r at $0532 + 96r), loaded with the game and never changed; read at $758F and $78E6 with the high bytes at $0470.
Landscape map row addresses, high bytes, rows 0-15 ($05 to $0A).

The shot table: six records of 12 bytes at $0480-$04C7, moved and drawn as characters by $6F0D once a frame: records 0 and 1 the Wiz's shots ($8467), 2 the cat's ($881F), 3-5 the spray ($850A). This label names byte 0 of record 0: the screen column.
Shot byte 1: the screen row.
Shot byte 2: the column step each move, +1 or -1 for straight fire, the spray's direction otherwise.
Shot byte 3: the row step (0 for straight fire).
Shot byte 4: the character drawn; 0 means the slot is free. $6FBE clears it when the shot hits an alien.
Shot byte 5: its colour: 7, 12 with blazers, 11 for the spray.
Shot byte 6: the landscape character under the shot, put back by erase_bullet ($70A4).
Shot byte 7: its screen address, high byte.
Shot byte 8: its screen address, low byte, also the colour RAM's.
Shot byte 9: its colour RAM page.
Shot byte 10: the second character of a two-cell (blazer) shot, 0 for none.
Shot byte 11: the character saved under the second cell. This label's span covers record 1 ($048C-$0497) as well.
Shot record 2, the cat's ($0498-$04A3), byte 0: fire_cat_shot writes the column here directly ($8848).
The cat's shot record, byte 1: the row.
The cat's shot record, byte 2: the column step.
The cat's shot record, byte 3: the row step.
The cat's shot record, byte 4: the character, 0 while the cat's slot is free.
The cat's shot record, byte 5: its colour ($88A1).

The cat's shot record, byte 10: the blazer's second character ($887A, $8899). The span covers the rest of the table, records 3-5 of the spray ($04A4-$04C7), and $04C8-$04E1, which $6FBE uses as a spare record when called with X = $48 and $7540 clears along with the table.

The last 30 bytes of the block $0480-$04FF ($04E2-$04FF): $7540 clears them with the shot table (its loop stores 0 at $0480,X for X below $80) on each pass of the outer cycle; no traced code reads them.
Row addresses of the landscape screen $E000, low bytes, rows 0-24 (40 apart), loaded with the game; read by the shot, bullet and tube code ($6F72, $7C44, $9A87).
Row addresses of the screen $E000, high bytes ($E0-$E3), rows 0-24; the code ORs them with the page of the landscape screen in use ($6F61, $9A76).

The landscape map: 16 rows of 96 tile numbers, $0532-$0B31, one byte per 5 x 5-character tile of the table at $2642. Four bands of four rows; each band holds two landscapes, columns 0-44 and 45-89, and columns 92-95 hold halves of the Wiz-lab and finale pictures. Rows 0-3 are band 0: level 2 (left) and level 1 (right), the finale's top half at the far right. This label covers row 0 ($0532-$0591).
Landscape map row 1 ($0592-$05F1), band 0's second tile row: levels 2 and 1.

False symbol: the operand of BIT $05A9 at $49E0, where A9 05 is really LDA #$05 for code entering one byte later (the skip idiom). The bytes from here to $05E8 are map row 1, columns 23-86 (the row runs $0592-$05F1).
The last nine tiles of map row 1, columns 87-95 ($05E9-$05F1): the end of level 1's landscape (87-89), two empty columns (90-91) and the finale picture's part of the row (92-95).
Landscape map row 2 ($05F2-$0651), band 0's third tile row.
Landscape map row 3 ($0652-$06B1), band 0's ground row, where each landscape opens with tiles $11 $12 and closes with $21 $22.
Landscape map row 4 ($06B2-$0711), the first row of band 1: level 7 (left) and level 6 (right), with the finale picture's lower half at the far right.
Landscape map row 5 ($0712-$0771), band 1's second tile row.
Landscape map row 6 ($0772-$07D1), band 1's third tile row, columns 0-54 here (the rest follows the false symbol at $07A9).
False symbol: the operand of BIT $07A9 at $4AFE, where A9 07 is really LDA #$07 (the skip idiom). The bytes from here to $07D1 are the end of map row 6, columns 55-95.
Landscape map row 7, band 1's ground row: columns 0-45 are here ($07D2-$07FF) and the row goes on at $0800.

Landscape map, tile row 7 from column 46 to 95 ($0800-$0831; the row starts at $07D2, below this range). The map is 16 rows of 96 tile numbers from $0532, row r at $0532 + 96 r (row address tables $0460/$0470), in four bands of four rows; each band holds two landscapes side by side (columns 0-44 and 45-89), a two-column gap and at 92-95 half of a special picture. Row 7 is the ground row of band 1 (rows 4-7): columns 45-89 are level 6's ground, 92-95 the bottom of the right half of the picture drawn after all eight levels are complete ($AF20, $B128 = 10). $78CF reads it, drawing one column of four tiles at a time.

Landscape map, tile row 8 ($0832-$0891), the top row of band 2 (rows 8-11): columns 0-44 are level 3's landscape (start column $FF in $B2F0), 45-89 level 5's (start column $2C), 92-95 the top row of the Wiz-lab picture's left half (tiles $79 $7E $7F $80; $B128 = 9, drawn by $AB20). Mostly empty sky (tile 0). Besides $78CF, $7586 reads this row: it looks for two empty tiles from the level's start column + 6 + a random 0-31 and puts the Wizball's start there ($B1F1).
Landscape map, tile row 9 ($0892-$08F1), the second row of band 2: level 3 in columns 0-44, level 5 in 45-89, Wiz-lab tiles $78 $8A $8B $8C in 92-95.

Landscape map, tile row 10 ($08F2-$0951), the third row of band 2. Level 3's part holds its three Mount Rushmores (tiles $BC $BD $BE at columns 8-10, 20-22 and 35-37, base $BF in row 11). At $092B (column 57, level 5) is the stray tile number $F8: the tile table has only 192 entries, so $78CF draws 25 bytes of sound-effect data ($2642 + 25 x $F8 = $3E7A) as characters there. Remember's crack changes exactly this byte to $00, apparently its fix for the 'matrix in level 5' bug. Columns 92-95: Wiz-lab tiles $76 $89 $8F $90. Live: on level 5, with the view at tile column 54, the tile's bytes were on screen just right of the first well, including two glyphs $FF (the vector bytes) and a glyph $64.

Landscape map, tile row 11 ($0952-$09B1), the ground row of band 2: level 3's ground (with dips, tiles $21 $22 and $11 $12 at columns 12-16, 28-32 and 43-46), level 5's ground from column 45, Wiz-lab tiles $77 $83 $84 $94 in 92-95.

Landscape map, tile row 12 ($09B2-$0A11), the top row of band 3 (rows 12-15): columns 0-44 are level 4's landscape (start column $FF), 45-89 level 8's (start column $2C), 92-95 the top of the Wiz-lab picture's right half (tiles $95 $81 $82 $7D), reached after band 2's columns 92-95 when $75DF runs out and $76A2 moves the tile row down by four. $7586 also scans this row for the start of levels 4 and 8.

Bonus-stage attack script, $3902-$39DB. $9CB2 copies $FE bytes from here (this script and the first 36 bytes of the table after it) to $ED02-$EDFF, and $9CEA runs the copy, one command per pass of the bonus-stage loop ($65C3; loops are followed at once), index in $BB06. A command is two bytes: an alien type (bit 7: first wait until all six object slots at $0200 are empty, else until one is free; type $63 spawns nothing) and a delay, counted in $BB05 over the passes that find room; the type indexes tbl_bonus_alien_templates. $FF and $FE set $B1F8 to $FF or 0, which makes $6755 ramp $B1F6 up to 6 or down to 0 (apparently the stage's scrolling speed); $FD ends the stage ($B1CF = $36). A loop is three bytes: the address of its target in this block, low byte first (the high byte $39 is what $9CEA compares with $BB04 to recognise a loop), and a count that $9CEA decrements in the RAM copy. Run to the end it spawns 355 aliens of types 0-19 (never 10); $39DA-$39DB, after the $FD, are never reached.

Bonus-stage alien template table: 20 words, the template address of each alien type (0-19), indexed by type x 2 at $9D97 ($9D9C reads the high bytes). Entries 9 and 10 are both $3B03, and the script never asks for type 10. $9DA1 copies a template's first 23 bytes into a free 42-byte object slot at $0200 (slot n at $0200 + 42 n, six slots), clears the other 19, then applies its random fields. Template bytes: 0-1 X (screen X = 2 x byte 0), 2-3 Y, 4-5 X velocity, 6-7 Y velocity, 8 movement mode (0 Y velocity grows by byte 9 a frame, 1 shrinks, 2 steered by the direction bits of the path at 10-11, 3 accelerated by them), 12 frames per path step, 13 bounce/scenery behaviour ($A659), 14 fire mode (0 none, 1 aimed, 2 turning, 3 eight-way; $A541) and 15 its interval, 16 colour (low bits, $10 cycles) and flags (bit 7 police siren while alive, bit 6 hires, bit 5 always a pearl), 17 animation mode (0 still, 1 eased index, 2+ timed list; $A5B1) with 18 its frame/index/delay and 19-20 the frame list, 21 kind (0 ordinary, 1 releases a droplet, 6 extra life, $FF bounces off shots; $A7F2), 22 points / 10 (added through $710B by $A891); byte 23 counts 3-byte random fields (mask, add, offset into the slot).

High byte of the first entry of tbl_bonus_alien_templates: the code reads the table's high bytes through this address ($9D9C, LDA $39DD,Y), so the disassembler gave it a symbol; it owns the rest of the 20-word table, $39DD-$3A03.

Sound-effect records, 26 of 24 bytes from $3C5F; $4553 copies 25 bytes of the record for effect Y (address from $BACA) into the slot of its voice ($0400, $0420 or $0440 by byte 0, through $BA7A) and $B960 plays the slot each frame: 0 voice, 1 priority (a new effect replaces one whose first gate count is still running only if its value is not higher: 0 always wins), 2-3 gate-on frames, 4 waveform, 5 attack/decay, 6 start flag, 7-8 frequency, 9-10 its step, 11-12 frames up and down, 13-14 pulse width, 15-16 its step, 17-18 frames up and down, 19-22 sweep state, 23 sustain/release, 24 unused (the next record's first byte). Sound effect 0 (24-byte record, $3C5F-$3C76): voice 1, priority 14, gate on for 26 frames, sawtooth, attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0, frequency $9600 swept by $05FF, up for 1 frame then down for 256 frames in turn. Effect 0 is the shot: started by fire_wiz_shot ($84FC) and fire_cat_shot ($88AD). If effect 0 cannot take voice 1, $45A6 starts effect 16 (the same sound on voice 3) instead, and with no music ($B8F1 = 0) $456E alternates effects 0 and 16. Its sustain level is the firing volume (see $3C76).

Sustain/release byte (byte 23) of sound effect 0, the shot: $BAA6 writes the firing volume $BA81 (0-15) times 16 here, so the shot's sustain level follows it. $BA82 raises $BA81 when $B254 is 5 and lowers it when $B254 is 6, the codes scan_keys_play ($7429) gives the up-arrow and = keys (row 6, columns 6 and 5 of the keyboard matrix), one step a press. $F0 in the loaded image; $A0 in both play snapshots, $BA81 starting at 10.

Movement script $4115 (bytes 10-11 of the $39DC records at $3A34, $3A52, $3B57, $3B6F and $3B87): $05, $FF. Script bytes are direction bits held for the record's byte-12 ticks each, and $FF restarts the script ($A3E5-$A40B). The bits ($A41D-$A48E): bit 0 adds step 1 (slot bytes 4-5) to coordinate 1 (bytes 0-1), bit 1 subtracts it, bit 2 adds step 2 (bytes 6-7) to coordinate 2 (bytes 2-3), bit 3 subtracts it. Start sound effect Y (0-25), called from 31 places in the game (list in notes-2.md). The effect's 24-byte record comes through the word table at $BACA (records 24 bytes apart from $3C5F); its byte 0 is the voice (1-3), turned by $BA7B into the offset of that voice's effect slot ($0400, $0420, $0440). The effect starts if the slot is idle (slot byte 2, the time left, is 0) or if its priority (record byte 1) is the same as or lower in number than the sound playing there (slot byte 1): low numbers win. Starting copies 25 bytes of the record into the slot (one more than a record, so slot byte $18 gets the next record's voice byte). The table holds 26 records (0-25) at $3C5F-$3ECE. Effect $18 first stores six random bytes (JSR $7533) into its own record at $3EA6-$3EAB, the frequency and sweep fields. Effect 0 flips bit 4 of $BB03 on every call and, with no music playing ($B8F1 = 0), plays record $10 (the same sound on voice 3) every other time; when its voice is taken by a more important sound it retries as effect $10. The effect number is kept in $BB02; X is saved in $62 and restored, except after that retry, which returns X = 0. The effects are played by the band routine $B960 on the voices the music leaves free.

Once a frame from the play loop ($6411): when voice 3 of the music has finished its track ($5B = 0, read through $5522), give every voice back to the sound effects: music mode $B8F1 = 0, filter-type nibble $B94D = 0 and $D417 = 0 (no voice filtered).

Music fade direction, used and cleared by step_music_fade ($45D0): 0 = none, $01 = fade in (volume up to 15), $FF = fade out (down to 0). Set by the game: $FF at $639D, $6471 and $6514; 1 at $64F8, $6550 and $6906.

Master volume, 0-15 ($0F in the loaded image). Stepped by step_music_fade and ORed with $B94D into $D418 by the band routine $B90C ($B910-$B916, and again at $B943-$B949 after the music has played). The game reads it at $64F1 to wait for a fade-out to finish.

Once a frame, from the band routine $B90C: move the master volume $45CF one step in the direction in $45CE, and clear $45CE when the volume reaches 15 (fading in) or 0 (fading out). A full fade takes 15 frames.

Start tune Y, with Y = 7 x tune + 5 ($05, $0C, $13, $1A, $21, $28, $2F, $36, $3D for tunes 0-8; the tunes are listed at $5525). Sets the filter-type nibble $B94D for $D418 to $70 (low-, band- and high-pass together) for tune $1A, the title tune, and to $10 (low-pass) for the others, then continues at $47F2. Callers: $6507 (tune 2), $6573 (tune 1 or 4), $6916 (tune 5), $6A91 (tune 7), $6BC0 (tune 6), $893D and $A17D (tune 0), $8F6A (tune 3), $AB75 (tune 8). The callers also set the music mode $B8F1 (0 = no music, the effects use all three voices; 1 = music on voice 3 only, effects on voices 1 and 2; 2 = music on all three voices, no effects) and the speed $B8F2 (the music is played once, twice or four times a frame for 0, 1 and 2, from the band routines $B90C, $B8FC, $B903 and $B8F3).
One unused byte ($00) between start_tune and the voice 1 command table at $4600; no instruction refers to it.

An odd command byte would jump through a word made of two entries' halves; the tunes use none.

Voice 2 command table, last word, for $E8: $4AD5, load a 14-byte pitch block.

Voice 3 command handlers, 22 words for $C0-$EA, selected by the JMP ($4654) at $4FFB (operand low byte = command + $94, written at $4FF6): $C0 $4C6E, $C2 $4B6C, $C4 $4C21, $C6 $4B66, $CA $4C4B, $CC $4BEE, $CE $4C54, $D0 $4BD4, $D2 $4CA3, $D4 $4C86, $D6 $4B8C, $D8 $4C9C, $DA $4B9E, $DC $4BAE, $DE $4C42, $E0 $4BBE, $E2 $4C2E, $E8 $4C0B, and $EA set tempo $4C8F, which only voice 3 has. $C8 (transpose and jump), $E4 and $E6 hold $0926, not a handler; no tune uses them on voice 3.
Voice 3 command table, word for $C8 (transpose and jump on voices 1 and 2): $0926, not a handler, so voice 3 cannot use $C8.

Voice 3 command table, words for $CA to $E2: $4C4B set instrument byte, $4BEE loop start, $4C54 loop end, $4BD4 load instrument, $4CA3 load envelope, $4C86 set live byte, $4B8C machine code, $4C9C transpose, $4B9E set instrument word, $4BAE set live word, $4C42 filter voice 3, $4BBE filter program, $4C2E filter off.
Voice 3 command table, words for $E4 and $E6 (the pitch-mode commands of voice 1): $0926 twice, not handlers; voice 3 changes its pitch mode with $CA or an instrument load instead.
Voice 3 command table, last two words: $E8 $4C0B (load a pitch block) and $EA $4C8F (set the tempo), the command only voice 3 has.

Voice 2 instrument template, 29 bytes $4680-$469C, the same layout as voice 1's $87-$A3 and voice 3's $A4-$C0 (all $EE in the loaded image). Written by the voice 2 commands $D0 ($4AAF), $E8 ($4AE3, bytes 0-13), $D2 ($4B5D, bytes 24-28), $CA ($4B0C) and $DA ($4A7F/$4A85); read by the voice 2 note start ($4ED8-$4FB5), which sends bytes 22-26 to the SID and copies the pulse fields (when byte 17 is not 0), the pitch fields (when byte 13 is not 0) and the gate and release times to the live block $46C0. Byte 0: pitch step 1, low byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 1 ($4680 + 1): pitch step 1, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 2 ($4680 + 2): pitch step 2, low byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 3 ($4680 + 3): pitch step 2, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 4 ($4680 + 4): pitch step 3, low byte (arpeggio mode: the tick counter's start).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 5 ($4680 + 5): pitch step 3, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 6 ($4680 + 6): pitch step 4, low byte (arpeggio mode: ticks per arpeggio note).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 7 ($4680 + 7): pitch step 4, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 8 ($4680 + 8): ticks of pitch step 1 (arpeggio mode: the table address, low byte).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 9 ($4680 + 9): ticks of pitch step 2 (arpeggio mode: the table address, high byte).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 10 ($4680 + 10): ticks of pitch step 3 (arpeggio mode: the base note, replaced by note + transpose at every note start).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 11 ($4680 + 11): ticks of pitch step 4 (arpeggio mode: the first table index; the table is read from it down to 0, then again).
Voice 2 instrument template byte 12 ($4680 + 12): ticks before the pitch steps begin (arpeggio mode: the current table index).

Voice 2 instrument template byte 13 ($4680 + 13): pitch-effect mode: 0 off; bit 3 arpeggio; otherwise four pitch steps, bit 1 also adding step 4 during the delay, and after the fourth step bit 7 restarting from the note's frequency, bit 0 repeating from where it is, neither holding.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 14 ($4680 + 14): pulse sweep, ticks of step 1.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 15 ($4680 + 15): pulse sweep, ticks of step 2.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 16 ($4680 + 16): pulse sweep, ticks before it starts.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 17 ($4680 + 17): pulse sweep mode: 0 off; after both steps bit 7 restarts from the start width, bit 0 repeats from the current width, neither holds.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 18 ($4680 + 18): pulse step 1, low byte.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 19 ($4680 + 19): pulse step 1, high byte.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 20 ($4680 + 20): pulse step 2, low byte.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 21 ($4680 + 21): pulse step 2, high byte.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 22 ($4680 + 22): pulse width at the note start, low byte.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 23 ($4680 + 23): pulse width at the note start, high byte.

Voice 2 instrument template byte 24 ($4680 + 24): control register value: waveform and gate bit 0; bit 3 (the test bit, masked off before the chip) picks the gate-off rule: set = release when fewer than byte 27 ticks of the note are left, clear = release byte 27 ticks after the start.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 25 ($4680 + 25): attack/decay register value.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 26 ($4680 + 26): sustain/release register value.
Voice 2 instrument template byte 27 ($4680 + 27): gate time in ticks ($FF = keep the gate on).

Voice 2 instrument template byte 28 ($4680 + 28): release time: ticks from the gate-off until the voice's seven SID registers are cleared ($FF = never; 0 = the voice is left alone, with no gate-off and no effects).

Bytes 0-12 are the live pitch block; byte 0: pitch step 1, low byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 1 ($469D + 1): pitch step 1, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 2 ($469D + 2): pitch step 2, low byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 3 ($469D + 3): pitch step 2, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 4 ($469D + 4): pitch step 3, low byte (arpeggio mode: the tick counter's start).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 5 ($469D + 5): pitch step 3, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 6 ($469D + 6): pitch step 4, low byte (arpeggio mode: ticks per arpeggio note).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 7 ($469D + 7): pitch step 4, high byte (arpeggio mode: unused).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 8 ($469D + 8): ticks of pitch step 1 (arpeggio mode: the table address, low byte).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 9 ($469D + 9): ticks of pitch step 2 (arpeggio mode: the table address, high byte).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 10 ($469D + 10): ticks of pitch step 3 (arpeggio mode: the base note, replaced by note + transpose at every note start).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 11 ($469D + 11): ticks of pitch step 4 (arpeggio mode: the first table index; the table is read from it down to 0, then again).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 12 ($469D + 12): ticks before the pitch steps begin (arpeggio mode: the current table index).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 13 ($469D + 13): pitch-effect mode, from template byte 13 (0 = no pitch update).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 14 ($469D + 14): pulse step 1 tick count, reloaded into byte 33 when the sweep repeats.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 15 ($469D + 15): pulse step 2 tick count, reloaded into byte 34 when the sweep repeats.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 16 ($469D + 16): pulse delay, counted down each tick.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 17 ($469D + 17): pulse sweep mode, from template byte 17 (0 = no sweep).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 18 ($469D + 18): pulse step 1, low byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 19 ($469D + 19): pulse step 1, high byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 20 ($469D + 20): pulse step 2, low byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 21 ($469D + 21): pulse step 2, high byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 22 ($469D + 22): pulse width at the note start, low byte (where a restarting sweep begins again).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 23 ($469D + 23): pulse width at the note start, high byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 24 ($469D + 24): the note's frequency, low byte (base of the pitch steps and of their restarts).
Voice 1 live sound state byte 25 ($469D + 25): the note's frequency, high byte.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 26 ($469D + 26): control register value as written at the note start; the gate-off clears bits 0 and 3.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 27 ($469D + 27): gate time, counted down to the gate-off (or compared with the note time left when control bit 3 is set); $FF holds.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 28 ($469D + 28): release time, counted down after the gate-off; $FF holds; 0 = voice idle, the per-tick update returns at once.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 29 ($469D + 29): ticks left in pitch step 1.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 30 ($469D + 30): ticks left in pitch step 2.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 31 ($469D + 31): ticks left in pitch step 3.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 32 ($469D + 32): ticks left in pitch step 4.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 33 ($469D + 33): ticks left in pulse step 1.
Voice 1 live sound state byte 34 ($469D + 34): ticks left in pulse step 2.

Voice 2 live sound state byte 12 ($46C0 + 12): ticks before the pitch steps begin (arpeggio mode: the current table index).
Voice 2 live sound state byte 13 ($46C0 + 13): pitch-effect mode, from template byte 13 (0 = no pitch update).
Voice 2 live sound state byte 14 ($46C0 + 14): pulse step 1 tick count, reloaded into byte 33 when the sweep repeats.
Voice 2 live sound state byte 15 ($46C0 + 15): pulse step 2 tick count, reloaded into byte 34 when the sweep repeats.
Voice 2 live sound state byte 16 ($46C0 + 16): pulse delay, counted down each tick.
Voice 2 live sound state byte 17 ($46C0 + 17): pulse sweep mode, from template byte 17 (0 = no sweep).
Voice 2 live sound state byte 18 ($46C0 + 18): pulse step 1, low byte.
Voice 2 live sound state byte 19 ($46C0 + 19): pulse step 1, high byte.

Duration table: 32 note lengths in ticks, entry n (at $46E2 + n) = n x tempo, 8-bit, for duration codes 1-32. Rebuilt by $4834 when a tune starts and when voice 3 plays command $EA; read with the byte after every note or rest below $60 ($4E74, $4FC3, $50E2). Code 0 would read $46E2 (voice 2's pulse counter) and codes above 32 run past the table; the tunes use 1-32, and none of their codes overflows 255 ticks at its tempo.

Voice 2 loop counters, 5 bytes $4703-$4707, one per level of the voice's stack (the index in $0E runs from 4 down to 0 as it fills): command $CC stores the repeat count at $4703 + level ($4ACB). This byte is level 0, the fifth level, which no tune reaches.
Voice 2 loop counters of stack levels 1-4 ($4704-$4707), as command $CE sees them ($4B14: DEC $4704,X with X = the stack index, one below the level pushed last).
Voice 3 return addresses, low bytes, 5 levels $4708-$470C (index $0F from 4 down to 0): calls and loop starts store the address to come back to at $4708 + level ($4B73, $4BF5). This byte is level 0.
Voice 3 return address low bytes of levels 1-4 ($4709-$470C), read back by the loop end ($4C5B) and the return ($4C76).
Voice 3 return addresses, high bytes, level 0 ($470D-$4711 hold levels 0-4; stored at $4B7A and $4BFC).
Voice 3 return address high bytes of levels 1-4 ($470E-$4711), read back at $4C5E and $4C79.

Voice 3 loop counters, level 0 ($4712-$4716 hold levels 0-4; command $CC stores at $4C01). The tunes nest at most three levels on voice 3 (levels 4-2), so $4712-$4713 keep the $EE of the loaded image.
Voice 3 loop counters of levels 1-4 ($4713-$4716), counted down by command $CE ($4C56: DEC $4713,X).

Three offsets from $0094, one per voice ($00, $F9, $1D): load_tune stores 0 at $0094 + offset and $0098 + offset ($4818/$481B) to switch off the pitch effect and the pulse sweep of each voice's instrument when a tune starts. That is right for voice 1 ($94, $98) and voice 3 ($B1, $B5), but for voice 2 the sums are $018D and $0191, in the stack page, instead of $468D and $4691, so voice 2 keeps the previous tune's modes until its instrument is loaded.

Note frequencies, low bytes: 91 entries for notes 0-90 (C-0 to F-7, and entry 90, which is 0); the high bytes follow at $4775. Tuned for PAL: frequency = value x 985,248 / 16,777,216 Hz lands 6 cents above equal temperament at A = 440 for every note (C-0 $0117 = 16.4 Hz, A-4 $1D60 = 441.6 Hz, F-7 $BA85 = 2,804 Hz); an NTSC machine (clock 1,022,727 Hz) plays every note 0.65 of a semitone higher, 71 cents above A = 440. Indexed by note + transpose at the note starts ($4D97, $4EC9, $5025) and by the arpeggios ($51ED, $535B, $54A8). The tunes' notes reach 7 to 89.

Note frequencies, high bytes, 91 entries matching $471A: $01 for C-0 up to $BA for F-7, and $00 for entry 90 ($47CF), so note 90 would be frequency 0, silence. A note above 90 would read the bytes after the table, the code at $47D0.

Silence the SID and stop the music: writes $08 (the test bit, which stops a voice's oscillator when it lands in a control register) and then $00 to every register from $D417 down to $D400 (all three voices and the filter; $D418 is left alone), then marks the voices idle ($59, $5A, $5B = 0 and the release counters $46B9, $46DC, $DD = 0), stops the filter sweep ($4E = 0) and sets the filter voice $57 to $FF (none). Called before tunes start ($6553, $6909, $6A87, $6BBB, $8F65, $AB5B) and at $696F (end of the get-ready screen) and $ADF2.

Second half of start_tune: Y points at the tempo byte of a record in the tune table (read as $5526,Y). The tempo goes into the operand at $4838; then for voice 3, 2 and 1 in turn: the track address into $08/$09, $06/$07 or $04/$05 (from $5525,Y and $5526,Y, stepping Y back two bytes a voice), transpose 0 ($12, $11, $10), pitch mode and pulse mode 0 (through the offsets at $4717, which miss voice 2), an empty stack (index 4 in $0F, $0E, $0D), a note time of 1 so that the first event is read at the next tick ($0C, $0B, $0A) and the active flag 1 ($5B, $5A, $59). Falls into $4834 with X = 0.

Fill the duration table $46E3-$4702 with 1 to 32 times the tempo held in the operand at $4838 (8-bit sums, so a long code at a high tempo would wrap). Entered from load_tune with X = 0 and from the voice 3 tempo command at $4C94.
the immediate is the tempo, written at $47F5 and $4C8F

The tempo: operand of the ADC # at $4837, written by load_tune ($47F5, from the tune record) and by the voice 3 command $EA ($4C8F): the number of ticks in duration code 1. $DD in the loaded image, 5 in the title and play snapshots.
Voice 1 pulse sweep restart (mode bit 7): the width goes back to the note's start width $46B3/$46B4, then falls into set_v1_pulse.

Voice 1: make X (low) and Y (high) the current pulse width $29/$2A and reload the two pulse step counters $46BE/$46BF from $46AB/$46AC. Used at the note start ($4DC4) and by the sweep when it repeats ($5197) or restarts ($5191 via $4842).
Voice 2 pulse sweep restart: the width goes back to the start width $46D6/$46D7, then falls into set_v2_pulse.

Voice 2: X/Y become the current pulse width $2B/$2C and the pulse step counters $46E1/$46E2 are reloaded from $46CE/$46CF. Used at the note start ($4EFB) and by the sweep ($5305, and $52FF via $4859).
Voice 3 pulse sweep restart: the width goes back to the start width $D7/$D8, then falls into set_v3_pulse.
Voice 3: X/Y become the current pulse width $2D/$2E and the pulse step counters $E2/$E3 are reloaded from $CF/$D0. Used at the note start ($504F) and by the sweep ($545F, and $5459 via $4870).
Filter sweep restart: X/Y and the current cutoff $51/$52 take the program's start cutoff $4F/$50, then falls into reload_filter_counts.

Filter sweep: reload the four step counters $53-$56 from $49-$4C (the cutoff carries on from where it is). Used when the sweep repeats ($4D35) and through $4881 when it restarts ($4D2F) or a program starts ($4D48).
Voice 1 pitch steps restart: the current frequency $2F/$30 goes back to the note's frequency $46B5/$46B6, then falls into reload_v1_pitch_counts.
Voice 1: reload the four pitch step counters $46BA-$46BD from live bytes 8-11 ($46A5-$46A8). Used at the note start ($4E5C via $489A) and when the steps repeat ($5263) or restart ($525D via $489A).
Voice 2 pitch steps restart: current frequency $15/$16 = the note's frequency $46D8/$46D9, then falls into reload_v2_pitch_counts.
Voice 2: reload the pitch step counters $46DD-$46E0 from live bytes 8-11 ($46C8-$46CB). Used at the note start ($4FA9 via $48BD) and by the steps ($53D1, $53CB).
Voice 3 pitch steps restart: current frequency $17/$18 = the note's frequency $D9/$DA, then falls into reload_v3_pitch_counts.
Voice 3: reload the pitch step counters $DE-$E1 from live bytes 8-11 ($C9-$CC). Used at the note start ($50CC via $48E0) and by the steps ($550D, $5507).
Voice 1 command $C6 t lo hi: set the transpose $10 to t, then call like $C2 with a return address 4 bytes on (the BIT $03A9 at $48FE skips $C2's LDA #$03).
BIT only skips the next two bytes; entered at $48FF (v1_cmd_call, command $C2) they are LDA #$03

Voice 1 command $C2 lo hi: call the pattern at hi:lo. Pushes the address 3 bytes on (low at $E4 + level, high at $E9 + level; the level in $0D runs from 4 down to 0) and reads on at hi:lo. This address is the operand of the BIT at $48FE; entered here the bytes read LDA #$03.

Voice 1 command $D6 lo hi: call the machine code at hi:lo (JMP ($0013)) with $4D5A pushed as the return address, so that its RTS lands on $4D5B: the voice steps 3 bytes on and reads its next event. The title tune uses it ($604D calls $5F2E).
Voice 1 command $DA i lo hi: store the word lo hi at template bytes i and i+1 ($87 + i), for example an arpeggio table (i = 8) or pitch step 1 (i = 0).
Voice 1 command $DC i lo hi: store the word at live bytes i and i+1 ($469D + i), which changes the note already sounding (i = 6 pitch step 4, i = $1B gate and release times).

Voice 1 command $E0 lo hi: copy the 16-byte filter program at hi:lo into $31-$40 (four cutoff steps, their tick counts, delay, mode and start cutoff; see $4D3B) through the operand of the LDA at $495C. It is started by the filter voice's next note, or at once by the tune's own code at $5AFF.
operand rewritten by $4951/$4957: the filter program's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $495C: the address of the filter program that voice 1's command $E0 copies, written at $4951.
High byte of the LDA operand at $495C, written at $4957 (voice 1 command $E0).
Voice 1 command $D0 n lo hi: copy n + 1 bytes from hi:lo into the voice 1 instrument template from $87 (n = $1C loads a whole 29-byte instrument), through the operand of the LDA at $4974.
operand rewritten by $496B/$4971: the instrument's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4974: the instrument address of voice 1's command $D0, written at $496B.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4974, written at $4971 (voice 1 command $D0).

Voice 1 command $CC n: start of a repeated section. Pushes the address after the command and the count n ($EE + level) on the voice's stack; the matching $CE plays the section n times (n = 0 would give 256).

Voice 1 command $E8 lo hi: copy 14 bytes from hi:lo into template bytes 0-13 ($87-$94): a pitch block (four steps, their tick counts, delay and mode, or an arpeggio set-up), through the operand of the LDA at $49A6.
operand rewritten by $499B/$49A1: the pitch block's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $49A6: the pitch block address of voice 1's command $E8, written at $499B. One of the operands that differ between cracks' title screens (orientation.md).
High byte of the LDA operand at $49A6, written at $49A1 (voice 1 command $E8).
Voice 1 command $C8 t lo hi: set the transpose $10 to t and continue at hi:lo (through $49B4).
Voice 1 command $C4 lo hi: continue reading at hi:lo; the tracks that repeat end with one.

Voice 1 command $E2: filter off. Stops the filter sweep ($4E = 0), $D417 = $F0 (resonance 15, no voice through the filter), filter voice $57 = 3 (none) and $D418 = $1F (low-pass, volume 15; the band routine rewrites $D418 from $45CF and $B94D later in the frame).
BIT only skips the next two bytes; v1_cmd_filter_on enters at $49C9, where they are LDY #$F1

Voice 1 command $DE: filter voice 1. $D417 = $F1 (resonance 15, voice 1 filtered), $57 = 0 (voice 1's notes restart the filter program), $D418 = $1F. It jumps into $49C1's code at $49C9, inside the BIT at $49C8, where the bytes read LDY #$F1.
Voice 1 command $E6: pitch mode 7 (template byte 13, $94): repeating steps, with step 4 added during the delay. The BIT $05A9 at $49E0 skips $E4's LDA #$05.
BIT only skips the next two bytes; entered at $49E1 (v1_cmd_pitch_mode5, command $E4) they are LDA #$05
Voice 1 command $E4: pitch mode 5, repeating steps (a vibrato). This address is inside the BIT at $49E0; entered here the bytes read LDA #$05.
Voice 1 command $CA i v: set template byte i ($87 + i) to v (for example i = $18 control, $1A sustain/release, $1B gate time, $0D pitch mode).

Voice 1 command $CE: end of a repeated section. Counts down the count of the innermost level ($EF + index); while it is not 0 the voice goes back to the address stored by $CC, otherwise the level is popped and the voice reads on.

Voice 1 command $C0: return from a pattern to the address pushed by $C2 or $C6; with the stack empty (index 4) the voice's track ends instead: $59 goes from 1 to 0 and the tick routine stops reading. First word of the table at $4600.
Voice 1 command $D4 i v: set live byte i ($469D + i) to v; with i = $1B, the gate time, it releases the sounding note after v ticks.
Voice 1 command $D8 t: set the transpose $10, added to every note number, to t.
Voice 1 command $D2 lo hi: copy the 5-byte envelope block at hi:lo into template bytes 24-28 ($9F-$A3): control, attack/decay, sustain/release, gate time, release time.
Voice 2 command $C6 t lo hi: set the transpose $11 to t and call hi:lo with a return 4 bytes on (the BIT $03A9 at $4A4A skips $C2's LDA #$03).
BIT only skips the next two bytes; entered at $4A4B (v2_cmd_call, command $C2) they are LDA #$03

Voice 2 command $C2 lo hi: call the pattern at hi:lo, pushing the address 3 bytes on at $F3 + level (low) and $F8 + level (high), the level in $0E from 4 down to 0. Operand byte of the BIT at $4A4A; entered here it reads LDA #$03.
Voice 2 command $D6 lo hi: call the machine code at hi:lo with $4E92 pushed, so it returns to $4E93 (step 3 bytes, read the next event). No tune uses it on voice 2.
Voice 2 command $DA i lo hi: store the word at template bytes i and i+1 ($4680 + i); tune 6 changes its arpeggio table this way ($5727-$575D).
Voice 2 command $DC i lo hi: store the word at live bytes i and i+1 ($46C0 + i), changing the sounding note.
Voice 2 command $D0 n lo hi: copy n + 1 bytes from hi:lo into the template from $4680, through the operand of the LDA at $4AAC.
operand rewritten by $4AA3/$4AA9: the instrument's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4AAC: the instrument address of voice 2's command $D0, written at $4AA3.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4AAC, written at $4AA9 (voice 2 command $D0).
Voice 2 command $CC n: start of a repeated section; the count goes to $4703 + level, the address to $F3/$F8 + level.
Voice 2 command $E8 lo hi: copy 14 bytes from hi:lo into template bytes 0-13 ($4680-$468D), through the operand of the LDA at $4AE0.
operand rewritten by $4AD5/$4ADB: the pitch block's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4AE0: the pitch block address of voice 2's command $E8, written at $4AD5.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4AE0, written at $4ADB (voice 2 command $E8).
Voice 2 command $C8 t lo hi: set the transpose $11 and continue at hi:lo; tune 6's voice 2 loops with it ($5777).
Voice 2 command $C4 lo hi: continue reading at hi:lo.
Voice 2 command $E4: pitch mode 5 into template byte 13 ($468D). The code has a second entry at $4AFF (inside the BIT at $4AFE) that would store mode 7, but the table at $462A has no word for it.
BIT only skips the next two bytes; entered at $4AFF they would be LDA #$07 (mode 7), but no table word points there
Voice 2 command $CA i v: set template byte i ($4680 + i) to v.
Voice 2 command $CE: count down the innermost loop count ($4704 + index) and go back to the section start while it is not 0, else pop and read on.
Voice 2 command $C0: return from a pattern, or with the stack empty end the track ($5A goes to 0). First word of the table at $462A.
Voice 2 command $D8 t: set the transpose $11 to t.
Voice 2 command $D4 i v: set live byte i ($46C0 + i) to v.
Voice 2 command $D2 lo hi: copy 5 bytes from hi:lo into template bytes 24-28 ($4698-$469C).
Voice 3 command $C6 t lo hi: set the transpose $12 to t and call hi:lo with a return 4 bytes on (the BIT $03A9 at $4B6B skips $C2's LDA #$03).
BIT only skips the next two bytes; entered at $4B6C (v3_cmd_call, command $C2) they are LDA #$03

Voice 3 command $C2 lo hi: call the pattern at hi:lo; the return address goes to $4708 + level (low) and $470D + level (high), the level in $0F from 4 down to 0. Operand byte of the BIT at $4B6B; entered here it reads LDA #$03.
Voice 3 command $D6 lo hi: call the machine code at hi:lo with $4FE1 pushed, so it returns to $4FE2. Tunes 1 and 8 use it to call $5AFF.
Voice 3 command $DA i lo hi: store the word at template bytes i and i+1 ($A4 + i).
Voice 3 command $DC i lo hi: store the word at live bytes i and i+1 ($C1 + i); tune 4 switches arpeggio tables this way ($5EAC-$5EBE).
Voice 3 command $E0 lo hi: copy a 16-byte filter program into $31-$40, through the operand of the LDA at $4BC9.
operand rewritten by $4BBE/$4BC4: the filter program's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4BC9: the filter program address of voice 3's command $E0, written at $4BBE.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4BC9, written at $4BC4 (voice 3 command $E0).
Voice 3 command $D0 n lo hi: copy n + 1 bytes from hi:lo into the voice 3 template from $A4, through the operand of the LDA at $4BE1.
operand rewritten by $4BD8/$4BDE: the instrument's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4BE1: the instrument address of voice 3's command $D0, written at $4BD8.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4BE1, written at $4BDE (voice 3 command $D0).
Voice 3 command $CC n: start of a repeated section; the count goes to $4712 + level, the address to $4708/$470D + level.
Voice 3 command $E8 lo hi: copy 14 bytes from hi:lo into template bytes 0-13 ($A4-$B1), through the operand of the LDA at $4C16.
operand rewritten by $4C0B/$4C11: the pitch block's address, not $DDDD
Low byte of the LDA $DDDD,X operand at $4C16: the pitch block address of voice 3's command $E8, written at $4C0B.
High byte of the LDA operand at $4C16, written at $4C11 (voice 3 command $E8).
Voice 3 command $C4 lo hi: continue reading at hi:lo. Voice 3 has no command $C8, so it cannot set the transpose while jumping.
Voice 3 command $E2: filter off: $4E = 0, $D417 = $F0 and $57 = 3; unlike voice 1's $E2 it leaves $D418 alone.
BIT only skips the next two bytes; v3_cmd_filter_on enters at $4C36, where they are LDY #$F4

Voice 3 command $DE: filter voice 3: $D418 = $1F, then into $4C2E's code at $4C36 (inside the BIT at $4C35, where the bytes read LDY #$F4): $D417 = $F4 (resonance 15, voice 3 filtered) and $57 = 2 (voice 3's notes restart the filter program).
Voice 3 command $CA i v: set template byte i ($A4 + i) to v.
Voice 3 command $CE: count down the innermost loop count ($4713 + index) and go back to the section start ($4709/$470E + index) while it is not 0, else pop.
Voice 3 command $C0: return from a pattern, or with the stack empty end the track ($5B goes to 0, which check_music_end at $45BD watches). First word of the table at $4654.
Voice 3 command $D4 i v: set live byte i ($C1 + i) to v.
Voice 3 command $EA n: change the tempo to n (operand $4838) and rebuild the duration table ($4834); tune 4 does it four times. Reached only through the twenty-second word of the table at $4654.
Voice 3 command $D8 t: set the transpose $12 to t.
Voice 3 command $D2 lo hi: copy 5 bytes from hi:lo into template bytes 24-28 ($BC-$C0).

Once per music tick (from the band routine at $B940): run the filter program's cutoff sweep; nothing while its mode $4E is 0. The delay $4D is counted down first (with mode bit 1, step 4 is added on each tick of it); then steps 1-4 ($41/$42 ... $47/$48) are added to the cutoff for $53-$56 ticks each; after the fourth, mode bit 7 restarts from the start cutoff ($4881), bit 0 repeats from the current cutoff ($4889), otherwise the cutoff holds. The cutoff is kept in $51/$52 and written by $4D10.

Write the cutoff in X (low) and Y (high) to the chip: $D415 = X AND 7 and $D416 = bits 3-10 of the value (shifted through $58), an 11-bit cutoff. Entered from the sweep (which stores $51/$52 first) and from start_filter_program.

Start the filter program: copy $31-$40 (put there by command $E0) to the working set $41-$50, set the cutoff to the start value and reload the counters ($4881), and write it to the chip ($4D10). Called at each note start of the filter voice (voice 1 when $57 = 0, $4D8F; voice 3 when $57 = 2, $501D) and by the tune code at $5AFF.

Voice 1 of the music, once per tick (from $B931, when the music has all three voices): while the voice is active ($59) count down its note time $0A, and when it runs out read the next events from its track at ($04) ($4D64).

Voice 1: step the track pointer $04/$05 on by 3 ($4D5B) or by A ($4D5D; $4D57 carries into the high byte), then read the event at $4D64. A byte of $C0 or more is a command: (byte + $40) goes into the operand at $4D75 and JMP ($4600) runs its handler with the first parameter in A and Y = 1; the handlers come back to these entries. A smaller byte is a note ($4D7A).
low byte of the operand set at $4D6F to command + $40: the word for this command in music_cmds_voice1

Low byte of the JMP ($4600) operand at $4D74, rewritten at $4D6F with (command + $40) to pick the handler word in the voice 1 table; $00 in the loaded image. The JMP $4E69 after it ($4D77) is the path of a rest.

Voice 1 note event: a note byte and a duration byte. Bytes $60-$BF are notes $00-$5F whose duration byte is a tick count instead of a code; $5F (and $BF) is a rest. Note + transpose $10 indexes the frequency tables $471A/$4775. If voice 1 drives the filter ($57 = 0) the filter program restarts ($4D3B). From the template $87-$A3 the frequency, pulse width, attack/decay, sustain/release and control go to $D400-$D406 (control with bit 3 masked; voice 1 does not reset the gate first, so a note following one whose gate is still on does not restart the envelope); the pulse sweep (if $98 is not 0) and the pitch effect (if $94 is not 0; for an arpeggio with note + transpose as its base) are copied to the live block, and the gate and release times to $46B8/$46B9. For notes $60-$BE in arpeggio mode the base note comes out 2 higher than the note played ($4E53: SBC #$5F, then ADC with the carry set); no tune uses that combination.

Voice 1: set the note time $0A from the byte after the note: for a note byte below $60 it is a duration code looked up in $46E3 (code x tempo), for $60-$BF the tick count itself; then step the pointer 2 bytes on.
Voice 2 of the music, once per tick (from $B937): while $5A is set count down the note time $0B, and when it runs out read the next events at ($06) ($4E9C).

Voice 2: step the track pointer $06/$07 on by 3 ($4E93) or by A ($4E95), then read the event at $4E9C: a command byte runs its handler through JMP ($462A) with the operand $4EAD rewritten, a smaller byte is a note ($4EB2).
low byte of the operand set at $4EA7 to command + $6A: the word for this command in music_cmds_voice2
Low byte of the JMP ($462A) operand at $4EAC, rewritten at $4EA7 with (command + $6A); $2A in the loaded image. A rest takes the JMP $4FB8 at $4EAF.

Voice 2 note event (as voice 1's at $4D7A, with the transpose $11 and the template $4680): sets the test bit ($D40B = $08) first, which silences the oscillator and makes every note restart the envelope, then frequency, pulse width, attack/decay, sustain/release and control to $D407-$D40D, and copies the pulse and pitch settings to the live block $46C0. Voice 2 never touches the filter.
Voice 2: set the note time $0B from the duration byte (a code for notes below $60, ticks for $60-$BF) and step the pointer 2 bytes on.
Voice 3 of the music, once per tick (from $B93D, whenever the music has voice 3): while $5B is set count down the note time $0C, and when it runs out read the next events at ($08) ($4FEB).

Voice 3: step the track pointer $08/$09 on by 3 ($4FE2) or by A ($4FE4), then read the event at $4FEB: a command byte runs its handler through JMP ($4654) with the operand $4FFC rewritten, a smaller byte is a note ($5001).
low byte of the operand set at $4FF6 to command + $94: the word for this command in music_cmds_voice3
Low byte of the JMP ($4654) operand at $4FFB, rewritten at $4FF6 with (command + $94); $54 in the loaded image. A rest takes the JMP $50D7 at $4FFE.

Voice 3 note event (transpose $12, template $A4-$C0): test bit first ($D412 = $08), the filter program restarts if voice 3 drives the filter ($57 = 2), then frequency, pulse width, envelope and control to $D40E-$D414 and the pulse and pitch settings to the live block $C1-$E3.
Voice 3: set the note time $0C from the duration byte and step the pointer 2 bytes on.

Voice 1 sound shaping, once per tick (from $B92E): nothing while the release counter $46B9 is 0. The gate is released (bits 0 and 3 cleared in $46B7 and $D404) when the gate time $46B8 has been counted down or, with control bit 3 set, as soon as fewer than $46B8 ticks of the note are left ($0A); the release time $46B9 is then counted down and at 0 the registers $D400-$D406 are cleared (and the filter sweep stopped if voice 1 drives it). $FF in either time holds. Then the pulse sweep ($5149) and the pitch effect ($51A7).

Voice 1 pulse sweep (mode $46AE not 0): after the delay $46AD, add pulse step 1 ($46AF/$46B0) for $46BE ticks, then step 2 ($46B1/$46B2) for $46BF ticks; then mode bit 7 restarts from the start width ($4842), bit 0 repeats from the current width ($4848), otherwise it holds. The width $29/$2A goes to $D402/$D403.

Voice 1 pitch effect (mode $46AA not 0): bit 3 selects the arpeggio ($51C5); otherwise the delay $46A9 is counted down first, adding step 4 on each tick of it when mode bit 1 is set (a slide into the note), and then the steps run ($51FA).

Voice 1 arpeggio: every $46A3 ticks (counter $46A1) play base note $46A7 plus the next offset from the table at ($46A5), with the index $46A9 counting down and going back to $46A8 below 0; the frequency from $471A/$4775 goes straight to $D400/$D401.

Voice 1 pitch steps: add step 1-4 ($469D-$46A4) to the current frequency $2F/$30 for $46BA-$46BD ticks each and write it to $D400/$D401; after the fourth, mode bit 7 restarts from the note's frequency ($489A), bit 0 repeats from here ($48A4), otherwise the frequency holds.

Voice 2 sound shaping, once per tick (from $B934): gate-off after the gate time $46DB (or when fewer ticks of the note $0B are left, with control bit 3 in $46DA), then the release time $46DC and the clearing of $D407-$D40D; then the pulse sweep ($52B7) and the pitch effect ($5315). As $50F4, with voice 2's variables.
Voice 2 pulse sweep: mode $46D1, delay $46D0, steps $46D2-$46D5 for $46E1/$46E2 ticks, width $2B/$2C to $D409/$D40A.
Voice 2 pitch effect: mode $46CD, arpeggio at $5333, delay $46CC (with step 4 during it for mode bit 1), steps at $5368.
Voice 2 arpeggio: every $46C6 ticks (counter $46C4) base note $46CA plus the offset from the table at ($46C8), index $46CC down to 0 then back to $46CB; to $D407/$D408.
Voice 2 pitch steps: steps $46C0-$46C7 for $46DD-$46E0 ticks added to the current frequency $15/$16, written to $D407/$D408; repeat or restart as mode $46CD says.

Voice 3 sound shaping, once per tick (from $B93A): gate-off after the gate time $DC (or by the note time $0C with control bit 3 in $DB), then the release time $DD and the clearing of $D40E-$D414, which also stops the filter sweep when voice 3 drives it ($5408 into $512E); then the pulse sweep ($541D) and the pitch effect ($546F).
Voice 3 pulse sweep: mode $D2, delay $D1, steps $D3-$D6 for $E2/$E3 ticks, width $2D/$2E to $D410/$D411.
Voice 3 pitch effect: mode $CE, arpeggio at $5489, delay $CD (with step 4 during it for mode bit 1), steps at $54B5.
Voice 3 arpeggio: every $C7 ticks (counter $C5) base note $CB plus the offset from the table at ($C9), index $CD down to 0 then back to $CC; to $D40E/$D40F.
Voice 3 pitch steps: steps $C1-$C8 for $DE-$E1 ticks added to the current frequency $17/$18, written to $D40E/$D40F; repeat or restart as mode $CE says.

Returns A not 0 (Z clear) while any voice of the music is still reading its track or releasing: $59 OR $5A OR $5B OR $46B9 OR $46DC OR $DD. The game-over screen waits on it ($6A9A). Voices 1 and 2 of a voice-3-only tune are never ticked, so their flags stay set until the next reset.
Returns A = $5B, voice 3's active flag (Z set once its track has ended). Used by check_music_end ($45BD).

Tune table: nine 7-byte records, one per tune: the voice 1, 2 and 3 track addresses (low, high) and the tempo (ticks per duration unit). start_tune takes Y = 7 x tune + 5, and load_tune reads $5526,Y (the tempo), then $5525,Y and $5526,Y backwards for voices 3, 2 and 1. Tune 0's record is $5525-$552B: voices 1 and 2 $59EF (a lone $C0, nothing), voice 3 $5E04, tempo 4. This first byte is also the base of the LDA $5525,Y at $4803.

Base of the LDA $5526,Y reads ($47F2, $4808), and bytes 1-6 of tune 0's record. Tune 0 plays on voice 3 alone (music mode 1) while voices 1 and 2 keep the sound effects: twice a 16-note bass figure with a pulse sound and a filter sweep. Started at $893D when an object of type $0E is collected (the handler at $8902, which gives an extra life for type 1) and at $A17D by the level timer, one second before the level's time limit ($A1B9: 45, 40, 25, 20, 20, 20, 15, 10 seconds). Apparently the filth-raid alarm (manual: a filth raid brings sirens).

Tune 1 (Y = $0C): voices $5B1A, $5B18, $5B10, tempo 6. Started at $6573 in the colour-completed sequence ($646F) when $BB0C flips from 0 to 2, with mode 2 (all voices) and speed 1 (two ticks a frame), before the loop at $6576 that counts the bonus kills: apparently the bonus-stage music, every second time (tune 4 the other times). A canon of four transposed figures, looping for ever from $5B1E.

Tune 2 (Y = $13): voices $59B9, $59B7, $59B5, tempo 7. Started at $6507 in the colour-completed sequence ($646F), in its first loop while $D022/$D023 cycle colours, once the music before it has faded out; it fades in (mode 2, speed 0). One C-5 held 224 ticks on all three voices, each an arpeggio of the table $5988, entering 0, 2 and 4 ticks apart.

Tune 3 (Y = $1A), the title tune: voices $6043, $61C9, $62D8 (the tracks are in $6043-$6387), tempo 5. Started by the title routine at $8F6A with mode 2 and speed 2 (four ticks a frame); the only tune for which start_tune sets $B94D to $70. Loops for ever.

Tune 4 (Y = $21): voice 3 only ($5C4F; voices 1 and 2 are the empty $59EF), tempo 2, changed four times inside by command $EA. Started at $6573 when $BB0C flips from 2 to 0, with mode 1 (voice 3 music, effects on voices 1 and 2) and speed 0: apparently the bonus-stage music of the other bonus stages ($BB0C is 2 in the loaded image, so the first bonus stage gets this one). Loops for ever.

Tune 5 (Y = $28), the get-ready tune: voices $59DD, $59F0, $59F2, tempo 5. Started at $6916 on the get-ready screen with mode 2 and speed 2 after a fade-in is set up: one D-4 on all three voices (voice 3 and voice 2 5 and 10 ticks late) whose pitch jumps about, held seven units of 160 ticks (5.6 seconds at four ticks a frame), then released.

Tune 6 (Y = $2F), the high-score tune: voices $57DF, $5657, $5947, tempo 9. Started at $6BC0 after the last game over when $BFD0 has left $BFF2 or $BFF3 not 0 (apparently a new entry in a high-score table; otherwise the game returns to the title, $6B8F), with mode 2 and speed 2, for the name entry that follows. Loops for ever.

Tune 7 (Y = $36), the game-over jingle: voices $5A00, $5A02, $5A35, tempo 2, all three playing the melody at $5A3B, voice 2 one tick and voice 1 three ticks after voice 3. Started at $6A91 when a player loses the last life, with mode 2 (speed as it was); the screen waits until it ends ($5513) or fire is pressed.

Tune 8 (Y = $3D), the Wiz-lab tune: voices $5A95, $5A93, $5A8B, tempo 8. Started at $AB75 as the Wiz-lab screen ($AB20, where the permanent weapon is chosen) opens, with mode 2 and speed 2, but only when $BB0C is 2, that is after a bonus stage that played tune 1; otherwise the lab is silent (mode 0). It plays tune 1's body with its own sound and tempo.

Instrument (29 bytes, layout at $4680): pulse at width $800, control $49 (gate released 20 ticks before the note's end), attack/decay $19, sustain/release $89, release 255 (held); vibrato (mode 5) +12, -12, +12 over 10, 20, 10 ticks after 50. Loaded whole by tune 6 voice 2 ($5691) and as a pitch block ($570C).

Instrument: sawtooth (control $21), attack/decay $CD, sustain/release $0F, gate 255, release 200; vibrato (mode 5) +17, -17, +17 over 10, 20, 10 ticks after 100; its pulse fields are unused (mode 0). Loaded by pattern $55E1 and as a pitch block at $5627; its last five bytes are the envelope block $5599.
Envelope block (5 bytes for command $D2, here at $55FE): control $21, attack/decay $CD, sustain/release $0F, gate 255, release 200; also the last five bytes of the instrument at $5581.
Pitch block (14 bytes for command $E8, here at $5622): mode 4, a fall of 10 per tick for 255 ticks after a 90-tick delay.
Envelope block ($D2 at $55F5): control $29 (sawtooth, gate released 20 ticks before the end), attack/decay $5A, sustain/release $CB, release 200.
Pitch block ($E8 at $5707): mode 7, vibrato +12, -12, +12 over 10, 20, 10 ticks after a 40-tick delay during which the pitch rises 13 a tick.
Envelope block ($D2 at $571B): control $21 (sawtooth), attack/decay $16, sustain/release $87, gate 20, release 10.
Instrument: noise, control $89 (gate released 25 ticks before the end), attack/decay $03, sustain/release $27, release 10, no pitch or pulse effect: a drum. Tune 6 voice 1 ($57E1).

Tune 6 pattern, called by voice 2 ($5687) and voice 3 ($596F): with instrument $5581 a slow tune (A-4, G-4, F#-4, A#-4 B-4 C#-5, D-5 ... F#-4), changing the envelope ($55AC, $5599), the attack/decay ($CA $19), the pitch block ($559E for a falling note, then $5581's vibrato again), and bending the last note with live pitch mode 7 and step 4 ($D4 $0D, $DC $06).

Tune 6 bass rhythm: note 0 nine times (codes 4, 8 and 16), always called with a transpose from voice 2 ($5723-$5761), so each call is one chord root in rhythm (an arpeggio instrument makes it a chord).

Tune 6 voice 2 track: instrument $5798 (a rising triangle blip) for an opening rhythm on G#-6 and C-5/D-7; pattern $55E1; then twice a melody on instruments $5564 and $5863 (long notes by switching sustain/release to $8D and back to $89); then chords: instrument $577B (24 bytes) with envelope $55BF, fifteen rests, and the rhythm $5644 on a series of roots with the arpeggio table changed by $DA 08 ($57BB, $57C1, $57C7, $57B5, $57CD); ends with $C8 00 $5657, back to the start with the transpose reset.

Instrument: arpeggio (mode 8) of the table $57B5 from index 5, a new note every 4 ticks; loaded whole it is sawtooth (control $21), attack/decay $18, sustain/release $6A, gate 30, release 150. Tune 6 voice 1 loads all 29 bytes ($57F4), voice 2 the first 24 ($5717).
Instrument: triangle (control $11), attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F2, gate 5, release 6, rising 1,200 a tick (mode 4) from the start: a short upward blip. Tune 6 voice 2's first sound ($5657).
Arpeggio table, 6 offsets read from index 5 down to 0: 0, 4, 7, 12, 24, 12 semitones, a major chord. The first of five tables that tune 6 switches between with $DA 08 commands.
Arpeggio table: 0, 4, 9, 12, 24, 12 (third and sixth, no fifth).
Arpeggio table: 0, 4, 10, 12, 24, 12 (third and minor seventh: a dominant seventh without its fifth).
Arpeggio table: 0, 3, 7, 12, 24, 12, a minor chord.
Arpeggio table: 0, 4, 7, 9, 24, 12, a major sixth chord.
Tune 6 voice 1 chord pattern: table $57C1, a rest, then F#-3 five times (code 12); called at pitch ($580E) and a whole tone down ($C6 $FE at $5837).
Tune 6 voice 1 track start: a rest of code 4, then on into the part at $57E1 that the track loops back to.
