Tune 6 voice 1 from its loop point (the $C4 at $5850 comes back here): the drum $55C4 on F-7 (a noise hit) three times and seven bars of three; then instrument $577B's arpeggiated chords, five at a time on A-3, G-3, the pattern $57D3, B-3, D-3 and so on, with the chord table switched by $DA 08 as it goes.

Filter program (16 bytes for command $E0: four cutoff steps, their four tick counts, delay, mode, start cutoff; here at $594C): steps +10, -10, +10, -10 for 8, 16, 8, 0 ticks after a 50-tick delay, mode 7, start cutoff $384.

Instrument, tune 6's melody sound: pulse, control $49 (released 15 ticks before the end), attack/decay $18, sustain/release $6B, release 254; vibrato (mode 5) +7, -7, +7 over 10, 20, 10 ticks after 40; pulse sweep (mode 5) from $900, +3 and -3 for 120 ticks each after 10. Loaded by voice 3 ($5964, $5972) and voice 2 (its first 14 bytes, $56CF); patterns $58AB and $58C2 reload its pitch block after each use of $5880.
Pitch block (mode 4): a rise of 6 a tick for 255 ticks after 40; patterns $58AB and $58C2 use it for single notes ($58B9, $58D3, $58E9, $5911).

Instrument: pulse at $800 (control $41), attack/decay $07, sustain/release $68, gate 40, release 40, falling 10 a tick after 25 (mode 4). Tune 6 voice 3's opening sound ($5947), whose fall is changed to 3 and to 8 a tick by $DA 00.

Tune 6 voice 3 bass bar: A-2 and E-3 in a fixed rhythm (A-2 E-3 E-3 A-2 A-2 E-3 E-3), a last E-2 with the rising pitch block $5880, then $5863's vibrato again. Called by $58C2 at pitch and an octave down ($C6 $F4 at $593D).

Tune 6 voice 3 bass line: bar $58AB, then the same rhythm on G-2/E-3, F#-2/E-3, B-2/F#-3, D-2/A-2, A-2/E-3, F#-2/C#-3 and E-2/B-2, some bars ending with the rising $5880, and $58AB an octave down and at pitch; called three times by $5947 and once at its end.

Tune 6 voice 3 track: instrument $588E, filter on voice 3 with program $5853, four bars of a G#-1/B-2 figure; instrument $5863 and the bass line $58C2 three times; filter off and pattern $55E1; 21 rests; filter on, E-3 F#-2 G#-2 and the bass line again; then back to its start.
Arpeggio table of tune 2, 16 offsets read from index 15 down: 0, 5, 3, 7, 12, 0, 5, 7, 3, 12, 0, 7, 5, 3, 12, 5 - the intervals 0, 3, 5, 7 and 12 in a shifting order.
Instrument of tune 2: sawtooth (control $21), attack/decay $33, sustain/release $9A, gate 50, release 50; arpeggio (mode 8) of the table $5988 from index 15, a note every 5 ticks.
Tune 2 voice 3 track: two rests of 2 ticks ($BF 02), then on into voice 2's track.
Tune 2 voice 2 track: one rest of 2 ticks, then on into voice 1's.
Tune 2 voice 1 track, which voices 2 and 3 run into: instrument $5998 and one C-5 of code 32 (224 ticks at tempo 7), then the end ($C0).

Instrument of tune 5: pulse at $800 (control $41), attack/decay $FF, sustain/release $F0, gate 255, release 1; pitch mode 5 with steps $4E20, $67A8, $36B0 and $63C0 added every tick for 220 ticks each, so the 16-bit frequency wraps round every few ticks: a bubbling, random-sounding pitch.
Tune 5 voice 1 track: filter on voice 1 with the program $5EC3, then on into the shared part at $59E1.

Tune 5's shared track (voice 1 runs into it, voices 3 and 2 jump to it 5 and 10 ticks later): instrument $59C0, one D-4 of code 32 (160 ticks) held through six more rests of code 32, then live gate time 1 ($D4 $1B 01) to release it; ends at $59EF.
A lone $C0: the end of tune 5's track, and the whole track of voices 1 and 2 in tunes 0 and 4, which play on voice 3 only.
Tune 5 voice 2 track: a rest of code 1 (5 ticks), then on into voice 3's.
Tune 5 voice 3 track: a rest of code 1, then a jump to the shared part $59E1.

Set-up pattern without notes: instrument $5E40, filter on (for voice 3, the only voice that calls it), filter program $5E30, return. Called by tune 4 ($5CA7, $5D3B), tune 7's voice 3 ($5A35) and pattern $5E93.
Tune 7 voice 1 track: a rest of 2 ticks, then on into voice 2's.
Tune 7 voice 2 track: instrument $5E40, a rest of 1 tick, then a jump to the shared melody $5A3B.
Pitch block of tune 7 (mode 4): a rise of 147 a tick for 7 ticks after 2.
Pitch block of tune 7 (mode 4): after 5 ticks, one drop of $0700 (1,792).
Pitch block of tune 7's last note (mode 5): +85 for 4 ticks, -85 for 4, a 2-tick hold, over and over, after a 4-tick delay.
Tune 7 voice 3 track: set-up $59F7 (instrument $5E40, filter on voice 3), filter program $5E5D, then on into the shared melody, which it starts first.

Tune 7's melody, played by all three voices a tick or three apart: control $41, gate 45, transpose +9; four times a falling G-4 (pitch block $5A19, 10 ticks), a rising D-4 ($5A0B) and a plain E-4; then G-4 G-4 A-4 G-4 F-4 E-4 F-4 E-4 D-4 E-4 F-4 E-4 D-4 D-4 C-4 A-3 C-4 D-4 and a long C-4 with vibrato ($5A27); end. Written notes; they sound a major sixth higher.
Tune 8 voice 3 track: filter program $5ABF, the code at $5AFF (all three voices through the filter), a rest of code 8, then on through voice 2's and voice 1's starts.
Tune 8 voice 2 track: a rest of code 8 (64 ticks), then on into voice 1's.

Tune 8 voice 1 track: instrument $5AA2 with the pulse sweep off ($CA 11 00) and control $15 (triangle with ring modulation), then a jump to tune 1's body at $5B1E. With the rests before them the three voices play that body 64 ticks apart.

Instrument of tunes 1 and 8: pulse at $800 (control $41), attack/decay $03, sustain/release $97, gate 13, release 8, falling 200 a tick after 10 (mode 4), pulse width growing 50 a tick for 255 ticks (mode 4).
Filter program of tunes 1 and 8 ($E0 at $5A8B and $5B10): steps -2, -2, +2, +2 for 255 ticks each after a 255-tick delay, mode 5 (repeating), start cutoff $4B0.
Tune 1 figure 1: C-1 A#-0 G#-0 F-0 D#-0 C-0 (written notes, code 4 each), called four times a bar at the transposes 67, 55, 43 and 31 ($5B22-$5B2E).
Tune 1 figure 2, the same notes going up: C-0 D#-0 F-0 G#-0 A#-0 C-1 ($5B35-$5B41, transposes 71, 57, 45, 31).
Tune 1 figure 3: C-1 C-0 A#-0 C-0 G-0 D#-0 ($5B49-$5B55, transposes 50, 55, 53, 58).

Machine code in the music data, called by command $D6 from tune 8's voice 3 ($5A8E) and tune 1's ($5B13): $D417 = $F7 (resonance 15, voices 1-3 through the filter), $D418 = $1F, filter voice $57 = 3 (no voice's notes restart the program), then JMP $4D3B to start the program just loaded ($5ABF) at once.
Tune 1 voice 3 track: filter program $5ABF, the code at $5AFF, a rest of code 6, then on through voice 2's and voice 1's starts.
Tune 1 voice 2 track: a rest of code 6 (36 ticks), then on into voice 1's; so the voices come in 36 ticks apart.
Tune 1 voice 1 track: instrument $5AA2, then the body at $5B1E.

Tune 1's body, shared by all three voices of tunes 1 and 8: twice, figure 1 ($5ACF) twice at four transposes and figure 2 ($5ADC) likewise; figure 3 ($5AE9) four times through four transposes; figure 4 ($5AF6) four times through eight; then back here, for ever.

Instrument of tune 4: pulse at $800, control $49 (released 2 ticks before the end), attack/decay $03, sustain/release $A7, release 5; vibrato (mode 5) +40, -40, +40 over 3, 5, 2 ticks after 10; pulse sweep (mode 4) +160 for 12 ticks, then -68 for 255.
Filter program of tune 4 ($E0 at $5C50): steps -40, +4, +12, -12 for 20, 25, 20, 20 ticks, no delay, mode 4 (holds after the four steps), start cutoff $2BC.
Pitch block of tune 4 ($E8 at $5CF8): mode 5, steps -45, 0, +45, 0 for 4 ticks each after 16, repeating.
Pitch block of tune 4 ($E8 at $5CFD): mode 7, a fall of 30 a tick for 255 ticks after 15, rising 4 a tick during those 15.
Tune 4 phrase: a rest, D-3 E-3 D-3 B-2 A#-2, a rest, A-2 (codes 1, 2, 3 and 6); called four times ($5CB5-$5CCA), each after a different held note.
Tune 4 melody phrase (A-2 F#-3 G-3 D-3 D#-3 E-3 G-3 ... about fifty notes), ending with a G-2 E-2 figure played twice; called at $5CAA and $5CCD.
Tune 4 bass figure: F-1 F-1 F-2 F-1 (code 2 each), called a whole tone down and at pitch ($5D5E, $5D62).

Tune 4 voice 3 track, the whole tune: filter on voice 3 with program $5B9D, instrument $5B80, a bass line of octave jumps falling from B to G#, and a twice-repeated section of falling lines; then tempo 4, set-up $59F7, melody $5BDA and the phrases $5BC9 with the pulse width set by $DA 16; a lead passage with pitch blocks $5BAD and $5BBB; four bars of figures; tempo 5 for the chord section $5E93; tempo 3 for four bars with the bass $5C46; G-2/F-2 and C-2 riffs; tempo 2 and back to the start.

Tune 0 voice 3 track, the whole tune: instrument $5E40, filter on voice 3 with program $5E30, then twice the 16 notes A-1 A-1 E-2 E-2 D#-2 D#-2 D-2 D-2 A-2 A-2 G#-2 G-2 E-2 D#-2 D-2 C-2 (code 2: 8 ticks each at tempo 4); end.
Filter program ($E0 at $59FC and $5E09): steps +20, -20, +50, -50 for 4 ticks each after 10, mode 7, start cutoff $258.

Instrument of tunes 0, 4 and 7: pulse, control $49 (released 2 ticks before the end), attack/decay $01, sustain/release $C4, release 5; vibrato (mode 5) +20, -20, +20 over 2, 4, 2 ticks after 8; pulse sweep (mode 5) from $400, +100 for 20 ticks then -10 for 200.
Filter program of tune 7's voice 3 ($E0 at $5A38): steps +20, -20, +20 for 4 ticks each, and +120 a tick during the 4-tick delay (mode 7), start cutoff $064.
Arpeggio set-up for command $E8 ($5E96): mode 8, a note every 5 ticks from the table at $5E7B, starting at index 7.
Arpeggio table, 8 offsets read from index 7 down: 0, -2, -4, -2, +3, -2, -4, -2 semitones. Pattern $5EAC switches between it, $5E83 and $5E8B.

Tune 4's arpeggio section (called at tempo 5 from $5D35): set-up $59F7, arpeggio $5E6D, filter program $5ED3, control $41 and gate held; one B-4 of code 16 that sounds on while $5EAC changes its chord three times with rests between, then runs into $5EAC once more.
Chord changes for the section at $5E93: live arpeggio table $5E83, $5E7B, $5E8B, $5E7B in turn ($DC 08), a rest of code 16 after each of the first three.
Filter program of tune 5 ($E0 at $59DE) and the title tune ($6048): steps -6, -1, +1, +6 for 128, 255, 255, 128 ticks, no delay, mode 5 (repeating), start cutoff $44C.

Instrument of the title tune (voice 1 at $6043; 13 bytes of it at $60AE, its pitch block at $60EB): pulse at $800 (control $41), attack/decay $06, sustain/release $FA, gate 255, release 254; vibrato (mode 7) +25, -25, +25 over 9, 18, 9 ticks after 100, rising 10 a tick during the delay; pulse sweep (mode 5) +8 and -8 for 160 ticks each. Tune 4's $E0 at $5E99 loads its first 16 bytes as a filter program (start cutoff $A0A0).
Pitch block of the title tune ($E8 at $6088): mode 5, steps -73, 0, +73, 0 for 10 ticks each after 10.
Five bytes laid out like an envelope block: control $41, attack/decay $06, sustain/release $F6, gate 20, release 50. No command in the tunes points at them (the address does not occur in the image).
Pitch block of the title tune ($E8 at $608D and $60DF): mode 4, +20 a tick for 41 ticks, a hold of 40, -40 a tick for 20, after 5.

Instrument of the title tune ($D0 at $6150 and $6237): triangle and pulse together (control $51), attack/decay $09, sustain/release $8A, gate 20, release 254; a slow rise of 4 a tick (mode 5) after 10; pulse sweep (mode $85, restarting) from $480, +41 for 28 ticks then +124 for 4.

Machine code called by the title tune's voice 1 ($604D, command $D6): $57 = 3, so no voice's notes restart the filter program any more and the sweep voice 1 started ($6048, program $5EC3) runs on by itself.

Title tune pattern ($6159, $615C on voice 1, $6245 on voice 2): four bars of a D-minor arpeggio figure (D-4 D-6 A-5 F-5, then D, F and A in shorter notes) and four of the same on E major (B-3 E-6 B-5 G#-5 ...).

Title tune pattern ($615F on voice 1, $6248 on voice 2), running on to $6042: the same arpeggio figure four bars each over F, E, D#, D, C#, C, B and A#, a bass line falling a semitone at a time under changing chords.

Title tune (tune $1A, started by $8F61): the end of the arpeggio pattern that begins at $5F6A in the previous range, called by the sequence command $C2 from $615F (voice 1) and $6248 (voice 2). Events are two bytes: a note below $60 with an index into the duration table, or a note $60-$BF with a literal duration; note $5F is a rest; $CC n ... $CE repeats n times; $C0 returns. $6000 is the duration byte of the note at $5FFF. Then the $CE ending the sixth block ($600B), the seventh block ($600C-$6026, first note $23) and the eighth ($6027-$6041, first note $22), each played four times, and the $C0 at $6042. Each block's first note is a semitone below the last, from $29 at $5F6C.

Title tune (tune $1A: its record at $553A points voice 1 here, voice 2 at $61C9, voice 3 at $62D8, speed 5), voice 1's sequence, $6043-$6166: loads the instrument at $5ED3 ($D0), switches the voice into the filter ($DE), copies 16 bytes from $5EC3 into $31-$40 ($E0), calls the code at $5F2E ($D6), then notes $34-$45 among long rests with instrument ($E8) and parameter ($CA, $DA, $D4, $DC) changes, a $CC $7F rest loop, instrument $5F11 at $6150, 24 rests, the pattern $5F33 twice and the pattern $5F6A ($C2 at $6159, $615C, $615F), a rest, and $C4 at $6164 jumping back to $6043, so the tune loops until another is started.

Title tune: a 29-byte instrument definition, loaded by the $D0 $1C commands of voice 2 at $621D and voice 3 at $6331. For voice 1 the same command fills $87-$A3, and bytes 24-26 ($41 $B6 $FF here) land in $9F-$A1, which $4DA6-$4DC1 write to the SID's control, attack/decay and sustain/release registers.

Five bytes, $41 $00 $56 $0C $32, between the instrument at $6167 and the tables at $6189. They have the shape of the block a $D2 command copies into $9F-$A3 (control $41, attack/decay $00, sustain/release $56, then $0C $32), but no sequence of the nine tunes in the table at $5525 refers to $6184 and no pointer to it was found in memory: apparently unused.

Title tune, voice 2: four 16-byte tables at $6189, $6199, $61A9 and $61B9 whose addresses voice 2's $DA/$DC commands put in its 16-bit instrument parameter 8 ($61CD, $61DF, $61E8, $61F2, $61FB, $620A, $6219). Each table is four groups of four bytes ending in $07 ($05 $0C $00 $07 ...). What the driver does with parameter 8 is in its own code.

Title tune (tune $1A), voice 2's sequence, $61C9-$624D: loads the instrument at $625E, points parameter 8 at $6189, 13 rests, note $3C, then long rests while switching parameter 8 between $6199 and $6189, parameter $12 swept ($FFFF then $0000) with the tables $61A9 and $61B9, instrument $6167 for three rounds of notes $18 and $1F, then instrument $5F11, 24 rests, the shared patterns $5F33 and $5F6A ($C2 at $6245 and $6248), and $C4 at $624B back to $61C9.
Title tune, voice 3: 16 bytes that the $E0 command at $634A copies into $31-$40, the block voice 1's own $E0 fills from $5EC3 at $6048.

Title tune: a 29-byte instrument definition loaded first by both voice 2 ($61C9) and voice 3 ($62D8) with $D0 $1C; bytes 24-26 are $41 $FE $BF (control, attack/decay, sustain/release in the layout $4DA6 uses) and bytes 8-9 are $6298, so parameter 8 starts at voice 3's first table.
Title tune: a 29-byte instrument definition loaded by voice 3's $D0 $1C at $6340, before its filtered bass notes.

Title tune, voice 3: four 16-byte tables at $6298, $62A8, $62B8 and $62C8 that voice 3's $DC commands put in its instrument parameter 8 ($62EA, $62F3, $62FD, $631E, $6327). They hold the same values as voice 2's tables at $6189-$61C8, each rotated by two bytes ($00 $07 $04 $0C ... against $05 $0C $00 $07 ...).

Title tune (tune $1A), voice 3's sequence, $62D8-$6387: loads the instrument at $625E, rests, note $3C, long rests alternating parameter 8 between the tables $62A8 and $6298, a sweep (parameters $1B, $12, $16), note $3C and more rests with the tables $62B8 and $62C8, instrument $6167 for notes $1D and $1A, instrument $627B, the filter ($DE, $E0 $624E), bass notes $1D, $17 and $22 each followed by long rests, note $16, a rest with literal duration ($BF $05), and $C4 at $6385 back to $62D8.
One byte, $EE, between the end of the title tune's voice 3 ($6387) and the entry at $6389. Nothing refers to it; $EE is also the byte that fills the unused table space at $4680-$4716.

Game entry, where Yeti's depacker jumps once the game is unpacked: sets the processor port $01 to $35 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000) and jumps to the initialisation at $EC00, which ends in the title sequence at $8F61. The two bytes after the JMP, $6390-$6391 ($0D $BB), are not referenced by any traced code.
Two bytes, $0D $BB, between the entry's JMP $EC00 and start_new_game at $6392. No traced code reads or runs them.

Start a new game. Reached by JMP from the title sequence when fire is pressed: $9014 (title and high scores), $90BA (player menu), $94D2 (Wiztips). Blanks the screen ($8C44), clears both sides' score digits $BFDA-$BFE7 and loads the table's top score into the HUD's HI digits $71D4-$71D9 ($70D3), sets up the sides, their lives and the continue level ($6830), then falls into the life cycle at $639B.

The outer game cycle, one pass per life (JMP $639B at $63C7): fades the music out ($45CE = $FF); resets the per-life variables and loads the current side's saved state ($6E42); clears the play screens and places the Wizball at the level's start ($63CA); 'get ready!' until fire ($6893); draws the HUD rows ($70EC); silences the SID ($BAAD); installs the play display list $B3E2 (pointer at $B414) with $7CB4; plays the life ($63E0, back when the life is over); 'game over' if it was the side's last Wizball ($69F2); blanks the screen ($8C44); saves the side's state ($6E38); takes the life away and picks the next side ($6B27, which leaves for the high scores when the game is over).

Prepares the play screen for a new life: clears the first page of $E000, $E400 and $E800 ($7C51), clears $B874 (the colour-complete flag) and $B1F9, puts the Wizball's x position $B20D at $AC, clears $F808-$FAD7 and the shot table $0480-$04FF and scatters five star pixels ($7540), and sets up the landscape at the level's start position ($75E0, entered by JMP so that its RTS returns to the cycle).

Plays one life: setup, then the frame loop at $640E until the life is over. Setup in order: icon-bar sprite pointers and the feature flags $B231-$B239 reset ($720B); the side's permanent Wiz-lab features re-applied ($6E4F); landscape colour RAM and multicolours for the level ($7D1A); highest reachable level $B1CE ($A9C6); random alien lists for the three highest reachable levels ($9F5F); font in play polarity ($8C84); one scroll step ($7A98); the four cauldron sprites back to the empty outline and the level's glyphs and colours ($9DE9, which calls $776D); alien table $0200 cleared ($9CD5); screen on ($8C50); the Wizball's start state, materialising ($8040); sprite multicolours $E7E9 = $0B, $E7EA = $0D (the band at $8A94 copies them to $D025/$D026); particle table $0300 cleared ($9CCB).

The frame loop, one pass per frame (reached after the setup, and by JMP from $AE0E and $AF1D where play resumes after the Wiz-lab or a completed level). Order: wait for raster 200-255 ($6E83); music player off while voice 3 plays no tune ($45BD); copy $B874 to $8309 for the HUD interrupt and leave for $646F if the colour is complete; RUN/STOP pause ($6EB7); while the Wizball lives ($B1CF = 0) its and the cat's character-cell boxes and the $0300 particles ($9AD6); erase the shots ($7090); scroll the landscape ($7A98); the Wizball: control and movement, or the death sequence ($7DF4); the cat's fire ($881F); icon bar: pearls light icons, a stick wiggle takes one ($72AA); copy a quarter of the landscape between the screen buffers ($77F7); move and draw the shots ($6F0D); while alive, shift the particles with the scroll ($99BD); move the stars ($747E); read joysticks and keys ($7429); give the sticks to Wiz and cat ($697D); cauldrons, which set $B874 ($9E0D); wait for raster 70-198 ($681D); the cat ($8640); start aliens whose landscape positions scroll into view ($A9DA); the six aliens ($A204); the level timer ($A14A). Loops until $B1CF is non-zero and the death countdown $B1D0 has reached 1, then returns to $63BB.

Colour completed: the frame loop jumps here when $B874 is non-zero (the mix cauldron is full, see $9E0D). Fades the music out, starts the Wizball dematerialising ($B216 = 2), moves sound effect 5 to voice 2 ($3CD7 = 2), zeroes the scroll, speed and bonus counters ($B1F2, $B1F4-$B1F9, $B1FB, $B1FF, $A858 ...), puts the Wizball at x $AC, erases the shots from the screen ($7090), frees the aliens ($A1C9), loads the bonus wave script ($9CB2: $3902 to $ED02) and gives the Wizball thrust and anti-grav ($7379 twice). Then, once a frame until the dematerialising ends ($B216 = 0): the Wizball with no stick input ($B23F = $FF) and the cat's input $FA (up and left), the landscape background cycling through colours ($B25C = 1, stepped by the band at $8A44) and $D022/$D023 incremented, and tune $13 started once the fade has reached 0. Then the bonus stage setup: colour RAM black, landscape restarted ($75E0), $0300 cleared, colour RAM $0C, multicolours 6 and $0E, materialising again ($B216 = 1, $B214 = $17), message 1 ($6733 = 1, 'colour completed / laboratory imminent'), the font copied into the landscape glyphs ($6743), and tune $21 or $0C, alternating through $BB0C.

The bonus stage, one pass per frame: wait for raster 200-255; sticks to Wiz and cat; cell boxes while $B1CF = 0; erase shots; pause; unless the tally has begun ($6733 bit 1): the Wizball ($7DF4), the cat and its fire; the scroll speed ramp ($6755) into $B1F4 and, when moving, the stars; move shots; particles while $B1CF = 0; icon bar; messages and tally ($6615); wait for raster 70-198; unless tallying, the next step of the wave script ($9CEA); aliens; read the sticks. The landscape does not scroll here. It ends when $B1CF is set: $36 (the script's end, $9D38) shows 'congratulations!' and the tally ($6733 = 3), any other value (the Wizball hit) the tally only ($6733 = 2); $B1CF = $80 then marks it handled, $7DF4 runs each frame through $65D2, and when the message time $6734 runs out sound effect 5 goes back to voice 1 and $AB20 (the Wiz-lab) takes over.

Runs the messages of the colour-completed and bonus phases, once a frame from $65B6 (and from $65E8 to cut message 1 short). State $6733: 0 nothing; on the first call of state 1 page 1 ('colour completed / laboratory imminent'), of state 2 page 3 (tally), of state 3 page 2 ('congratulations!' and tally); for 2 and 3 it also shows sprite 1 (shape $60, x $6D, y $8C, colour 5) and resets the count ($66E9). Bit 7 marks it started. Each call: one tally step in states 2 and 3 ($6693), draws the page in cycling colours ($66FC), counts $6734 down, and at 0 clears the state and redraws the page in colour 0 with character offset 0 to take it away.

One step of the bonus tally: until the tallied count $A859 equals $A858 (aliens shot since $64A8 cleared it, stopping at 255), keeps the message on ($6734 = $FF) and, every second call ($A85A), adds 40 points (A = 4 to $710B) and increments $A859 and the three digits $B841-$B843 of 'x 40 x 000' (a space digit becomes 1, 9 carries). With the count equal it returns and the timer runs out.
Resets the bonus tally: $A859 = 0 and the digits $B841-$B843 of 'x 40 x 000' to space, space, 0.

Draws message page $6735 (pointer from the table at $6739) with the printer $8CFA. While the timer $6734 runs, the colour steps every second frame ($6737) through the 12 colours at $B61C ($6738); with the timer at 0 it draws in colour 0. $B874 is non-zero in these phases, so the printer writes to the landscape screen with $6732 added.

Character offset the printer adds to each screen code when $B874 is non-zero ($8D16 puts it into the ADC operand at $8D8E): $A0, so letters come from glyphs $A0-$DF of the landscape character set, where $6743 copies the font. $6687 sets it to 0 for the pass that takes a message away and $668F puts $A0 back.

Message state of the colour-completed and bonus phases ($6615): 0 none, 1 'colour completed', 2 tally, 3 'congratulations!' and tally; bit 7 set once started. Bit 1 also stops the Wizball, cat and wave script in the bonus loop (tests at $658A and $65BC). Written at $6548, $65ED, $65FA, $666E, $6682.

Frames left for the current message ($6615 decrements it, $6693 holds it at $FF while the tally runs, $65E5 sets 1 to end message 1 early). The bonus loop waits for 0 before leaving for the Wiz-lab ($6605).
Page number for $66FC: 1 colour completed, 2 congratulations and tally, 3 tally only; index into the word table at $6739. The byte after it, $6736, is not referenced.
Frame counter of the message colour cycle: $66FC advances the colour when it is even. Cleared at $6627; also read and written at $B12F-$B132.
Index 0-11 into the colour list at $B61C for the message colour ($66FC), cleared at $6624; also stepped by $B139.

Word table of the message pages for $66FC, indexed by $6735 x 2: entry 0 $0000 (unused), 1 $B7E8 'colour completed / laboratory imminent', 2 $B813 'congratulations! / tishshshshsh / x 40 x 000', 3 $B826 'tishshshshsh / x 40 x 000', 4 $B7E8 again (never selected).
High byte of entry 0 of the message page table at $6739 ($672A reads the table as $673A,Y); the table runs to $6742.

Copies glyphs 0-63 of the font at $F000 ($F000-$F1FF) over $FD00-$FEFF, which the landscape band's character set at $F800 (its $D018 value comes from $8A25) shows as glyphs $A0-$DF. Called at $654B before the bonus stage, so that text printed with the offset $6732 shows letters there. The level's own glyphs at $FD00 are copied back by $77C6 when a level is set up again.

Bonus stage scroll speed ramp, once a frame: with $B1F8 set (by the wave script at $9D31) it adds $10 to the fraction $B1F7 and carries into $B1F6 until $B1F6 reaches 6; with $B1F8 clear it runs $B1F6.$B1F7 down to 0. The loop copies $B1F6 into the scroll speed $B1F4.
Waits for raster line 266 ($6E92) and fills colour RAM rows 3-22 ($D878-$DB97) with 0; entry $678A takes the colour in A instead.

Entry of $6788 with the colour in A (from $652A with $0C): waits for raster line 266 ($6E92, which also moves the stars) and fills $D878-$DB97, colour RAM rows 3-22, 256 bytes at each of $D878, $D978, $DA78 and $DA98.

Flashes the current side's part of the HUD, from the play display list's band at $89FF (in the raster interrupt). $B88F counts frames, $B890 steps every fourth; the colours come from $B5CB, $B5D7 and $B5DF indexed by $B890 AND 7. Writes colour RAM rows 0-1: six cells from column $71DC/$71DD ('1UP' and score, column 0 or 34), the HI score's columns 17-22 as well when $720A says this side has passed it (not in the Wiz-lab, $AC4E = 0), two cells of row 1 at $71DE/$71DF (columns 9-10 or 29-30; colour 0 while $8309, the copy of $B874, is set) and the lives digit at $71E0/$71E1 (column 7 or 32). In the lab it also fills columns 12-27 of rows 0-1 with the cycling colour $EBD7.

Waits until the raster is between lines 70 and 198 ($46-$C6 with bit 8 clear). The frame loop's second synchronisation point ($6453; also $650A, $65B9): with $6E83 at the top, it keeps the loop to one pass per frame.

Game setup for both sides: clears $B116-$B12E (all but the level $B128); for a continued game ($AF7E = n, chosen on the title with the keys 0-5, see $AF85) marks levels 1..n complete ($B11F.. = 3), gives the first n permanent features from $B10D (1, 1, 2, 3, 5) and starts on level $B128 = n; saves the block as both sides' state ($6E08, $6E14); lives $B278 = $B279 = 3; current side $BFD9 = 1; and copies the player-menu mode $B272's record from $B2AC (4 bytes each) into $BFD6-$BFD8: side 1 kind, side 2 kind (1 player, 2 team) and the number of sides (1 or 2).

The 'get ready!' screen, before each life: sprites off, background 10, display list $B4B2 (music bands only), screen $EC00 filled with glyph $DE, colour RAM 0; the page chosen from the word table at $B71B by the side and mode bits (current side, number of sides, side 2 kind, side 1 kind from $BFD9-$BFD6) printed in the large font: 'get ready!', 'wizard / press fire', 'player one / press fire', 'team one / wizard / press fire', 'player two ...', 'team two ...'. Eight white sprites (shape $0C) as the rings, tune $28. Loops ($691C) moving the rings ($90BD), cycling the background ($98BE, $EBD7) and the ring colours every 5 frames ($B87D), showing the rings twice a frame ($915F, $9163 at line $87), until fire on either port ($91FA bit 4). The port pressed goes to $B240 (0: port 2, $10: port 1) for $697D. Screen off, music off.

Gives the joysticks to the Wiz ($B23F) and the cat ($B23E), once a frame after $7429 has read port 2 into $B256 and port 1 into $B257. A team side: the Wiz gets the port fire was pressed on at 'get ready!' ($B240), the cat the other. A single player: the Wiz gets that port and the cat only its fire bit ($EF or $FF); but with the catelite ($B234) and fire held for 10 frames ($B242), the cat gets the whole stick and the Wiz no directions and a fire bit that toggles each frame ($B241), the manual's 'hold fire to steer the cat'.

After a life: returns at once unless the current side had one Wizball left ($B277,side = 1). Otherwise draws 'game over' ($6AC9, large font, $8E32) into sprite shapes from $B4 (cleared, $B4-$B9) and, from shape $B5 and 42 bytes lower ($8EDB = $2A), the side's name from the table at $6B11 ($8DE4); while shape $B9 is borrowed the first cauldron sprite shows the clean outline (pointer $B51E = $38, back to $B9 at $6AC5). Sets sprites 2-7 from $B4E5-$B504, erases the shots, blanks colour RAM rows 9-11 columns 11-28, plays tune $36 and waits once a frame ($6E92): the sprite colours cycle, fire is only read after the tune has ended ($5513), and it gives up after 1,000 frames ($9215 with 200, stepped every 5 by $921E). Leaves the first cauldron's row counter $9EC6 at 0.
Text 'GAME OVER' and its $FF ($6AC9-$6AD2), with no column and row: $69F2 draws it into sprite shapes $B4-$B9 in the large font through the pointer at $6B0F.
Column 8 and row 0 of the ' PLAYER ONE' record: the page the high-score entry prints as its heading (entry 0 of the table at $6B19); the text follows at $6AD5.
' PLAYER ONE', $FF, and the $FF that ends the page ($6AD5-$6AE1): the name the game-over sprites show for side 1 as one player (entry 0 of the table at $6B11).
Column 8 and row 0 of the '  TEAM ONE ' record: heading page entry 1 of the table at $6B19; the text is at $6AE4.
'  TEAM ONE ', $FF, $FF ($6AE4-$6AF0): side 1 as a team, entry 1 of the table at $6B11.
Column 8 and row 0 of the ' PLAYER TWO' record: heading page entry 2 of the table at $6B19; the text is at $6AF3.
' PLAYER TWO', $FF, $FF ($6AF3-$6AFF): side 2 as one player, entry 2 of the table at $6B11.
Column 8 and row 0 of the '  TEAM TWO ' record: heading page entry 3 of the table at $6B19; the text is at $6B02.
'  TEAM TWO ', $FF, $FF ($6B02-$6B0E): side 2 as a team, entry 3 of the table at $6B11.
Pointer to 'GAME OVER' at $6AC9, low byte here, read into X at $6A0E for the sprite text printer $8E32.
High byte of the 'GAME OVER' pointer at $6B0F ($6A), read into Y at $6A11.

Word table of the side names without their column and row, for the sprite printer $8DE4 at $6A33 (game over): $6AD5 player one, $6AE4 team one, $6AF3 player two, $6B02 team two, indexed by (side - 1) x 4 + (side kind - 1) x 2.
High byte of entry 0 of the side-name text table at $6B11, and entries 1-3 after it ($6B13-$6B18); $6A36 reads the table as $6B12,Y.
Word table of the side-name pages with their column and row, for the high-score entry heading at $6C12: $6AD3 player one, $6AE2 team one, $6AF1 player two, $6B00 team two, indexed by $6B21.
High byte of entry 0 of the side-name page table at $6B19, followed by entries 1-3 ($6B1B-$6B20); read as $6B1A,Y at $6C15.
High-score entry: which heading $6BFB prints from the table at $6B19: 0 side 1, 2 side 2 (set at $6BD5, $6BEA), plus 1 for a team entry ($6C08).
High-score entry: the side as a digit character, $31 or $32 ($6BD8, $6BED), passed in A to $BD32 through $BFD3 at $6CB6.

High-score entry: the side's result code from $BFF2 or $BFF3 (set by the check at $BBA0): below 3 one name, 3 and above two names (wizard and feline); odd also asks for ten characters of 'a few words'.
Column of the name field being typed ($6CBC stores X, $6CCE reads it back for $6D44 each frame).
Row of the name field being typed ($6CBF, read at $6CD1).
Length of the name field being typed, 3 or 10 ($6CC2, read at $6CD4 and passed to $6D44).

After each life: takes a Wizball from the current side ($B277,$BFD9: $B278 side 1, $B279 side 2). One side ($BFD8 = 1): returns while it has lives. Two sides: when both are at 0 the game ends; otherwise switches $BFD9 to the other side (EOR #3), and back again if that one has none left, so the sides take turns life by life. Game end ($6B5B): drops its return address, takes $B1CE into $AF7D (the reads after loading side 1's and side 2's state compare the same global, so the last side to play decides), clears the continue level $AF7E and the BOREWIZ flag $BB07, subtracts 2 ($AF7D = levels opened, the most the title's keys 0-5 may choose) and goes to $6B92.

End of a game: black background, screen off, installs the display list $B482 (pointer at $B4B0; colour bands $6DD5-$6E00), text screen, the font's polarity as the title uses it ($8C8D, $8CBE), and runs the check at $BBA0 through $BFD0. With no entry for either side ($BFF2 = $BFF3 = 0) it goes straight to the title at $8F61 (via $6B8F). Otherwise tune $2F, then the name entry $6BFB for side 1 if $BFF2 is set and for side 2 if $BFF3 is set, and back to the title at $8F75.

Name entry for one side ($6B21-$6B23 set by the caller): clears the screen ($8F41), heads it with the side's name ($6B19), prints 'what a mega display of fun !!! type your name' ($B633), blanks the name buffer $BFF4-$BFFD. Result below 3: one three-letter name at column 17, row 17 into $BFF4-$BFF6. Otherwise 'wizard' and 'feline' ($B680) and two names at columns 10 and 24, row 17, into $BFF4-$BFF6 and $BFF8-$BFFA. Odd result: 'and also a few words' ($B668) and ten characters at column 10, row 23 into $B6AA-$B6B3, the text shown under the top score ('sensi soft' as loaded). Ends by JMP $BFD3 ($BD32) with the side digit $6B22 in A.

Reads one name field: X column, Y row, A length (3 or 10), kept in $6B24-$6B26. Once a frame (after $6EA8) it cycles the band colours ($9436), takes a key ($6D07) and redraws the field ($6D44), until RETURN (key $3F) with at least one character typed; then fills the buffer from the cursor to 10 with spaces.
Scans the keyboard once ($73D4, which updates the last-key memory $B255 and leaves $B254 at 0 unless a new key is down), fills the name buffer $6D76-$6D7F with $30 and puts the cursor $6D73 at 0.

Scans the keyboard ($73D4) and applies the new key $B254 through the table at $6D94: DEL ($14) moves the cursor back and puts $30 there; space, $21 (the 1 key) and the letters $41-$5A are stored at the cursor, which advances until it reaches the field length $6D72 (a further key overwrites the byte after the field, which $6D44 then sets to $FF). Anything else is ignored.

Draws the name field at column X, row Y with length A: stores the position in both records ($6D74/$6D75 and $6D82/$6D83), ends the text after A characters with $FF $FF, prints the blank record at $6D82 and then the name record at $6D74 in the large font in colour 0 ($8CF4).
Length of the field being edited (3 or 10), set by $6D50; $6D2A stops the cursor there.
Cursor in the name buffer, the number of characters typed (0 to the length); $6CDA needs it non-zero for RETURN.
Text record of the name field: this byte is its column (X at $6D44), then the row at $6D75, the ten characters $6D76-$6D7F and the terminators $6D44 writes after them; pointer at $6D90.
Row byte of the name record at $6D74 ($6D47), and the base the name copies use as $6D75,Y with Y from 1 ($6C4B, $6C6D, $6C84, $6CAD, $6CFD), so that Y = 1 is the first character.

First character of the ten-character name buffer $6D76-$6D7F (stored at $6D27, $6D40, filled at $6CEF, ended at $6D56). As loaded it holds CC 1F 02 90 14 CC 20 02 B0 0F A9 01 to $6D81, the same bytes as the instructions at $6FC8-$6FD3: leftovers, overwritten before use.

Second character of the name buffer, named because $6D59 writes the second $FF terminator as $6D77,Y; its span covers the rest of the buffer to $6D7F and $6D80-$6D81, where the terminators of a ten-character field land.
Blanking record for the name field: column here, row at $6D83 (both set by $6D44), ten spaces $6D84-$6D8D and $FF $FF; printed before the name so a deleted character disappears.
Row byte of the blanking record at $6D82 ($6D4D), followed by its ten spaces and $FF $FF ($6D84-$6D8F).
Pointer to the name record $6D74 (low byte), loaded into X at $6D67 for the printer.
High byte ($6D) of the name record pointer at $6D90, loaded into Y at $6D6A.
Pointer to the blanking record $6D82 (low byte), loaded into X at $6D5C.
High byte ($6D) of the blanking record pointer at $6D92, loaded into Y at $6D5F.

Keyboard table, 65 bytes, indexed by the key number $73D4 leaves in $B254 (64 minus the key's matrix row x 8 + column; 0 no key): 1 RUN/STOP $03, 2 Q, 4 space, 5 '2', 7 left arrow, 8 '1' as $21, 9 '/', ..., 58-61 F5 F3 F1 F7 ($87 $86 $85 $88), 62 CRSR right $1D, 63 RETURN $0D, 64 DEL $14; $00 for the shift, C= and CTRL keys. Read at $6D0D by the name entry; decoding the title's keys with it gives 'BOREWIZ' for the cheat table at $AFCE and 0-5 for the continue keys at $AF7F.

High-score entry screen (display list $B482, installed at $6BA4), band from raster line $2C: background $D021 = $EBD2, the front of the three-colour ring $EBD2-$EBD5 that $9916 shifts every third frame (one of the colour cycles $9436 runs each frame while a name is typed).
High-score entry screen band from line $4E: background = $EBF1, which $997D sets every fourth frame from the eight colours at $B5DF.

High-score entry screen band from line $8E: calls $973B twice with Y = $90, which sets the background every second line from $91 to $9F to $EBE4-$EBE7, twice over (the ring $EBE4-$EBF0 that $98E9 shifts every third frame).
High-score entry screen band from line $A6: background = $EBD6, set by $996A from the four colours at $B5F3.
High-score entry screen band from line $B6: background = $EBE4, the front of $98E9's ring.
High-score entry screen band from line $CF: background = $EBD1, which $994A sets every seventh frame from the four colours at $B5EF.

High-score entry screen band from line $E6: calls $9401 twice with Y = $E8, which steps the background every second line through $EBDA down to $EBD7 (the ring $98BE shifts) and ends each call with colour 6 (blue).
Saves the per-side block $B116-$B12D (24 bytes) as side 1's state at $E3C0-$E3D7.
Saves the per-side block $B116-$B12D as side 2's state at $E3D8-$E3EF.
Loads side 1's saved state $E3C0-$E3D7 into the per-side block $B116-$B12D.
Loads side 2's saved state $E3D8-$E3EF into the per-side block $B116-$B12D.
Saves the per-side block for the current side $BFD9 (1: $6E08, 2: $6E14), after each life.
Start of each life: resets the Wizball's variables $B20D-$B26C, the sprite table and the death flags $B1CF/$B1D0 ($7CDA), then loads the current side's saved block (1: $6E20, 2: $6E2C).

Re-applies the side's permanent Wiz-lab features at the start of a life: waits for raster line $23, sets $B074 (non-zero: $72DF skips the activation sound and the band at $89D4 uses sprite multicolour 2) and activates each icon number in $B11E down to $B116 through $72DF, then clears $B074.
Waits until the raster is between lines $CD and $FE (205-254, bit 8 clear): the pace of the colour-completed loop and the pause loop, and of the title loops ($8FEE).
Waits until the raster is between lines 200 and 255 ($C8-$FF with bit 8 clear): the first synchronisation point of the frame loop ($640E) and the bonus loop ($6576).
Waits for raster line 266 exactly (bit 8 set, $D012 = $0A), then moves the stars ($747E); X is kept. Used as the frame wait of the game-over loop, by $678A and by many routines from $82E1 on.

Waits until the raster is between lines 256 and 275 (bit 8 set, $D012 below $14), below the visible screen; used before screen switches ($7CB4, $8C44, $8C50) and as the frame wait of the get-ready and name-entry loops.

Pause: returns unless the play-key scan left RUN/STOP ($B254 = 1; a test for Q, 2, at $6EBE branches to the RTS either way). Paused, it loops on the raster wait $6E71 and the play-key scan $7429, several passes in each frame's lines 205-254 (about seven, measured live): RUN/STOP again resumes, Q ($6ED7) clears the continue level $AF7E and the BOREWIZ flag $BB07, drops one return address and jumps to the title $8F61. The CMP #5 at $6ECC is overwritten by the CMP #2 after it. Live: RUN/STOP stopped the frame loop, and Q then reached the title.

41 bytes of code that no traced instruction reaches: if level $B128's count $B11F,X is not yet 3 it sets it to 3, clears the key $B254, takes the level's colours from $B1D1 into $B27D/$B27E and jumps to $ADEF, which recomputes $B1CE and, with the count at 3, runs the level-completed sequence ($AE11). Its BEQ at $6EEC targets the RTS at $6EC2, inside $6EB7, whose test for Q at $6EBE branches nowhere ($D0 $00): apparently a developer key that completed the level, disconnected.

Moves and draws the character-mode shots, once a frame: six 12-byte slots at $0480-$04C7 (0-1 the Wizball's fire from $8467, 2 the cat's from $881F, 3-5 the spray from $8505), each handled by $6F21 while its character $0484,X is non-zero. Slot layout: +0 column, +1 row, +2/+3 step, +4 character (0 free), +5 colour, +6 saved screen character, +7/+8 screen address high/low, +9 colour RAM high, +10 second character of a two-cell shot (0 none), +11 its saved character. $7090 restores the saved characters before the landscape moves.

Moves shot X with the landscape's character steps (column - 1 when $B1FF is positive, + 1 when negative), then by its step; frees the slot off screen (column 39 or more, row 20 or more). Tests the aliens ($6FAE), finds the screen row (table $0500/$0519 with row + 3, screen $E000 or $E400 from $B1FD, colour RAM to match), and if the cell holds a character of $80 or more (apparently scenery) frees the slot; otherwise saves the character and draws the shot and its colour. A second cell is drawn the same way, and dropped if it meets scenery.
Converts shot X's cell to pixel coordinates (y = row x 8 + $4B in Y, x = column x 4 + $0C in A) and falls into the alien test at $6FBE.

Tests the point A (x), Y (y) against the boxes of the six aliens, $021D-$0220 (left, right, top, bottom) and every $2A bytes on, to $02EF-$02F2 in $706D. On a hit: sets that alien's hit byte ($0225 + $2A x n) to 1, frees slot X ($0484,X = 0), sets Y to the alien's offset and returns past its caller (PLA PLA RTS). Other callers ($7E98, $8613, $88FA) pass X = $48, a spare slot at $04C8-$04D3.

Erases the Wizball's bullets before they move: for each of the six 12-byte bullet records at $0480-$04C7 (X = $3C down to 0) whose +4 byte (the bullet's character; 0 = free slot) is non-zero, calls erase_bullet to put back what the bullet covered. Once a frame from the frame loop ($642A) and from $64B6, $6584, $6A6C; $6F0D then moves and redraws the bullets. Record: +0 column, +1 row, +2/+3 column and row step, +4 character, +5 colour, +6 character saved under it, +7 screen address high, +8 screen and colour address low, +9 colour RAM high, +10 non-zero when two cells wide, +11 character saved under the second cell.

Erases one bullet (X = its record offset in $0480-$04C7): writes the saved character (+6) back at column +0 of the screen row at +7/+8 and the landscape colour from $894D (the level's character colour $B27F, or 8 while $8959 is set) at the colour RAM row +9/+8; when +10 is non-zero it also restores the next cell from +11. Uses $60/$61 (screen) and $62/$63 (colour RAM) as pointers.

New game ($6395, once before the first turn): clears both players' score digits $BFDA-$BFE7 (player one $BFDA-$BFE0, player two $BFE1-$BFE7: an overflow digit and six digits each) and copies the six PETSCII digits of the first high-score table row ($BFEB-$BFF0, after "1. " at $BFE8) into hiscore_digits ($71D4-$71D9) as values 0-9.

Draws the score line at the top of the landscape screen $E000: colour RAM rows 0-1 ($D800-$D84F) light blue ($0E), clears hiscore_beaten, calls add_score with 0 points so both scores and the high score are printed on row 1, then prints the 40-byte header from $71E2 on row 0 ($E000-$E027, AND #$3F): "1UP" at columns 0-2, "HI" at 19-20, "2UP" at 37-39. Called from the outer cycle ($63A9) and on leaving the Wiz-lab ($B070).

Adds A x 10 points to the current player's score ($BFD9 = 1 or 2; X preserved in $66) and reprints the scores. A score is six decimal digits, one per byte, most significant first: $BFDB-$BFE0 for player one, $BFE2-$BFE7 for player two, each after an overflow digit; tbl_player_score_offset gives their offset from $BFD4 (7 or 14). A is split by repeated subtraction: hundreds go to the thousands digit, tens to the hundreds, the rest to the tens; the units digit is never added to, so scores end in 0. Carries run up six places; an overflow sets all six digits to 9, so the score stops at 999,999. An equal or higher score than hiscore_digits is copied there and sets hiscore_beaten. Prints player one's score at columns 0-5 and player two's at 34-39 of row 1 of $E000, and the high score at 17-22 unless $AC4E is set. If the hundred-thousands digit changed, the player gets an extra life (INC $B277 + player), sound $11 and draw_lives: an extra Wizball every 100,000 points. Callers pass 0 ($70FA), 1 ($AEB0), 4 ($66AC), 5 ($88F2), 10 ($7E90, a pearl), 100 ($9F51, $ADC2), $66 ($AD94) and $0216,X ($A894, $A8DF, $A944).
overflow digit set: saturate at 999999
hundred-thousands digit unchanged: no extra life
The byte before hiscore_digits: reset_scores writes through $71D3,Y and add_score prints from it with Y = 6 down to 1, so this byte ($00) itself is never read or written.

The high score shown in the middle of the score line: six digits 0-9, most significant first, $71D4-$71D9. Loaded from the high-score table by reset_scores, compared by add_score at $716C and replaced there ($7184) when the current player reaches it, printed at $71A9.

Two things in one: $71D9 is the last high-score digit (0, since scores end in 0, unless a score saturated at 999,999), and it is the base of a table indexed by the player number (1 or 2, $BFD9): $71DA = 7 and $71DB = 14, the offsets from $BFD4 of player one's and player two's score digits. Read at $7110, $7164, $717C and $71B8.

Player two's score-digit offset (14, the second entry of tbl_player_score_offset) and the base of a table indexed by the player number: $71DC = 0 and $71DD = 34, the first column of each player's score on rows 0-1, which $67C3 colours in the player's flashing colour.

Player two's score column (34, see tbl_player_score_column) and the base of a table indexed by the player number: $71DE = 9 and $71DF = 29, the column on row 1 of each player's two-digit counter (the value $B1AF, printed at $9F06 and coloured at $67EA).

Player two's counter column (29, see tbl_player_counter_column) and the base of a table indexed by the player number: $71E0 = 7 and $71E1 = 32, the column on row 1 of each player's spare-lives digit, used by draw_lives ($7D6A) and coloured at $67FE.

Player two's lives column (32, a space byte doubling as the second entry of tbl_player_lives_column) and the base of the score-line header, $71E2-$7209, 40 bytes that draw_score_line prints on row 0 of $E000 after AND #$3F: "1UP" at columns 0-2, "HI" at 19-20, "2UP" at 37-39, spaces between. Bytes $3A, $3B, $3C, $3D stand for H, I, U, P in the game's character set, so the stored text reads "1<=", ":;", "2<=" in PETSCII.

Non-zero (6) once the current player's score has reached the high score: set by add_score ($718D), cleared by draw_score_line ($70F6); while it is set $67D7 colours the HI label and high score in the player's flashing colour too.

Start of the play routine ($63E0), once a turn: sets the eight sprite pointers of the icon bar, $EFF8-$EFFF (the screen at $EC00 that the icon band shows), from $B4DE-$B4E5: shapes 7, $0B, 2, 6, 8, 1, 0 for icons 1-7 and 0 for sprite 7; clears the weapon flags $B231-$B239; sets the beam's two sprite shapes $B8DE/$B8DF to 5 and clears shape 5 ($C140-$C17F) through $8F15 (A = 0, X = 1 shape, Y = 5), so the beam shows nothing.
The stick direction detect_wiggle waits for next, as a joystick bit mask: 4 (left) or 8 (right), flipped with EOR #$0C each time it is seen. 4 in the loaded image; nothing resets it between lives.
Frames since the last direction reversal of the wiggle: cleared by detect_wiggle on a reversal; at 10 detect_wiggle clears it and wiggle_count.
Direction reversals in the current wiggle: detect_wiggle adds one per reversal and clears it after 10 frames without one; update_icons takes the lit icon when it is exactly 4 ($72D2).

Counts the left-right wiggle that takes a feature, once a frame from update_wizball ($7E1E): tests the Wiz's stick $B23F (active low) for the direction in wiggle_expect; if that bit is low it flips the expected direction, clears wiggle_idle and adds one to wiggle_count. Otherwise wiggle_idle counts frames, and at 10 (a fifth of a second at 50 frames a second) both counters go back to 0. So every push the opposite way from the last one counts, as long as less than 10 frames pass between pushes.

Colours the icon bar, from the icon band ($89FC, once a frame) and $9686: the seven icon sprite colours $B4D6-$B4DC light blue ($0E), or light red ($0A) while $B074 is set (the Wiz-lab), then the lit icon ($B258, 1-7; none when 0) gets a flashing colour: $B25A counts frames, every fourth frame $B25B steps 0-5, and the colour is $B53D + step (black, blue, light blue, light grey, light blue, blue) or in the lab $B543 + step (black, red, light red, light grey, light red, red).

Once a frame (frame loop $6436; $64E8, $65B3): if pearls are waiting ($B259, added by check_wizball_hits), takes one and lights the next icon ($B258 steps 1-7, 7 wraps to 1) with sound 9. Otherwise, when wiggle_count is exactly 4, takes the lit icon through take_lit_icon. Two leftovers do nothing: a test of key code 4 at $72B5 whose BNE and BEQ both go to $72D2, and LDA $B254 / CMP #3 before the RTS at $72D9, whose flags no caller uses.
dead test: both branches go to $72D2
leftover: flags returned but unused

Takes the feature of the lit icon $B258 (1-7). Returns at once when none is lit or the icon's sprite pointer ($EFF7 + icon) is 9, the used-up shape. Plays sound 8 (sound $0D for the smart bomb, icon 6) unless $B074 is set (the Wiz-lab, and $6E4F applying the permanent weapons at the start of a turn), puts the light out ($B258 = 0) and jumps through the word table $B549, indexed by the icon number, by writing the address into the JMP at $7316: 1 $7379, 2 $734B, 3 $7366, 4 $731A, 5 $7325, 6 $7394, 7 $73B0 (entry 0 is $7319 and is never used). Callers: update_icons ($72D7), $6E63, $B00C and $B0DE.

Two things in one: this LDY #0 is part of take_lit_icon's dispatch (the STA/STY $B258 put the icon out, A x 2 indexes $B549, the handler address goes into the JMP operand), and $7300 is the base of the 256 bytes $7300-$73FF that random ($7533) reads as its table with LDA $7300,Y: the machine code of this dispatch, the icon handlers and the start of the keyboard scanners serves as a fixed list of pseudo-random bytes.
Low byte of the JMP operand at $7316, written by take_lit_icon ($730D) from the icon jump table $B549; $00 in the loaded image.
High byte of the JMP operand at $7316, written by take_lit_icon ($7313) from $B54A: with icon_jump_lo, the address of the handler of the icon being taken.

A lone RTS byte ($60) that entry 0 of the icon jump table $B549 points at, a handler for no icon. take_lit_icon returns before the jump when no icon is lit, and nothing else jumps here, so it is left as data.
Icon 4, blazers: sets $B236 (read when bullets are fired, $84E3 for Wiz and $888D for the cat) and turns the icon into the used-up shape 9 ($EFFB).

Icon 5, spray. The first take sets $B237 (spray on, tested at $84FF) with the spray on Wiz ($B238 = 0) and shows shape $0A on the icon; every later take flips $B238 between Wiz (0) and the cat (1; the cat's spray is at $855E) and shows shape $0A or 8, the other one's spray. The icon never runs out, and Wiz and the cat never both have a spray. Remember's crack swaps the two images (8 and $0A) in its copy of this handler, so its icon shows who holds the spray; here, as for every icon, it shows what the next take gives.

Icon 2. The first take sets $B235, the beam (animated by $8592), and shows shape 4 on the icon; the second sets $B233, double fire (each shot alternates direction at $84B6), and turns the icon into the used-up shape 9. $B235 is not cleared, so the beam flag stays set with double.

Icon 3, catelite: sets $B234 (the cat is present: read at $69DA, $8640, $881F), turns the icon into the used-up shape 9 ($EFFA) and clears $B26C and $861A, two bytes of the cat's state that $806F and $805A also clear when a Wizball materialises.

Icon 1. The first take sets thrust ($B231: update_wizball then applies the stick's spin every frame through $818E, where without it the spin only changes the speed at a bounce) and shows shape 3 on the icon; the second sets anti-grav ($B232: bounce_wizball hands vertical motion to $8BEA) and turns the icon into the used-up shape 9. $64C4 and $64C7 call it twice to give both.

Icon 6, smart bomb: $B25C = 1 starts the background flash (the band at $8A44 then counts it up, writing each value to $D021, for 127 frames until it reaches $80), sets the hit flag +$25 of all six objects at $0200-$02FB (records of $2A bytes; X steps $2A up to $FC), then calls $9AD6 and $9CCB (which clears $0300-$03FF). The icon is not used up: it can be lit and taken again.

Icon 7, shields: shield_time = 40 and the cat's copy $89B6 = 40, clears shield_frames and shield_warned and the cat's $89B7 and $89B9, sets shield_flicker and the cat's $89B8 to $34, and shows the used-up shape 9 on the icon; update_shield gives the icon back (shape 0) when the shield runs out.

Full keyboard and joystick scan, for name entry ($6CF6, $6D07) and the title and menu loops ($9006, $90A2, $94C4). First, with both CIA 1 data-direction registers set to input so no keyboard row is driven, reads $DC00 into $B256 (joystick port 2) and $DC01 into $B257 (port 1): bits 0-4 up, down, left, right, fire, active low. Then restores DDRA = $FF and DDRB = 0 and scans all 64 keys, rows 7 down to 0 ($DC00 = $7F, $BF ... $FE) and in each row columns 7 down to 0, numbering them 1-64 in that order: 1 RUN/STOP, 2 Q, 3 C=, 4 SPACE, 9 /, 10 up-arrow, 11 =, 63 RETURN, 64 DEL (the game's own tables agree: key to PETSCII at $6D94, BOREWIZ at $AFCE). The highest-numbered key held is kept in $B255 and reported in $B254 only when it differs from the last scan, else $B254 = 0, so each press is seen once. Uses $5E (key found), $5F (rows left), $66 (row mask).

The key scan used in play and on the get-ready and pause screens (frame loop $644A; $65C9, $695B, $6A97, $6EC6, $9420): the same joystick latch into $B256 (port 2) and $B257 (port 1) as scan_keyboard, then only rows 7, 6, 5 and in each only columns 7, 6, 5, numbered 1-9: 1 RUN/STOP, 2 Q, 3 C=, 4 /, 5 up-arrow, 6 =, 7 comma, 8 @, 9 colon. Columns 7-5 are $DC01 bits that a joystick in port 1 cannot pull low, so the port-1 stick never reads as a key. $B254 gets the code when it changes, as in scan_keyboard. Users: $6EB7 (RUN/STOP pauses; while paused RUN/STOP resumes and Q quits) and $BA82 (up-arrow raises and = lowers the firing volume, $BA81 0-15).

Moves the five sky stars, once a frame in play (frame loop $6447; $64D5, $65A5, $6EA2, $AB84, $AEAB): for star n = 0-4 (X = 5n into the records at $B1B4) calls move_star with ($60) = $F80A + 144n, the star's strip of 18 sky glyphs (8 bytes each) in the landscape character set at $F800.

Moves one star, record X at $B1B4 (+0 byte offset in its strip 0-$8F, +1 position 0-$7F within the glyph, +2 layer $00/$08/$10/$18, +3 frame counter, +4 twinkle phase): erases its byte, then moves it against the scroll velocity $B1F4 by $B8A1 + layer + |velocity| (four layers, 1 to 4 times as fast; velocity 1-6 gives 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16 in the slowest), stepping 8 bytes to the next glyph (wrapping within the strip) when the position crosses 7 bits. Every fourth frame it picks a random twinkle phase 0, 4, 8 or 12; the pattern $B891 + phase + (bits 6-5 of the position) sets one multicolour pixel in $D023, $D022, nothing or the character colour.

The state of random: an index into rng_table ($7300-$73FF), incremented before each use, one byte wrapping at 256. 0 in the loaded image; the initialisation calls random 98 times ($EC93) while it overwrites itself.

Returns a pseudo-random byte in A (Y = the new index; flags from A): increments rng_index and exclusive-ORs the byte at $7300 + index, the game's own code used as a 256-byte table, with the low byte of CIA 2 timer B ($DD06). The initialisation sets timer B's latch to $FFFF and starts it counting every cycle ($EC43-$EC67), so that byte is the cycle count modulo 256 at the moment of the call: the result depends on exactly when the game calls, which varies with everything the player does. 28 callers, among them the stars, sound effect $18 ($455B), the explosion debris, the aliens and the start position.
CIA 2 timer B low byte, free-running

Before each turn ($63DA): clears the 90 sky glyphs at $F808-$FAD7 (glyphs 1-90 of the landscape set at $F800, five strips of 18) and $0480-$04FF (the bullet records and what follows), then puts one fixed dot in each strip: a random single-pixel pattern from $B891-$B898 at a random offset 0-127 from $F808 + 144n.

Picks where the view starts for a new turn (from start_landscape): from the level's record at $B2F0 + 4 x level ($B128: start block column, block row, column within the block, 0) it takes that block row of the map (pointers $0460/$0470) from 6 blocks right of the start column, and from a random block 0-31 searches right up to block 36 (then left down to 0, and round again) for two consecutive empty blocks (number 0); the view column $B1F1 = 5 x (index of the second) + 2. The search has no exit if no such pair exists.

How many block columns draw_landscape draws before its map source jumps 4 block rows down and 4 block columns back, so one screen is made of two parts of the map: $FF from start_landscape (never within 8 blocks), 5 from $AB25 and $AF2A, $38 from $AE16. Counted down at $7697.
Starts a turn's landscape (JMP from $63DD at the end of $63CA; JSR from $6522 and $8267): choose_start_column, draw_jump_blocks = $FF, then draw_landscape with A = 1 (full level set-up).

Draws a whole landscape screen into a hidden buffer and shows it. A = 1 also sets up the level's graphics and colours (setup_level_graphics), 0 only copies the glyphs and applies the colours; A is kept in $AB9C. If the band shows screen 0 ($B1FD = 0) it draws into screen 1 ($E400), else into screen 0 ($E000), with $B1FE the target, and resets the roles $B203-$B205 and build counters $B200-$B202 to match. The map position $B209-$B20C is the level's record at $B2F0 plus the view column $B1F1 in blocks of 5 columns. For each of 40 columns it fetches the map column (fetch_left_column; a blank one while $B874 is set), fills in the sky (sky_fill_next) and writes it to rows 3-22 (put_column); draw_jump_blocks can move the source mid-screen. After the raster passes line $C8 ($6E83) it shows the new screen and builds the other two with eight calls of build_scroll_buffer.

Sprite-row masks for draw_level_digit_sprite, 8 entries of 3 bytes ($76E9-$7700): entry n, for bit n of a glyph row (bit 0 at the right), sets 3 adjacent pixels of a 24-pixel sprite row: 00 00 07, 00 00 38, 00 01 C0, 00 0E 00, 00 70 00, 03 80 00, 1C 00 00, E0 00 00. $76E9 is the left byte of each entry, read as $76E9,Y with Y = 3n.
The middle byte of each 3-byte entry of tbl_wide_pixel, read by draw_level_digit_sprite as $76EA,Y (Y = 3n); this label owns the one byte of entry 0.
The right byte of each 3-byte entry of tbl_wide_pixel, read as $76EB,Y (Y = 3n); this label's span runs to $7700 and so holds entries 1-7 of the table.

One byte per level (9 entries, $7701-$7709, index $B128): 0, $0C, $14 in turn, the start in the colour table $B5CB of the level-number sprite's flashing; draw_level_digit_sprite copies it to digit_flash_offset.
Frame counter for the level-number sprite's flashing, incremented by the cauldron band at $8B9A; every second frame it advances digit_flash_step.

Step of the level-number sprite's colour cycle, advanced every second frame at $8BA4; the band takes it AND 7, adds digit_flash_offset and stores the colour from $B5CB + that in $B515, sprite 0's colour in the cauldron band.
Offset (0, $0C or $14) of the level-number sprite's colour cycle within $B5CB, set per level by draw_level_digit_sprite from tbl_digit_flash_offset and added at $8BAD.

Draws the level number into sprite shape $A0 at $E800 (cleared just before by setup_level_graphics): the digit is glyph $31 + level ($B128) of the character set at $F000, read from $F188 + 8 x level; each of its first 7 rows is widened three times through tbl_wide_pixel and written to two sprite rows, a 24 x 14-pixel digit. The cauldron band shows it as sprite 0 (pointer $B51D = $A0). Also sets digit_flash_offset from tbl_digit_flash_offset.

Sets up a level's graphics (from draw_landscape with A = 1; $9E09, $AE27): copies its glyphs to $FD00 (copy_level_glyphs), clears sprite shape $A0 and draws the level digit in it (draw_level_digit_sprite), clears $9EC9, copies the target cauldron's shape $CE00-$CE3F to shape $BC at $EF00-$EF3F, then sets the landscape colours: the greys $B27D = $0B, $B27E = $0C, $B27F = 9, of which the first $B11F + level are replaced by the level's own colours from $B1D1 + 4 x level (the colours already restored), while the next byte of that record, the colour to mix now, goes to $B51A, the target cauldron's sprite colour. $B27F gets bit 3 (multicolour) and set_landscape_colours applies them.

Copies the level's 760 bytes of landscape glyphs to $FD00-$FFF7, glyphs $A0-$FE of the character set at $F800, stopping short of glyph $FF so the processor vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF survive. The source is the word at $B31C + 2 x level ($B128), $1142 for the first level.

Builds a quarter of a scroll buffer, once a frame (frame loop $6439; eight times at $76E1; $AEA5). The landscape band shows one of three screens, $E000, $E400 or $E800 ($B1FD = 0, $10, $20); each has a role in $B203-$B205 (0 shown, 1 ready for a one-column step left, 2 for a step right) and a build counter 0-4 in $B200-$B202. This picks the first unfinished one (screen 2, 1, 0), counts it up and copies the next of four chunks of rows 3-22 of the shown screen into it, shifted one column (right for role 1, left for role 2): 226 bytes a chunk, 126 the last, through the self-modified loop at $787A. After the fourth chunk it draws the new edge column from the map: column 0 for role 1 (fetch_left_column, sky_fill_previous, put_column_left), column 39 for role 2 (fetch_right_column, sky_fill_right, put_column_right). $64 = the screen, $65 = its role, $61 = the chunk's byte count.
Low byte of the source operand of the LDA at $787A in build_scroll_buffer's copy loop: $B332 + chunk ($78, $59, $3A, $1B), minus 1 for a role-1 screen.
High byte of the LDA $787A source: the shown screen's page ($B33A + shown screen: $E0, $E4, $E8) plus the chunk's page ($B336 + chunk, 0-3).
Low byte of the destination operand of the STA at $787D: $B332 + chunk, minus 1 for a role-2 screen.
High byte of the STA $787D destination: the target screen's page ($B33A + screen) plus the chunk's page.
Low byte of the source of the second LDA, at $7880: the first source plus the chunk's count ($71, or $3F for the last chunk), so each pass of the loop moves two bytes that far apart.
High byte of the LDA $7880 source, the first source's page with the carry from shift_src2_lo.
Low byte of the destination of the second STA, at $7883: the first destination plus the chunk's count.

High byte of the STA $7883 destination, with the carry from shift_dst2_lo. After it the loop counts Y down to 1, and after the fourth chunk (counter pulled back as 3) build_scroll_buffer draws the new edge column: $7895-$789D for role 1, $78A2-$78AA for role 2.

Fetches, for a new right-hand edge, the map column 8 blocks and one column to the right of the view's map position ($B209 + 8 block columns, $B20B + 1 columns, carried into the next block at 5) into the column buffer $E79A-$E7AD, through the code of fetch_left_column from $78DE.

Fetches the map column at the view's map position ($B209 block column, $B20A block row, $B20B column 0-4 within the block) into the 20-byte column buffer $E79A-$E7AD: for 4 block rows it reads the block number from the map row at $0460/$0470 + row, and copies that column's 5 characters from the block graphics at ($B62B) + 25 x block + column (blocks are 5 x 5 characters, rows 5 bytes apart). Used for every column by draw_landscape and for a new left-hand edge by build_scroll_buffer.

Steps the sky glyph number $B27A up by one ($5B wraps to $49), then (from $79C2) gives every empty cell (0) of the column buffer a sky glyph: in each block row the bottom character row gets the row's glyph and each row above 18 less, the four block rows starting at $B27A plus 0, 7, 16 and 11 (wrapped into $49-$5A). So the empty sky is made of the 90 star glyphs 1-90 of the $F800 set. Used for every column by draw_landscape.
Steps the sky glyph number $B27A down by one ($48 wraps to $5A) and fills the column buffer's empty cells with sky glyphs as sky_fill_next does; for a new left-hand column.

For a new right-hand column: steps $B27A up by one (wrapping at $5B), keeps that in $B27B, fills the column buffer's empty cells with the sky glyphs one number further on, then puts the kept value back in $B27A.
Writes the column buffer into column 39 of screen A (0-2) through put_column.
Writes the column buffer into column 0 of screen A (0-2) through put_column.

Writes the 20-character column buffer $E79A-$E7AD into column A of screen X (0-2: $E000, $E400, $E800 from $B33A), rows 3-22: sets the operands of the four STAs in the loop at $7A75 to the column's address in rows 3, 8, 13 and 18, one per block row, then copies 5 rows of each, 40 bytes apart.

Low byte of the operand of the STA at $7A78, the column's address in row 3, written by put_column through $7A79,X; the operands of the other three STAs, $7A7F, $7A85 and $7A8B, are written the same way 6 bytes apart.

High byte of the STA $7A78 operand (and, through $7A7A,X, of the STAs at $7A7E, $7A84, $7A8A). From here the loop copies the four block rows of the column buffer 5 rows down, 40 bytes a row, and returns.

Scrolls the landscape, once a frame (frame loop $642D; $63F2, $AEA2). Advances the scroll position $B1F2/$B1F3 by the velocity (advance_scroll_position) and keeps the frame's pixel step in $B1FB. When the fine scroll (low 3 bits) passes 7 or 0 it moves the column counter $B1F1 and, while that stays below $BB (the scrolling part of the level) and $B25D is clear, steps the map position ($B209 blocks, $B20B columns 0-4) and swaps screens: the one ready for that direction becomes the shown one ($B1FD), the old shown one takes the opposite role, the stale third takes this direction's role with its build counter reset for build_scroll_buffer, and $B1FF = 2 (right) or $FF (left) makes the bullets shift a column ($6F21). From $BB up the view has reached an edge: the map stops, $B25D is set (it also blocks the first step back), and $B1F9, the Wizball's signed offset from the screen centre, becomes 8 x (count - $BB) + fine on the right, or -(8 x ($FF - count) + 7 - fine) on the left, where the count has gone below 0 ($DC and up). $B1FC gets the fine scroll for the band's $D016.
Returns in X (0-2) the first screen whose role in the copy $B206-$B208 equals A; the search has no limit.
Returns in A the step direction opposite to $60: 2 for 1, 1 for 2.

Adds the scroll velocity $B1F4 (-6 to +6) to the 8.8 fixed-point position $B1F2/$B1F3 and the same whole-pixel change to $63: 0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 1 1/2 or 2 pixels a frame, from the fraction and whole tables $B33D/$B344 (forward) and $B34B/$B351 (backward). Called by scroll_landscape and, while the screen is fixed, by slide_on_fixed_screen.

Converts a sprite position to the address of the character under it in the shown landscape screen: X = sprite x / 2, Y = sprite y; column = (x - 12 + fine / 2) / 4 with the fine scroll $B1FC, row = (y - 51) / 8; returns ($60) = the row's start from $0500/$0519 on the screen chosen by $B1FD, plus the column. Used for the Wizball ($8382) and for objects ($A69B).
Clears the first 256 bytes (rows 0-6) of each of the three landscape screens $E000, $E400 and $E800, before each turn ($63CA); on $E800 that includes sprite shape $A0, the level digit.

NMI handler (vector $FFFA). CIA 2 timer A calls it once a frame: the initialisation sets the latch to $4CC7 (19,656 cycles, one PAL frame) and starts it at raster line $1E, so it comes at the same raster position every frame; the RESTORE key also lands here. It saves A, reads $DD0D to acknowledge CIA 2, writes 0 to $85 and returns; eight NOPs pad it. $85 is a watchdog: band $8BBB sets it non-zero at raster line $F7 in play (the title bands $936A-$93C5 add to it through INC $FFB0,X, which wraps to $0085), and the checks at $8B04 and $9287, written in undocumented opcodes (LAX $86 / DCP $FF86,X, which wraps to $0085), pass only if this NMI has cleared it since; otherwise they unbalance the stack and the game crashes. Because those readers use undocumented opcodes and wrapped indexed addresses, a search of ordinary operands finds no reader of $85. RESTORE only brings the next clearing forward, so it does no harm.

Raster IRQ handler (vector $FFFE): runs one entry of the current display list per interrupt. Saves A, waits until $D019 bit 0 (raster) is set and acknowledges it, saves Y and X, then reads the entry at index $B1CD of the list at ($68): the band routine's address into the JSR operand at $7C9D, the raster line of the next interrupt into $D012; the index steps by 4, the routine is called and the registers restored. An entry whose next-line byte is 0 ends the list ($7CA6): the index goes back to 2, $D012 gets the list's first line (byte 0) and that last routine still runs, so the list repeats every frame. A list is: first raster line, 0, then entries of routine (low, high), next line, 0. Entered without the raster flag (a BRK), it loops back to the PHA and pushes A again on every pass.
no raster flag: loops back to the PHA
Low byte of the JSR operand at $7C9D, the current band routine, written by irq_handler ($7C87) from the display list.

High byte of the JSR operand at $7C9D, written at $7C8D. Then irq_handler's exit (X, Y and A restored, RTI) and, at $7CA6, the end of a list: index back to 2, $D012 = the list's first line, BNE back to $7C9D to run the last routine.
end of list: restart at entry 0, next IRQ at the first line

Switches the raster IRQ to the display list at X (low), Y (high): waits for raster lines $100-$113 ($6EA8), then with interrupts off stores the pointer in $68/$69, sets the index $B1CD to 2 (the first entry), $D012 to the list's first line with the compare's bit 8 cleared in $D011, acknowledges and enables the raster interrupt ($81 to $D019 and $D01A) and turns interrupts back on. Callers: $63B5 (the play list $B3E2), $68A3, $6BA4, $8F89, $9020, $9469.

At the start of each turn ($6E42): clears the 96 bytes $B20D-$B26C (the Wizball's position and motion, weapon flags, stick copies $B23E/$B23F, the port choice $B240, key and joystick bytes $B254-$B257, the lit icon and more) and the sprite copies $E7C4-$E7D4; puts the Wizball at y = $49 with the view column $B1F1 = $B4; stops the scroll ($B1F4 = 0); clears $B1CF and $B1D0 (death flag and death timer); turns sprite expansion and priority off; sets the sprite-enable copy $E7D9 = 3; calls $8C84 and $8CB5.

Applies the landscape colours: colour RAM rows 2-22 ($D850-$DB97) get the character colour $B27F (8 while $8959 is set), rows 23-24 black, border and background black, and $D022/$D023 get $B27D/$B27E (black while $8959 is set).

Prints the current player's spare lives on row 1 of $E000 at the column from tbl_player_lives_column (7 or 32): glyph $2F + lives ($B277 + player), lives capped at 10, so it shows lives - 1 as a digit up to 9 (0 lives would give glyph $2F).

Starts the Wizball's explosion (from start_death_sequence): fills the 16 records of 16 bytes at $0300-$03FF with the Wizball's character position (+0 column (x - 16) / 8, +1 row (y - 64) / 8), a random step -7 to +8 in each direction (+4, +5), +10 = 2 and +11 = 0.

The Wizball has just died (update_wizball, after setting the death timer $B1D0 = 200): calls $9AD6 and spawn_debris, stops the music ($B8F1 = 0) and the filter routing ($D417 = 0), plays sounds $15, $16 and $17, stops the scroll ($B1F4 = 0) and runs the first step of continue_death_sequence.

One frame of the death sequence: counts the death timer $B1D0 down, holding at 1 (which ends the frame loop at $6467, 199 frames after the death), calls $99BD unless $B874 is set, and clears sprite 0 (the Wizball) in the sprite-enable copy $E7D9.
Frame counter of update_wizball (and of $AAAB): when it wraps to 0, or whenever the sound slot byte $0422 is 0, sound $18 is started again.

The Wizball's work for one frame (frame loop $6430; $64E2, $6591, $65D2, $8306, $AC81, $ACB9): draw_lives; restarts sound $18 when $0422 is 0 or every 256 frames (hum_count); while the death timer $B1D0 runs, continue_death_sequence; when $B1CF has just been set, starts it with $B1D0 = 200. Otherwise detect_wiggle, and $8216 when $B213 is set; else set_wizball_x, bounce_wizball, $80F8, animate_materialise, $8097, $836E (unless $B216), the fire routines $8444 and $8467, $857B, the beam $8592, the horizontal control $818E when thrust ($B231) or $AC4E is set, check_wizball_hits, update_shield, the firing-volume keys ($BA82) and slide_on_fixed_screen.

Tests the point (Wizball x / 2, Wizball y + 11) against the six objects' boxes (test_wizball_point). On a hit, with Y = the object's offset in $0200: type ($0215 + Y) below 2 sets wizball_hit for update_shield; type 5, a pearl, is removed ($0202, $021F and $0220 cleared), adds one to the pearls waiting ($B259) and scores 100 (A = 10); other types are ignored.

Calls the box test at $6FBE with X = $48, a dummy bullet slot ($6FBE clears $0484 + X, here $04CC). On a hit $6FBE sets the object's hit flag (+$25), drops its own return address and returns to $7E75 in check_wizball_hits with Y = the object's offset; with no hit it returns here, and the PLA PLA drops check_wizball_hits's return address so that routine ends too.

Shields and collisions, once a frame from update_wizball. While shield_time is non-zero it goes down one every 50 frames (shield_frames); below 8, sound $12 plays once (shield_warned); below 5 the shield is off (0). While it is 0 the shield icon's sprite pointer $EFFE is kept at 0, so the icon can be taken again. Then a collision flagged in wizball_hit: with a shield it costs 8; without one the Wizball dies ($B1CF = 1) unless $BB07 is set (BOREWIZ, typed on the title at $AF85) and $B874 is clear.

The Wizball's shield in units of 50 frames: 40 from take_shield, -1 a second, -8 a collision, off below 5, so a shield lasts 36 seconds without collisions. Cleared by update_shield and at $AB14; nothing on the way from a quit to a new game clears it. Live: 40 to 38 in 100 frames; a collision cost 8 with no life lost; a shield running at a quit was still running in the next game.
Frames towards the next second of shield_time, 0-49, counted by update_shield.

Counter for the Wizball's flicker while shielded: $34 from take_shield, incremented at $80E8 each frame while shield_time is non-zero; when its bit 1 is set, $80F2 turns the Wizball's colour copy $E7EB (5, green) to black, two frames in four.
Non-zero once the running-out sound $12 has played for this shield; cleared by take_shield.

Set when something harmful touches the Wizball: by check_wizball_hits ($7E94, an object of type 0 or 1) and by $9B94 (a record of the $0300 table inside the Wizball's box). update_shield clears it and takes 8 from the shield or kills the Wizball; $806C also clears it when a Wizball materialises.

The end of update_wizball: while $B874 is set (the landscape does not scroll) the scroll velocity $B1F4 moves the Wizball across the screen instead: advance_scroll_position runs on $B1F2, which becomes the Wizball's offset $B1F9 (copied before the limit is applied) and is held between -121 ($87) and +83 ($53), the spin $B21C cleared at either limit. Does nothing while $B874 is 0.

Sets the Wizball's sprite x ($B20D, bit 8 in $B20E) to 172 + its signed offset $B1F9: 0 from the start of a turn ($63D2) while the landscape scrolls under it, set by scroll_landscape at the level's edges and by slide_on_fixed_screen on a fixed screen.

The Wizball's vertical motion. With anti-grav ($B232) or $AC4E set, jumps to $8BEA. Otherwise the y position $B20F.$B210 moves by the speed $B211.$B212 (8.8 fixed point) in the direction $B217 (1 down, 0 up); gravity $B27C (constant $10, 1/16 pixel per frame per frame) adds to the speed going down and takes from it going up. At y $C8 (200) the ball bounces: the direction flips with the speed kept and $818E turns its spin into the scroll velocity; at speed 0 going up it starts to fall.

The Wizball's materialising animation: while $B216 is 1 the frame $B214 counts down from $17 to 0 one step every 3 frames ($B215), while 2 it counts up to $17, then $B216 goes to 0; the sprite shape offset $B21A = frame + $10 and $E7DF = 1 while it runs, 0 otherwise. (Continues at $8000.)

Tail of the routine at $7FEA (the Wizball's appear and vanish animation, called every frame from $7E32), cut here by the $8000 edge; this label sits on the operand of CMP #$03 at $7FFF. The animation steps every third frame ($B215 counts to 3). Appearing ($B216 = 1, set by $8040 and $6539): $B214 counts down from 23, and when it passes 0 $B216 and $B21A are cleared. Vanishing ($B216 = 2, set at $6476): $B214 counts up, and at 23 $B216 is cleared. Otherwise the frame $B21A = $B214 + 16 (sprite shapes $20-$37 through $8097) and sprite 0 goes behind the scenery ($E7DF = 1, the shadow of $D01B).

Resets the Wizball before the frame loop (JSR at $63FE in the play routine): starts the appear animation ($B216 = 1, $B214 = 23), puts it on the ground at Y $C8 ($B20F, fraction $B210 = 0) with a bounce speed of 3 + $F0/256 pixels a frame ($B211/$B212), makes sprites 0 and 1 multicolour ($B1B2 = 3), and clears $A1B7, $A1B8, the mutant-cat flag $861A, $A133, $A9A7, freaky bits $8959, $AB9B, $B1CF, the Wizball-hit flag $7F0A and the cat's lost lives $B26C. Puts five random multiples of 8 ($7533 AND #$F8) in $A76D-$A771 (read at $A7C2 and $A7CF; purpose unknown). With anti-grav owned ($B232, re-granted as a permanent weapon by $6E4F just before) the Wizball starts at Y $49, the top limit, instead.
