Every frame from $7E35, and from $8236 while sinking into a tube: keeps the Wizball's Y $B20F within $49-$C8, setting the anti-grav vertical speed $B218 to +1 at the top limit and -1 at the bottom; copies X ($B20D, bit 8 in $B20E) and Y into the VIC register shadow for sprite 0 ($E7C4, bit 0 of $E7D4, $E7C5); sets sprite 0's colour to green (5 in $E7EB) and its shape to $B21A + $10 in $B525 (rotation frames $10-$1F, appear frames $20-$37, $B4 in a tube); writes 1 to $E7E0, the shadow's $D01C slot, which no traced code reads (band $8A52 takes $D01C from $B1B2). While the Wiz's shield runs ($7F06) the colour is black whenever bit 1 of the counter $7F08 is set, so the ball blinks. LDA #$F3 / TAY at $80CD is dead: Y is not used.
dead: Y is not used afterwards

Spin control, every frame from $7E2F, from the Wiz's joystick bits in $B23F (0 = pressed). Left (bit 2) lowers the spin $B21C by 6 to at most -48 ($D0); right (bit 3) raises it by 6 to at most +48. With neither pressed the spin decays by 1 a frame toward 0, but only when thrust $B231 and anti-grav $B232 are both owned or $AC4E is set; otherwise the ball keeps spinning. A non-zero spin is copied to $B21D, whose sign gives the direction of the Wiz's shots ($84AF) and the side the cat trails on ($8717). The angle $B21A.$B21B then advances by twice the spin (signed), and $B21A is kept to 0-15, the rotation frame.

Turns the spin $B21C into the horizontal speed $B1F4 (read at $74A7 and $7BCB): 0 when |spin| < 4, else ((|spin| - 4) >> 3) + 1 with the spin's sign, so -6 to +6. Does nothing while sinking into a tube ($B213). Called when the ball bounces on the ground ($7F95), after a bounce off scenery ($83E4), and every frame only with thrust $B231 or $AC4E ($7E54): without thrust the horizontal speed changes only when the ball touches something.

Enters a tube, jumped to from $83A6 with A holding the character found beside the tube mouth: $BE (the up arrow) raises the level $B128 by one unless it already equals $B1CE; anything else lowers it by one. Clears $A1B7/$A1B8, copies the Wizball's current frame (64 bytes from $C400 + 64 x $B21A) into sprite block $B4 ($ED00), sets the sinking counter $B213 to 21, stops rolling and spinning ($B1F4, $B1FF and $B21C = 0) and starts sound effect 3 through $4553.

One frame of sinking into a tube, run instead of the Wizball's movement while $B213 is non-zero (JMP from $7E26): moves the copied image in sprite block $B4 ($ED00) down one pixel row and clears its top row, sets $B21A = $A4 so that $8097 shows shape $B4, and jumps to $8097; band $8B22 meanwhile puts sprite 0 behind the scenery below the tube mouth. When $B213 reaches 0, after 21 frames, it goes on to $8239.

Arrives on a level out of a tube: after sinking ($822F), and called from $AE09 and $AF18. Puts the Wizball at X $AC, Y $4C with no speed ($B211, $B212, $B218, $B1F9 = 0), the cat at $B261 = 0, $B262 = $3C, $B1FC = $B1F2 AND 7, hides all sprites ($E7D9 = 0) and calls $A1C9, $75E0, $9ECF, $8C50 (screen on) and $9CCB, apparently to set up the new level. Then the tube animation, one step a frame ($6E92): sprites 1 and 2 (cyan, double height, X $D0 and $E8, Y $46, shapes $B5 and $B7 cleared by $8F15) lower the images of sprite blocks $3A/$3B (the tube's end, going by the shapes) one row a frame for 21 frames ($830A); the Wizball, drawn as sprite 3 (shape $10, green), rolls left one pixel a frame from X $D0 to $AC; the images drop 5 rows more, then rise out of the sprites in 21 frames ($8334). Ends with sprites 0 and 1 on ($E7D9 = 3), $B21A = 0 and a jump to the Wizball update at $7DF4.

One byte: a copy of $B874 stored every frame by the frame loop ($6417), which leaves for $646F, the bonus stage's setup, when $B874 is non-zero; $67EE reads this copy to blank two colour cells of the current player's score line while it is set.

Tube animation, moving down, for A frames (21, then 5, from $8239; count in $65). Each frame waits for the raster ($6E92), adds 3 to $BB02 and copies 64 bytes from $CE7F to $ED00 + $BB02 and from $CEBF to $ED80 + $BB02, so the images of sprite blocks $3A and $3B slide one pixel row a frame down through sprite blocks $B4-$B5 and $B6-$B7, of which sprites 1 and 2 show $B5 and $B7.

Tube animation, moving up, for A frames (21 from $8239; count in $65). Each frame waits for the raster ($6E92), subtracts 3 from $BB02 and moves the contents of sprite blocks $B5 ($ED40) and $B7 ($EDC0) up one pixel row (copying from three bytes on), then clears their last row ($ED7C-$ED7E, $EDFC-$EDFE).

The Wizball against the scenery, every frame from $7E3D unless it is appearing or vanishing ($B216); skipped while $B874 or $AC4E is set. $7C1D gives in $60/$61 the screen address of the character under the sprite's top-left corner, and the 3 x 3 characters from there are probed. If the bottom-middle one (offset $51) is a tube mouth ($C2, $C3, $C6 or $C7), the next three characters of that row are searched for the up arrow $BE and it jumps to $81C9. Otherwise the eight probes of $B3B6 (bottom, left, right, top, then the corners) are tried in turn; the first character of $98 or above (solid scenery) sets the freaky-bits flash $895A = 3 and selects a pair of bounce handlers from $B3BE (4 bytes a probe), whose addresses are written into the JSRs at $83D0 and $83E1 and called; then it jumps to $818E.
Low byte of the JSR at $83D0 (it assembles as JSR $0000), rewritten by $83C7 from $B3BE + 4n, n being the probe that hit: the first bounce handler of the pair.
High byte of the JSR at $83D0, rewritten by $83CD from $B3BF + 4n. After the call $83D3-$83DE fetch the second handler of the pair into the JSR at $83E1.
Low byte of the JSR at $83E1, rewritten by $83D8 from $B3C0 + 4n: the second bounce handler of the pair ($8404, an RTS, for the four edge probes).
High byte of the JSR at $83E1, rewritten by $83DE from $B3C1 + 4n. After the call $83E4 jumps to $818E to recompute the rolling speed.

Part of the floor bounce under anti-grav (from $8420): if the vertical speed $B218 is 0 or downward it is negated and the Wizball moved by the new speed ($B20F), that is back up. $83EC, the negate-and-move, is shared with $83FD.
Part of the ceiling bounce under anti-grav (from $840B): if the vertical speed $B218 is below 1 (upward or still) it is negated and the Wizball moved by the new speed through $83EC.
RTS: the do-nothing second handler of the four edge probes in $B3BE, and the exit of $8405 and $841A.

Bounce handler (table $B3BE) for scenery touching the Wizball's top (probes top, top-left, top-right). Under anti-grav ($B232 or $AC4E) an upward speed is reversed ($83FD). Under gravity, if the ball was rising ($B217 = 0) it starts falling ($B217 = 1) and gets one step of gravity at $7F99.

Bounce handler (table $B3BE) for scenery under the Wizball (probes bottom, bottom-left, bottom-right). Under anti-grav ($B232 or $AC4E) a downward speed is reversed ($83E7). Under gravity, if the ball was falling ($B217 = 1) it bounces: $B217 = 0 and the rising step at $7FD0.
Bounce handler (table $B3BE) for scenery to the right (probes right, bottom-right, top-right): a spin $B21C of 0 or more is negated, so the ball turns back; $8434 is the negate shared with $843E.
Bounce handler (table $B3BE) for scenery to the left (probes left, bottom-left, top-left): a negative spin $B21C is negated through $8434.

Fire as a single press, every frame from $7E40: $B23D = 1 only in the frame the fire bit of the Wiz's stick ($B23F bit 4, 0 = pressed) goes down after being up, 0 otherwise; $B23C keeps the previous fire bit. Holding fire does not repeat the Wiz's shots.

Fires the Wiz's shot when $B23D says fire was pressed (every frame from $7E43). First starts the beam animation ($B8DC = 1, $B8DB = 0) if it is idle, whether or not the beam is owned. The shot takes the first free of two slots of the shot table at $0480 (12 bytes a slot; slots at $0480 and $048C; in use while byte 4 is non-zero): column (X - $10)/8 and row (Y - $40)/8 of the Wizball in bytes 0-1, direction +1 or -1 in byte 2 from the sign of the last spin $B21D (with double, $B233, alternating each shot through $B23A), 0 in byte 3, character $B8D3[Y AND 7] ($79-$7B, by the ball's pixel row) in byte 4, colour 7 in byte 5, 0 in byte 10. With blazers ($B236) the character is 3 higher, the colour 12, and byte 10 holds the character. Plays sound 0 ($4553) and goes on to the spray at $84FF; with both slots busy it goes straight there.

Wiz spray: with the spray owned ($B237) and not given to the cat ($B238 = 0), falls into $850A to fire a fan of three from the Wizball's column and row in $60/$61. The LDA $84FF at $8558 reads this instruction's opcode byte $AD as if it were a flag.

Fires a spray fan from the column in $60 and row in $61, only when all three spray slots of the shot table are free ($0480 + $24, $30 and $3C; byte 4 = 0). $B23B alternates between 0 and 9 to pick one of two sets of three (dx, dy, character) from $B8C1: down-left, down and down-right (characters $77, $76, $78), or up-right, up and up-left. Each slot gets column, row, dx, dy, character, colour 11 and 0 in byte 10.

Cat spray, from $882C when the cat fires. Its test of the spray flag is LDA $84FF, the opcode byte $AD of the instruction there rather than $B237, so it always passes; then, with the spray given to the cat ($B238), it fires the fan of $850A from the cat's column ($B261 - $0C)/4 and row ($B262 - $40)/8.
reads the opcode $AD at $84FF, not $B237: always non-zero

Every frame from $7E46: stores the Wizball's Y ($B20F) and X/2 ($B20D shifted right; bit 8 in $B20E is not used) in the eight-entry ring $B244/$B24C at index $B243 (advanced first, AND 7). The cat follows the oldest entry, eight frames behind ($86F5).

The beam, every frame from $7E49 when it is owned ($B235). Idle ($B8DC = 0): the shapes above and below the ball ($B8DE, $B8DF) are the blank shape 5. Firing ($B8DC = 1-3, started by $8467): tests for objects above and below ($85F2), steps $B8DC every four frames ($B8DB) and ends after the third step, sets the shapes to $3E and $3F + 2 x $B8DC (shapes $40-$45, arcs, shown by sprite 0 in bands $8A52 and $8B22) and the colour $B8E0 from $B881 indexed by $B8DD AND 3 ($0D, $0E, 1, 2), black on odd frames.

Tests the beam against the objects: calls $8613 at the Wizball's X/2 ($B20D with bit 8 from $B20E) with Y = $B20F - 10 and again with Y = $B20F + 30, so it hits above and below the ball. $67 keeps X/2 between the two calls.

Calls $6FBE with X = $48 to test the point (A = X/2, Y) against the objects' boxes at $0200 (42 bytes a record). On a hit $6FBE marks the object ($0225 + record = 1), clears $04CC (byte 4 of slot $48 of the shot table) and returns straight to this routine's caller, which is why the test sits one JSR deeper.
Frame counter of the mutant cat (INC at $861C); a new random direction is drawn when its low four bits are 0, every 16 frames.

Mutant cat flag: 1 after the cat catches a purple droplet (colour 4, $8928); cleared by $8040 and when the catelite is taken ($7375). While set, $8652 takes the cat's input from $861B instead of its stick.

The mutant cat's input: a random byte from $7533, drawn again every 16 frames. With bit 4 forced on (fire up) it becomes the cat's stick bits $B23E, so the mutant cat wanders at random and never fires.

Mutant cat input, from $8655 while $861A is set: every 16 frames ($8619) draws a random byte into $861B and plays sound $0F if its bit 4 is set; sets the cat's stick bits $B23E to $861B OR $10 and continues the cat's update at $8657.

The cat (sprite 1), every frame from the frame loop ($6456, $64E5, $6594). Without the catelite ($B234 = 0) it parks the cat off screen (sprite 1 Y $E7C7 = 0, $B261 = $B262 = 0) and ends its shield ($89B6 = 0); otherwise it goes on at $8652.

The cat's update when the catelite is owned (from $8643; also jumped to from $AC03). The mutant cat takes its input from $861C. At nine lost lives ($B26C = 9) the cat is gone: $B234 = 0, icon 3's sprite pointer back to 2 ($EFFA) and sound $0F. Otherwise it checks what the cat touches ($88B5) and its shield and hits ($895B), then moves it. With a direction on its stick $B23E (or always with $AC4E) it is steered for 10 frames at a time ($B26B): up -4 and down +3 pixels a frame into $B264, left -3 and right +2 into $B263 (X is kept halved, so 6 and 4 pixels), while the follow speeds $B265/$B266 decay to 0. With no direction it follows the Wizball toward its position eight frames ago from the ring $B244/$B24C: Y + 3 at up to 4 pixels a frame ($B266), X/2 - 8 + $B269 at up to 2 ($B265), with $B269 sliding between 0 and 21 so the cat trails on the side away from the spin $B21D. Then $B261 (X/2) and $B262 (Y) move and are limited (X/2 $0F-$A0, the $0F only when not appearing; Y $47-$C7 unless $AC4E), go to sprite 1 ($E7C6/$E7C7, bit 1 of $E7D4) with shapes $0D-$0F in turn every 4 frames ($B526), colour 5, flashing through $B5DF on its last life ($B26C = 8) and black on alternate pairs of frames while its shield runs ($89B6).

The cat's shot, every frame from $6433 and $6597 while the catelite is owned ($B234) and the cat's fire bit (bit 4 of $B23E) is down: first its spray ($8558); then, if slot 2 of the shot table ($0498-$04A3) is free, a shot from the cat's column ($B261 - 8)/4 and row ($B262 - $44)/8, moving the way the Wiz last spun, or while the cat is steered ($B26A = 0) the way it moves ($B263), with character $B8D3[($B262 + 4) AND 7] and colour 7 (blazers: character + 3, colour 12, byte 10 set). Unlike the Wiz, the cat fires again whenever its slot is free while fire is held. Sound 0, or 4 on its last life ($B26C = 8).

What the cat touches, from $866D: tests the point (X/2 $B261, Y $B262 + 11) against the objects through $88FA, which ends this routine when nothing is there. On a hit, Y is the object's record offset: class ($0215 + Y) below 2 is harmful and counts a hit in $89BA; class 2 is a droplet, which the cat collects (zeroing bytes $02, $1F and $20 of the record) and whose colour ($0210 + Y) decides the effect: red, green or blue (2, 5, 6) adds one to the cauldron counter $B12B + $B194[level $B128] and scores through $710B with A = 5; other colours go to $8902. Other classes, such as the pearls (5) the Wiz collects, are ignored.

Calls $6FBE with X = $48 for the cat's point (A = X/2, Y). On a hit $6FBE returns straight into $88C2 with Y = the object's record; with no hit this routine drops its caller's return address (PLA, PLA) so that $88B5 ends here.

The effect of a droplet the cat catches whose colour ($0210 + Y, in A) is not red, green or blue: white (1) gives the current player an extra Wizball (INC $B277 + $BFD9, sound $11); purple (4) makes the mutant cat ($861A = 1, and $B26C = 8, one hit from its end); light blue ($0E) starts the filth raid ($A133 = 6, $B8F1 = 1, tune 5 through $45F1); black (0) starts freaky bits ($8959 = 1, one flash frame in $895A, colours redrawn by $7D1A); any other colour (the manual's indestructacat is grey) sets $B26C = $80, so the cat takes 128 hits before its nine lives start to count, silently while $B26C is negative ($89A8).
Returns in A the colour for scenery characters in colour RAM: 8 (multicolour with black) while freaky bits is on ($8959), otherwise the level's colour $B27F. Called from $70BD, $70CD and $9B70.

Freaky bits flag: 1 after the cat catches a black droplet ($8943). While set, scenery is coloured black ($894D, $7D1A) and band $89BB forces $D022/$D023 to black. Cleared by $8040, $647E and $9FA2 (read at $9F9B).

Frames left in which band $89BB shows the real scenery colours ($B27D/$B27E) while freaky bits is on: 3 each time the Wizball bumps into scenery ($83BC), 1 when freaky bits starts ($8946); counted down at $8A18.

The cat's shield and hits, from $8670. While $89B6 (seconds of shield left) is non-zero it counts down once every 50 frames ($89B7), plays the warning sound $13 once when it drops below 8 ($89B9), and ends below 5. A hit this frame ($89BA, set by $88F6 and $9BB1) then costs 8 seconds of shield, or without a shield one of the cat's nine lives: $B26C + 1, with sound 4 unless $B26C is negative (indestructacat).

Seconds of shield left for the cat: 40 ($28) from the shields icon ($73B5), 8 fewer for each hit ($89B2); counted down by $895B and cleared below 5, by $8640 without a cat, and at $AB17. While non-zero the cat blinks ($880A).
Frame counter of the cat's shield: $895B takes a second off $89B6 each time it reaches 50; zeroed by the shields icon ($73BD).
Blink counter of the cat's shield, incremented at $880F; the cat is drawn black while its bit 1 is clear. The shields icon starts it at $34 ($73CB).
Set once the cat's shield warning (sound $13) has played ($8983); cleared by the shields icon ($73C3).
The cat was hit this frame: incremented at $88F6 (a harmful object) and $9BB1; $895B clears it and takes a shield chunk or a life.

Display-list band at raster line $14 (list $B3E2): the icon bar, seven multicolour sprites in the top border (opened by $8BBB). Positions and colours of sprites 0-7 from $B4C6-$B4DD (in play X $58 to $E4 and $100, 28 apart, Y $1A, colour $0E), multicolour 0 blue (6), or red (2) while $B074 is set, multicolour 1 white; $D018 = $B0, screen $EC00, so the icon shapes are the sprite pointers $EFF8-$EFFE (characters $C000 are not displayed here); X bit 8 for sprite 6 only, sprites 0-6 on, none widened. Then $7269 prepares next frame's icon colours (the lit icon $B258 cycling) and $67A1 colour-cycles the current player's score label. With freaky bits ($8959) it sets $D022/$D023, the landscape's two shared colours, to $B27D/$B27E while $895A counts down, else to black.

Display-list band at raster line $41 (list $B3E2): the landscape begins, below the two score rows. $D018 = $8E OR $B1FD: the landscape screen $E000, $E400 or $E800 (in play-start.vsf the same scenery one column apart, so a coarse scroll step is a change of screen) and the level character set at $F800. $D016 = 7 - $B1FC (the fine horizontal scroll, the world X $B1F2 AND 7), multicolour, 38 columns, OR $AB9B (8, 40 columns, when set at $AB09). $D011 back to 25 rows with Y scroll 3, undoing $8BBB. Background $D021 = $B25C AND $7F, which steps one colour a frame while non-zero (the smart bomb's flash from $7396, and $64CA's).

Display-list band at raster line $30 (list $B3E2), above the score rows: $D018 = $8C (screen $E000, characters $F000: the score line in the text font). Loads the play sprites from the VIC shadow at $E7C4: enable $E7D9, positions, $D010, colours $E7EB-$E7F2, multicolours $E7E9/$E7EA, Y-expand $E7DB OR $B1B1, X-expand $B1B1, multicolour select $B1B2, priority $E7DF; the pointers of sprites 1-7 ($B526-$B52C) go to the landscape screen in use, whose page ($E3, $E7 or $EB from $B1FD) is patched into $8A90, $8B00, $8B1A and $8B3E. Sprite 0 serves three times down the screen: here it is the beam's upper part ($B8DE, colour $B8E0) 23 lines above the Wizball, and the raster lines of the next two bands are written into the list: $B3F6 = Y - 2 for $8B0F, $B3FA = Y + 20 for $8B22 (in a tube, (Y AND $F8) + 20). Ends with the NMI check at $8B04.

High byte of STA $E3F8 at $8A8E, rewritten by $8A67 with $E3 OR ($B1FD >> 2): the beam's upper shape goes to sprite 0's pointer in the landscape screen in use. The STA at $8A91 writes $E3F8 as well, for the score rows, which come from screen $E000.
High byte of STA $E3F8,Y at $8AFE, rewritten by $8A64: the pointers of sprites 1-7 ($B526-$B52C) go to the landscape screen in use.

Anti-tamper check at the end of band $8A52, in undocumented opcodes, typed as bytes because the disassembler does not decode them: A7 86 = LAX $86 (A = X = $FF, stored in $86 by the initialisation at $EC4B); DF 86 FF = DCP $FF86,X, which wraps to $0085: decrements $85 and compares it with $FF; F0 03 = BEQ $8B0E; 68 = PLA; C2 C2 = NOP #$C2. $85 is cleared by the NMI ($7C6B) and made non-zero by band $8BBB at the bottom of each frame, so the check passes only if the once-a-frame NMI came in between. If not, the PLA leaves the IRQ's JSR return address ($7C9F) short and the RTS at $8B0E jumps to $7D in the page of the X register the IRQ saved: apparently a deliberate crash. The same check is at $9287. Live: with CIA 2's interrupts switched off in play the check failed on the next frame (the PLA at $8B0B ran once) and the CPU ran into screen memory and stopped on a JAM at $EA7D.
RTS ending band $8A52: reached by the BEQ of the NMI check at $8B04 when the NMI has run, and after the PLA when it has not.

Display-list band at the raster line in $B3F6, 2 lines above the Wizball (written by $8A52): sprite 0 becomes the Wizball: Y $E7C5, shape $B525 into sprite 0's pointer of the landscape screen (page patched at $8B1A), colour $E7EB.
High byte of STA $E3F8 at $8B18, rewritten by $8A6A: the Wizball's shape $B525 goes to sprite 0's pointer in the landscape screen in use.

Display-list band at the raster line in $B3FA, 20 lines below the Wizball's top (written by $8A52): normally moves sprite 0 23 lines down to show the beam's lower part (shape $B8DF, pointer page patched at $8B3E, colour $B8E0). While sinking into a tube ($B213) it instead puts sprite 0 behind the scenery ($D01B = 1) from here down, so the ball disappears into the tube mouth.
High byte of STA $E3F8 at $8B3C, rewritten by $8A6D: the beam's lower shape $B8DF goes to sprite 0's pointer in the landscape screen in use.

Display-list band at raster line $EE (list $B3E2), below the landscape: background black, then after 15 NOPs $D018 = $DC (screen $F400, used only for its sprite pointers at $F7F8-$F7FD inside the character set; characters $F000) and $D016 = 8. Sprites 0-2 and 4-6 take positions from $B505-$B50A and $B50D-$B512, sprites 0-5 colours from $B515-$B51A and pointers from $B51D-$B522. On: sprite 0 (the level digit, shape $A0, at X $44), sprites 1, 2 and 4 (the red, green and blue cauldrons, shapes $B9-$BB) and sprite 5 (the target cauldron, $BC, at the far right in the target colour $B51A), all at Y $F8 or $FC in the bottom border (opened by $8BBB); 1, 2, 4 and 5 multicolour with grey outlines ($0F, $0B), X bit 8 for sprite 5. Every other frame steps sprite 0's colour through eight entries of $B5CB from $770C ($770A, $770B). Then jumps to $B589.

Display-list band at raster line $F7 (list $B3E2): switches $D011 to 24 rows (keeping the display-enable bit, Y scroll 3) after line 247, where a 24-row screen's bottom border would begin, and before line 251, where the 25-row one would: the VIC never switches the border on, so sprites show below and above the screen (the cauldrons and the icon bar). $8A25 puts back 25 rows. Stores that $D011 value in $85 for the NMI check at $8B04, then jumps to $B589.
A stray RTS after the JMP at $8BC7: nothing reaches it.

Display-list band at raster line $E8 (list $B3E2), where the landscape ends: resets the play sprites' settings (priority, X bit 8, both expansions off, all multicolour), moves sprite 0 to X 0 so that the beam's lower part cannot show in the panel, and after a short delay (DEX from 1) makes the background black ($D021 = 0).

Vertical movement with anti-grav, jumped to from $7F6A instead of the bouncing when $B232 or $AC4E is set: every third frame ($B219) down on the Wiz's stick (bit 1 of $B23F clear) adds 1 to the vertical speed $B218, up to +4, and up (bit 0) subtracts 1, down to -4; with neither the speed decays toward 0. Every frame $B20F += $B218.
Blanks the screen: waits for raster lines 256-275 ($6EA8), then clears the display-enable bit and raster bit 8 in $D011 (AND #$6F). Used by the screen changes ($6392, $8F61, $8F80, $9017 and others).
Shows the screen again: waits for raster lines 256-275 ($6EA8), then sets the display-enable bit of $D011 and clears raster bit 8.
Fills 1,024 bytes from the page in $61 with A ($60 is set to 0; $61 ends four pages on). $8F54 clears the text screen $EC00-$EFFF with spaces this way.
Fills colour RAM, $D800-$DBFF, with A.

Makes the text font (glyphs 0-63, $F000-$F1FF) normal: if $F100, the top row of the space glyph, is non-zero the font is inverted and $8C96 inverts it back. $B276 ends up equal to $F100: 0 when normal, $FF when inverted, which $8DE4 uses to draw text into sprites in the right polarity. Called when play starts ($63EF) and from $7D13.

Makes the text font ($F000-$F1FF) inverted: if $F100 is 0 it inverts all 512 bytes (EOR #$FF) and stores the new $F100 in $B276. The loaded image holds the font inverted; the title page ($8F8F) and $6BAA, $946C keep it so.

Makes the large font and logo glyphs (glyphs $40-$FF, $F200-$F7FF) normal: if $F6F0, row 0 of glyph $DE, is non-zero it inverts the six pages through $8CC7. $B277 ends up equal to $F6F0, used by $8E32 in the same way as $B276.
Makes the large font and logo glyphs ($F200-$F7FF) inverted: if $F6F0 is 0 it inverts the six pages with EOR #$FF; $8CED then stores the new $F6F0 in $B277. Called from $68A6, $6BAD, $9023 and $946F.
Unreachable code, skipped by the JMP at $8CDF: B1 60 49 FF 91 60 C8 C0 40 D0 F5, a loop that would invert 64 more bytes at ($60), which after the six pages is $F800-$F83F.
Tail of $8CB5 and $8CBE after inverting the large font: $B277 = $F6F0, the font's new polarity.
Prints a text page in the large font: sets $B25E = 1 and continues as $8CFA, with X/Y = the page's address and A = its colour. Each letter becomes 2 x 2 glyphs from $B591.

Prints a text page: X/Y = its address (low, high), A = its colour, $B25E = 0 for the text font. A page is records of column, row, PETSCII text and $FF, ended by an extra $FF; the loop at $8D1F takes each record and $8D42 prints it. The screen is $EC00, or while $B874 is set the landscape screen in use ($E0 OR $B1FD >> 2), in which case $6732 is added to each text-font character; both are written into the code at $8D6B and $8D8E.

Prints one text record: column in X, row in Y, text from $62/$63 up to its $FF ($62/$63 left pointing past it). Screen address 40 x row + column on the page in $8D6B, the same offset in colour RAM ($64/$65) filled with the colour in $66. Text font: character AND #$3F plus the value in $8D8E. Large font ($B25E set): $B591[character] + $40, + $41 beside it, + $60 and + $61 below, then two columns on, one for i and l (codes 9 and 12).
Operand of ADC #$EC at $8D6A, the high byte of the screen page to print on, rewritten by $8D19: $EC, or $E0/$E4/$E8 by $B1FD while $B874 is set.
Operand of ADC #$00 at $8D8D, added to every text-font character, rewritten by $8D1C: 0, or the value of $6732 while $B874 is set ($A0 in the snapshots).

Draws a text string into sprite data in the text font: X/Y = the string (ended by $FF), A = the first sprite block, $8EDB = the byte offset in it. Each character's eight bytes from $F000 ($8E0E), exclusive-ORed with $B276 so the font's polarity does not matter, go down a byte column three bytes apart; two calls of $8EDC move one column right, three characters to a sprite, then on to the next block. The title page draws "1. 050000" this way ($8FCF).
Next character of the string at $5E/$5F (index $B274, then advanced): $64/$65 = $F000 + 8 x (character AND #$3F). At the $FF end it drops its return address, which ends the caller $8DE4.

Draws a text string into sprite data in the large font: X/Y = the string, A = the first sprite block. Each character is four 8 x 8 quarters from $8E59 (top left, bottom left, top right, bottom right), exclusive-ORed with $B277 and placed by $8EDC (down 8 rows, then back up and one column right), so a sprite holds one and a half characters. The title page draws the WIZBALL logo this way from the string "#$%&'((" at $B693, whose characters map through $B591 to the logo's glyphs ($8FBB).

Next quarter of a large-font character from the string at $5E/$5F: glyph $B591[character AND #$3F], +1 for the right half (bit 1 of $B273), + $20 for the lower half (bit 0); $64/$65 = $F200 + 8 x glyph. $B273 counts the quarters 0-3 and moves on to the next character ($B274) after the fourth. At the $FF end it drops its return address, which ends $8E32.
Sets up $8DE4 and $8E32: the string's address X/Y into $5E/$5F, the counters $B273-$B275 to 0, and the destination $60/$61 and its column start $62/$63 = $C000 + 64 x A + $8EDB.

Byte offset into the first sprite block where $8EAC starts drawing text (row x 3 + column): 0 normally; $6A1B sets $2A (row 14) and $AE49 sets $21 (row 11) for a second line, and both put 0 back afterwards.

Moves the sprite-text destination $62/$63 (copied to $60/$61) on by one 8 x 8 cell: even steps (counted in $B275) go 24 bytes down (8 rows), odd steps 23 bytes back up, one column right; after six steps, three columns, it adds $3D to reach the next 64-byte sprite block.
Fills X sprite blocks from block Y (address $C000 + 64 x Y) with A (kept in $66). Used to clear sprite shapes before drawing into them, and at $8FE3 to make three solid ones.

Prepares the text screen with the display off: $D011 = $0B (blank, 25 rows), $D016 = 8, $D018 = $BC (screen $EC00, characters $F000), $EC00-$EFFF filled with spaces (sprite pointers included), sprites off ($D015 = 0), colour RAM black ($8C6F).

Where the initialisation continues (JMP from $ECB1); also jumped to from $6EE1, which leaves a game when $B254 is 2, and from $6B8F: blanks the screen, disables interrupts (the display-list install at $8F89 enables them again), silences the SID ($47D0), starts tune $1A through $45F1, sets $B8F1 = $B8F2 = 2 and falls into the title page at $8F75.

The title page with the high scores (also jumped to from $6BF8, $909F and $94E7): black border and background, $B254 = 0, the display list $B416 (pointer $B450) installed, the text screen cleared ($8F41), the text font inverted and the large font normal. Prints the page at $BEB5 (pointer $BFFE: "top  scores", "one  plr", "two  plrs" and rows 2-7 of both tables) in colour 0, clears $EBB2-$EBF3 (state of the routines at $9829-$98E5), draws the WIZBALL logo ($B693) in the large font into sprite blocks $80-$84 and "1. 050000" ($BFE8) in the text font into blocks $85-$8B, prints "sensi soft" ($B69B, after ten spaces at the same place) in the large font in white, fills blocks $8C-$8E with $FF and turns the screen on with a timeout of 150 x 5 frames ($9215). Then once a frame ($6E71): to $944D when $B254 reaches 4, else $9829, the timeout ($921E; the player menu at $9017 when it runs out), and the sticks ($73D4, $91FA): fire starts a game ($6392), any other input from $91FA goes to the menu.

Player-select menu over a starfield, the second screen of the attract sequence. Entered from the title loop when its timer runs out ($9003) or a joystick moves without fire ($9012), and from Wiztips ($94D5). Blanks the screen ($8C44), installs display list $B452 (bands $93CC-$93F7, $9419), puts the large font in its inverted form ($8CBE), clears the screen ($8F41) and prints the menu page $B6B6 (pointer at $B7E0: 'one player', 'two player', 'two player team', 'three player', 'four  player', 'press space for wiztips'). Clears sprite shape 5 and sets $C161 = $C0, a two-pixel star; all eight sprites unexpanded, hires, in front, white, shape 5; unblanks ($8C50); screen timer 130 ticks (650 frames). Loop, once a frame: colour cycles $98BE, $994A, $996A; moves the four stars ($90BD); SPACE ($B254 = 4) goes to Wiztips ($944D); places the stars in the bottom border ($6EA8, $915F) and again once the raster is at $87-$8B ($9163); when the timer ($921E) runs out, sprites off and back to the title ($8F75); a joystick change ($91FA) moves the highlight ($91DB, option $B272 = 0-4) and restarts the timer at 90 ticks; fire starts the game (JMP $6392).

Moves the four stars of the menu and 'get ready!' starfields (from $9075 and $691C). Each star is a 6-byte record at $EB9A + 6n, n = 0-3: X whole and fraction, Y whole and fraction, X speed, Y speed. A star whose X byte is 0 is respawned: X = random 0-127 + $24 (+ carry), Y = $91, both speeds random with bit 5 set ($7533); every star is then moved by $910A. The loads at $90E6-$90EC are dead (the TXA discards them). Finally compares the hardware vectors $FFFA-$FFFF with the copy at $B62D-$B632 (NMI $7C61, reset $0000, IRQ $7C73) and increments the background colour $D021 if any byte differs: apparently a tamper check that makes the screen flicker when something has replaced the game's interrupt vectors.

Moves one star (X = record offset 0, 6, 12 or 18 in the table at $EB9A): adds twice the X speed (byte 4) to the 16-bit X (whole part byte 0, fraction byte 1) and twice the Y speed (byte 5) to the 16-bit Y (bytes 2-3). Speeds are unsigned, so every star drifts right and down; $915F/$9163 mirror it into the other three directions. The star is killed (X byte = 0, respawned next frame by $90BD) when X leaves $0C-$AB or Y leaves $7A-$F9 (signed compares used as ranges, see notes).
Entry to $9165 with $B271 = 1: every star's Y is mirrored as $FF - Y, giving the copy for the top half of the screen. Called in the bottom border before the frame is drawn ($9085, $692B).

Places all eight sprites as the four stars of $EB9A mirrored left and right: sprites 0-3 at X*2 and sprites 4-7 at ($B0 - X)*2 (bit 8 into $D010), Y as stored, or $FF - Y when $B271 is 1 (entry $915F). This entry clears $B271: the copy for the bottom half, placed once the raster has passed line $87 ($9092, $6958). With both calls the eight sprites show sixteen stars flying out from the middle of the screen. Uses $5E, $5F, $60, $61, $66.

Moves the menu highlight. A = joystick byte (active low, from $91FA), kept in $66. Up (bit 0 low) with $B272 > 0 decrements $B272; down (bit 1 low) with $B272 < 4 increments it. $B272 is the chosen game option, 0 one player to 4 four players, read by the bands $93CC-$93F7 and at $687E.

Returns A = both joystick ports combined ($B256 AND $B257, read by $73D4 or $7429; active low, bits 0-4 up, down, left, right, fire) with bits 5-7 forced on, but only when that differs from the value it last returned ($B270); otherwise A = $FF, which is also what releasing everything returns. Leaves $B256 in $66 and $B257 in $67. Used by the title ($9009), menu ($90A5), Wiztips ($94C7) and 'get ready!' ($695E) loops and at $6A9F.

Starts the attract-screen timer: $B25F = A ticks, $B260 = 5 frames to the first tick (A = 0 gives 256 ticks). Callers: the title 150 ticks (750 frames), the menu 130, each menu move 90, Wiztips 0 (1,280 frames), $6A81 200.
Counts the attract-screen timer down, one call a frame: every fifth call decrements $B25F. Returns with Z set (BEQ) on the call that takes $B25F to 0, Z clear otherwise.

Title band at raster $23 (list $B416). Text colour $D021 = $EBD1 for 'top  scores'; sprites 0-4 on, hires, in front, X-expanded, not Y-expanded, at the positions in $B571-$B57A (X $48, $78, $A8, $D8, $108; Y $3D) with shapes $80-$84, the WIZBALL logo that $8E32 draws into sprite data. Then on each raster line from $3E to $4D sets all five sprite colours to the next of $EBD0 down to $EBC1, the 16 bar colours $9884 scrolls. Falls into the NMI watchdog at $9287.

NMI watchdog, the tail of $922C, in opcodes the disassembler does not decode (so typed as bytes): $A7 $86 = LAX $86 (A = X = $FF, stored once at $EC4B); $DF $86 $FF = DCP $FF86,X, which with X = $FF wraps to $0085: decrement $85 and compare it with A; $F0 $03 = BEQ $9291, the RTS. The NMI at $7C61 writes 0 to $85 once a frame and the bands $936A-$93C5 increment it later in the frame, so the check passes only if an NMI has arrived since the previous frame. Otherwise $68 = PLA, then $7C $C2 $60 = NOP $60C2,X (an illegal three-byte NOP whose last byte is the RTS) leads into $9292. The STX $DF / STX $FF an ordinary decode shows here are false.
The RTS ($60) that is also the last byte of the three-byte NOP at $928F: the BEQ at $928C lands here when the NMI watchdog check passes, and the logo band returns normally.

Failure path of the NMI watchdog, reached only after the PLA at $928E has taken a byte off the stack, and never traced by the disassembler (typed as bytes): JSR $7533 / STA $929F / JSR $7533 / STA $92A0 / INC $1000,X / RTS. It writes two random numbers into the INC's operand ($1000 is a placeholder), increments that random byte of memory, and returns through the unbalanced stack to an unpredictable address: apparently a deliberate crash when the once-a-frame NMI has been stopped, as a freezer cartridge or monitor would.

Title band at raster $6B: text colour 0; $D018 = $BC (screen $EC00, characters $F000); colour RAM of rows 8 and 9, columns 20-39, = $EBF2, the colour of 'sensi soft' in the large font; sprites 0-2 not Y-expanded, on, shapes $85-$87 ('1. 050000' drawn by $8DE4) at X $18, $48, $78, Y $76 (from $B57B-$B580). After 16 NOPs of timing it colours the three sprites at rasters $76, $78, $7A and $7C with $EBD5 down to $EBD2; at raster $8C it writes $D018 = $BD (the same layout, bit 0 unused) and text colour $D021 = $EBD6 for 'one  plr' and 'two  plrs'.

Title band at raster $93: makes sprites 0-3 four solid bars behind the high-score table: Y $A2; X $E8, $30, $00, $B8 (bit 8 clear); behind the characters ($D01B = $FF); Y-expanded, and still X-expanded from $922C; shape $8C, which $8FE3 filled with $FF. The title's small font is inverted (letters are background pixels, $8C8D), so the bars show only through the letters and colour the ranks and scores of both tables.
Title band at raster $A0: text colour $D021 = $EBF1, the colour of every name in the table, then colours high-score row 2 from raster $A2 with X = 8 (falls into $9374).

Shared tail of the high-score bands. A = the row's first raster line, X = colour index. Moves the four bars (sprites 0-3, $9327) to Y = A, then at exactly lines A, A+2, A+4 and A+6 sets sprites 1 and 3 to $EBD6+X and sprites 0 and 2 to $EBE3+X, X counting down (sprite 2 covers the left table's rank, 1 its score, 3 the right table's rank, 0 its score). Ends with INC $FFB0,X at X = $D5, which wraps to INC $85, the counter the NMI watchdog at $9287 expects the NMI to have cleared.
Title band at raster $AF: high-score row 3, the bars and their colours from raster $B2 with X = 9 ($9374).
Title band at raster $C0: high-score row 4, the bars and their colours from raster $C2 with X = 10 ($9374).
Title band at raster $D0: high-score row 5, the bars and their colours from raster $D2 with X = 11 ($9374).
Title band at raster $E0: high-score row 6, the bars and their colours from raster $E2 with X = 12 ($9374).
Title band at raster $F0: high-score row 7, the bars and their colours from raster $F2 with X = 13 ($9374). The list's last entry, so the next interrupt is its first line again.

Menu band at raster $48 (list $B452), 'one player' (row 3): when $B272 is 0, colours the row in stripes from raster $4B ($9401); otherwise sets the text colour $D021 = 6, the blue of every row that is not highlighted.
Menu band at raster $60, 'two player' (row 6): when $B272 is 1, colours the row in stripes from raster $63 ($9401); otherwise returns and the row stays blue.
Menu band at raster $78, 'two player team' (row 9): when $B272 is 2, colours the row in stripes from raster $7B ($9401); otherwise returns and the row stays blue.
Menu band at raster $90, 'three player' (row 12): when $B272 is 3, colours the row in stripes from raster $93 ($9401); otherwise returns and the row stays blue.
Menu band at raster $A8, 'four  player' (row 15): when $B272 is 4, colours the row in stripes from raster $AB ($9401); otherwise returns and the row stays blue.

Colours one text row in four stripes of two lines. Y = raster line; for X = 4 down to 1 waits until the raster is past Y (signed compare), sets $D021 = $EBD6+X ($EBDA, $EBD9, $EBD8, $EBD7: the head of the ramp $98BE feeds from $B5DF), Y += 2; then $D021 = 6 (blue). For the highlighted menu option and the band at $6E00.
Menu band at raster $E6: text colour $D021 = $EBD6 for 'press space for wiztips' (row 23).

Joystick reader of the Wiz-lab's weapon choice ($B07B): reads the joysticks and nine control keys ($7429), then returns A = $B256 AND $B257 when that differs from its last value ($944B), else $FF. Unlike $91FA it keeps bits 5-7 as read.
Steps all seven colour cycles once: $98BE, $98E9, $9916, $994A, $996A, $997D, $999D. Every frame on the Wiztips pages ($94C1) and from $6CC8.
Last joystick value returned by the Wiz-lab reader $9420, kept for its change test.

Wiztips page on show, 0-2: $944D increments it (3 wraps to 0) each time Wiztips opens or SPACE is pressed on it; indexes the display lists at $B86E and the text pointers at $4199. Starts at 2, so the first SPACE shows page one.

Wiztips, entered on SPACE ($B254 = 4) from the title ($8FF8), the menu ($907F) and Wiztips itself ($94DF). Blanks the screen, advances $944C, installs that page's display list from $B86E ($9549, $957B, $95A1), puts both fonts in their inverted form ($8C8D, $8CBE), fills the screen at $EC00 and the colour RAM with 0, sprites off, prints the page body ($8CFA) and its large-font title ($8CF4) from the four-byte entry at $4199 + 4 x page, sets the sprites unexpanded, in front, multicolour and all on, unblanks and sets the timer to 256 ticks (1,280 frames). Loop, once a frame: waits for the border ($6EA8), steps the colour cycles ($9436), reads keys and joysticks ($73D4); fire starts the game (JMP $6392), another joystick change goes to the menu ($9017), SPACE shows the next page, and when the timer runs out it returns to the title ($8F75).

Places A sprites, starting at sprite X, from 5-byte records at ($7D): X position (low 8 bits), Y position, X bit 8 (non-zero sets the sprite's bit in $D010 from $9539, zero clears it with $9541), colour ($D027+n) and shape ($EFF8+n, the sprite pointers of the screen at $EC00). The sprite number wraps from 7 to 0. Uses $78 (sprite number), $79 (twice it) and $7F (count). Called by the Wiztips bands.
The bit of sprite n, 1, 2, 4 ... $80: 8 bytes indexed by sprite number, ORed into $D010 at $950B to set the sprite's X bit 8.
Mask that clears sprite n's bit, $FE, $FD ... $7F: 8 bytes indexed by sprite number, ANDed into $D010 at $9516.

Display list of Wiztips page one ('getting  started'), installed by $9469 from $B86E. Typed as words: the first raster line (1), then pairs of band routine and raster line of the next interrupt, so each routine runs at the line before it: $9681 at 1, music $B90C at $16, $9703 at $41, $970C at $50, music $B903 at $64, $972F at $97, music $B8FC at $AD, $971A at $B4, $9750 at $BE, $9721 at $CD, $9728 at $E6, music $B8F3 at $FF; a next line of 0 ends it.

Display list of Wiztips page two ('cat  control'), from $B870, words as for $9549: $9762 at 1, $B90C at $16, $97C2 at $41, $97CB at $50, $B903 at $64, $97D2 at $7F, $97D7 at $96, $B8FC at $AD, $B8F3 at $FF.

Display list of Wiztips page three ('general  hints'), from $B872, words as for $9549: $97F0 at 1, $B90C at $16, $97FC at $41, $9805 at $5E, $B903 at $6E, $9812 at $76, $9805 at $8E, $9812 at $A6, $B8FC at $AD, $9805 at $C6, $9812 at $D6, $9805 at $EE, $B8F3 at $FF.

Wiztips page one, sprites 0-7 placed by $9681: eight 5-byte records (X, Y, X bit 8, colour, shape; $94EA). Three aliens after 'shoot' on row 6 (X $78, $A8, $D8, Y $5B, colours 3, 6, 5, shapes animated by $9681); the pearl after 'pickup' on row 9 (X $90, Y $73, colour 5, shape $78); a flashing icon after 'to move' (X $100, colour from $B4D6, shape $0B); the thrust, anti-grav and beam icons on row 17 (Y $B3, X $18, $87, $F8, colour $0E, shapes $07, $03, $0B).
Shape byte of page one's first alien (the record at $95D7), rewritten every frame by $96D8 with $4C-$4F from $96F7; the next four bytes are the second alien's X, Y, X bit 8 and colour.
Shape byte of page one's second alien, rewritten by $96E1 with $46-$49 from $96FB; the next four bytes are the third alien's X, Y, X bit 8 and colour.
Shape byte of page one's third alien, rewritten by $96EA with $3C, $3D, $3E, $3D from $96FF; then the pearl's record (X $90, Y $73, colour 5, shape $78) and the icon record's X, Y and X bit 8.

Colour byte of the icon after 'to move' on Wiztips page one, copied from $B4D6 by $968C every frame, so it flashes as $7269 makes icon 1's colour flash; then its shape ($0B) and the records of the thrust, anti-grav and beam icons.

Wiztips page one, sprites 0-5 placed again by the band $9750 at raster $BE: six records for icon rows 20 (Y $CB: double $04, cat $02, blazers $06) and 23 (Y $E3: wizspray $08, catspray $0A, shield $00), at X $18, $87, $F8, colour $0E.

Wiztips page two, sprites 0-7 placed by $9762: on row 10 a colour sphere after 'shoot' (X $50, Y $7B, colour 2, shapes $7B-$7D) and a droplet after 'pickup' (X $C8, colour 2); then the legend's droplets, two a row at X $18 and $C0: red chemical colour 2 and green chemical 5 (Y $9B), blue chemical 6 and mutant cat 4 (Y $B3), filth raid $0E and bonus Wizball 1 (Y $CB). Droplet shapes $50-$52, animated.
Shape byte of the colour sphere on Wiztips page two, rewritten every frame by $9783 with $7C, $7B, $7C, $7D from $97B8; the next four bytes are the 'pickup' droplet's X, Y, X bit 8 and colour.
Shape byte of the droplet after 'pickup' on page two, rewritten by $977D from $97BC; the next four bytes are the red-chemical droplet's X, Y, X bit 8 and colour.

Shape byte of the red-chemical droplet, the first of eight shape bytes 5 apart ($962B, $9630 ... $964E) that $977A rewrites with $50, $51, $52, $51, each droplet one phase on from the last; the bytes between are the green, blue, mutant-cat, filth-raid and bonus-Wizball records.

Wiztips page two, sprites 0-1 placed again by the band $97D7 at raster $96: the last legend row, indestructacat (X $18, colour $0B) and freaky bits (X $C0, colour 0), Y $E3; their shape bytes $9649 and $964E are animated by $9762.

Eight 5-byte sprite records that no code reads: X $50, $58, then $18 five times and $20 (bit 8 set), Y $62 to $EA, colours 3, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 3, all shape $80. Only the fifth word at $967F points here; apparently a leftover layout.
Low byte of $95D7, page one's first sprite table, read by $9691; the first of five words ($95D7, $95FF, $961D, $9645, $964F), each byte loaded on its own.
High byte of the pointer to $95D7, read by $9696.
Low byte of the pointer to $95FF, page one's icon rows, read by $9752.
High byte of the pointer to $95FF, read by $9757.
Low byte of the pointer to $961D, page two's first sprite table, read by $9798.
High byte of the pointer to $961D, read by $979D.
Low byte of the pointer to $9645, page two's last droplet row, read by $97E1.
High byte of the pointer to $9645, read by $97E6.
Fifth word of the sprite-table pointers, $964F; no code reads it.

Wiztips page one, band at raster 1. Sets $B258 = 1 and calls $7269, which resets the seven icon colours $B4D6-$B4DC and flashes the one of icon $B258, then copies icon 1's colour $B4D6 to $95EE; places sprites 0-7 from $95D7 ($94EA); sprite multicolours $D026 = $0D, $D025 = $0B; text colour $D021 = $EBD2 for 'wiztips one'. Then animates the three aliens: timers $96EE-$96F0 count to 6, 4 and 4 frames ($96F4), each period advances a frame 0-3 ($96F1-$96F3), and the shapes from $96F7, $96FB, $96FF go into $95DB, $95E0, $95E5.
Three frame counters, one per alien on Wiztips page one ($96EE-$96F0), counted up by $9681 and reset at the period in $96F4.
Animation frame, 0-3, of page one's first alien, and the base of the three frames $96F1-$96F3 that $96C2 advances by index; read at $96D2 to pick a shape from $96F7.
Animation frame of page one's second alien, read at $96DB to pick its shape from $96FB.
Animation frame of page one's third alien, read at $96E4 to pick its shape from $96FF.
Frames per animation step of the three aliens on Wiztips page one: 6, 4, 4 (compared at $96B8).
Shapes of page one's first alien, frames 0-3: $4C, $4D, $4E, $4F.
Shapes of page one's second alien, frames 0-3: $46, $47, $48, $49.
Shapes of page one's third alien, frames 0-3: $3C, $3D, $3E, $3D.
Wiztips page one band at raster $41: text colour $D021 = $EBD2 with bit 3 flipped (the lighter or darker shade of the title's colour) for 'getting  started'.
Wiztips page one band at raster $50: text colour $D021 = $EBF2 for the 'shoot' and 'pickup' rows.
Seven bytes shaped like a band routine, LDA $EBD7 / STA $D021 / RTS, that no display list or code refers to: apparently a leftover, left undefined.
Wiztips page one band at raster $B4: text colour $D021 = $EBD8 for 'thrust  anti-grav  beam' (row 17).
Wiztips page one band at raster $CD: text colour $D021 = $EBD9 for 'double  cat  blazers' (row 20).
Wiztips page one band at raster $E6: text colour $D021 = $EBDA for 'wizspray  catspray  shield' (row 23).
Wiztips page one band at raster $97: sprite multicolours $D026 = 1, $D025 = 6 for the icons below, then colours 'wiggle joystick to select..' (row 13) in stripes from raster $99 (falls into $973B).

Colours one text row in four stripes of two lines. Y = raster line; for X = 0 to 3 waits until the raster is past Y, sets $D021 = $EBE4+X (the head of the ramp $98E9 feeds from $B5CB), Y += 2. Unlike $9401 it leaves the last colour set. Used by $972F, $97D2 and the bands at $6DE3.
Wiztips page one band at raster $BE: reuses sprites 0-5 for icon rows 20 and 23 from $95FF ($94EA).

Wiztips page two, band at raster 1. Every fourth frame ($97C0) advances the phase $97C1; writes the sphere shape for the phase ($97B8) into $9621 and droplet shapes ($97BC, one phase further for each record) into $9626 and the eight legend records ($962B + 5n); places sprites 0-7 from $961D; multicolours $D025 = $0B, $D026 = $0D; text colour $D021 = $EBD2 for 'wiztips two'.
Shapes of the colour sphere on Wiztips page two, by phase: $7C, $7B, $7C, $7D.
Shapes of the droplets on Wiztips page two, by phase: $50, $51, $52, $51.
Frame counter of the Wiztips page two animation; $9762 steps the phase every fourth frame.
Animation phase, used modulo 4, of the sphere and droplets on Wiztips page two.
Wiztips page two band at raster $41: text colour $EBD2 with bit 3 flipped for 'cat  control' (the same code as $9703 and $97FC).
Wiztips page two band at raster $50: text colour $D021 = $EBF1 for 'one plr - hold down fire' and 'two plr team - other joystick port'.
Wiztips page two band at raster $7F: colours 'shoot , pickup with cat for,' (row 10) in stripes from raster $81 ($973B).
Wiztips page two band at raster $96: text colour $EBD1 with bit 3 flipped for the droplet legend (rows 14-23); reuses sprites 0-1 for the last droplet row from $9645.
Wiztips page three (no sprites), band at raster 1: text colour $D021 = $EBD2 for 'wiztips three', all sprites off.
Wiztips page three band at raster $41: text colour $EBD2 with bit 3 flipped for 'general  hints'.
Wiztips page three band at rasters $5E, $8E, $C6 and $EE: text colour from $9821 by $EBB8 AND 3 (the counter $98BE steps), for the first, third and fifth hints.

Wiztips page three band at rasters $76, $A6 and $D6: text colour from $9825 by ($EBB8 AND 3) EOR 3, for the second and fourth hints and 'continue game feature....', so they cycle out of step with the others.
Four text colours for $9805: 2, 8, $0E, 8 (red, orange, light blue, orange).
Four text colours for $9812, read backwards: $0E, 8, 2, 8.

Title-screen colour sequencer, once a frame from the title loop ($8FFB). Counts $EBF3 up to $FF (it starts at 0: $8FA0 clears the colour state) and starts the cycles one by one, so the screen appears in stages: from frame 10 the logo bars ($9884), 35 'top scores' ($994A), 90 the top score's sprites ($9916), 105 'sensi soft' ($999D), 155 and 195 the table's ramps ($98BE, $98E9), 254 the headings and names ($996A, $997D; the second test at $987C repeats $FE). Until its cycle starts, a colour is 0, black on black.

Every second call ($EBB2) scrolls the 16 logo bar colours $EBC1-$EBD0: the lower eight move down a place and the upper eight up, away from the middle, and the middle pair $EBC9-$EBCA take the next colour of the 32-entry sequence at $B5FB (index $EBC0 / 2), so bands of colour flow out from the middle of the WIZBALL logo.

Every third call ($EBB3): shifts the 13-colour ramp $EBD7-$EBE2 up one place into $EBD8-$EBE3, steps $EBB8 and puts $B5DF[$EBB8 AND 7] (0, 6, 4, $E, 1, $E, 4, 6: black to white by way of blue) in $EBD7. Read by $9401, the high-score bands and the Wiztips bands; $EBB8 also times Wiztips page three.

Every third call ($EBB4): shifts $EBE5-$EBF0 down one place into $EBE4-$EBEF, steps $EBB7 and puts $B5CB[$EBB7 AND 7] (0, 2, 4, $A, 1, $A, 4, 2: black to white by way of red) in $EBF0. Read by $973B and the high-score bands.

Every third call ($EBB5): shifts $EBD3-$EBD5 down into $EBD2-$EBD4, steps $EBBB (0-7) and puts $B5E7[$EBBB] (5, $D, 1, $D: greens and white) in $EBD5. $EBD2 is the Wiztips title colour; $EBD2-$EBD5 colour the top score's sprites.
Every seventh call ($EBBA, back to 0): steps $EBB9 and sets $EBD1 = $B5EF[$EBB9 AND 3] (0, 6, 3, $E).
In the frame $994A steps (while $EBBA is 0): sets $EBD6 = $B5F3[$EBB9 AND 3] (2, 9, 8, 9).
Every fourth call ($EBBC): steps $EBBD and sets $EBF1 = $B5DF[$EBBD AND 7].
Every fourth call ($EBBE): steps $EBBF and sets $EBF2 = $B5CB[$EBBF AND 7].

Moves and draws the alien bullets, once a frame in play ($6444), in the bonus stage ($65B0) and at $7DE7, not while $B1CF is set. When $B1FF is positive every record's column moves one left, when negative one right: apparently to keep the bullets on the landscape when it scrolls by a whole character. Then flips $B280 and handles half the 16 records at $0300, 0-7 or 8-15 in turn, calling $9A14 for each in use. Record, 16 bytes: +0 column, +1 row, +2/+3 position in the cell (0-31), +4/+5 X and Y speed (signed), +6 the character under the bullet, +7/+8 its screen address (high, low), +9 its colour RAM page, +$A state (0 free, 2 just fired, 1 flying), +$B colour counter.

Moves one bullet (X = record offset, A = its state; 2 becomes 1). Adds the X speed to the position in the cell (0-31), stepping a column on overflow or underflow, and the same for Y and the row; at row 20 or more, or column 39 or more, the record is freed. Otherwise reads and saves the character under it on the landscape screen (page from $B1FD and the row tables $0519/$0500, three rows down) with its address; over a character of $80 or more (scenery) the bullet is freed, or only not drawn while $B1D0 is non-zero; else draws character $5B-$6A from $B8E1, the one with a dot at the bullet's place in the cell (4 x 4 places), coloured from $B885 (1, 4, 1, 6, 1, 7, 1, 2: flashing).
End column (exclusive) of Wiz's box for bullet hits: first column + 2, set at $9AE9, tested at $9B80.
First column of Wiz's bullet box: (Wiz X / 2 - 11) / 4, set at $9AE3.
End row (exclusive) of Wiz's bullet box: first row + 2.
First row of Wiz's bullet box: (Wiz Y - $43) / 8, in bullet rows (screen row - 3).
End column (exclusive) of the cat's bullet box: its column + 1.
Column of the cat's bullet box: ($B261 - 12) / 4.
End row (exclusive) of the cat's bullet box: its row + 1.
Row of the cat's bullet box: ($B262 - $43) / 8.

Once a frame before the bullets move ($6427, $64B3, $6581, $7DB8). Works out two boxes in bullet cells: Wiz's from $B20D/$B20E (X, 9 bits) and $B20F (Y), two columns by two rows ($9ACE-$9AD1), and the cat's from $B261 and $B262, one cell ($9AD2-$9AD5); clears $B281, the 'no free record' flag; then calls $9B53 for each record of the half that $99BD drew in the previous frame ($B280).

For a flying bullet (state 1; X = record offset): puts back the character it covered and colours the cell with $894D's colour ($B27F, or 8 while $8959 is set); if its cell is in Wiz's box the record is freed and $7F0A is incremented (Wiz hit, handled at $7EDF); in the cat's box it is freed and $89BA incremented (the cat hit, handled at $8992).

Fires a bullet from the alien in slot X of the table at $0200 (42 bytes a slot; +0 X / 2, +2 Y). A = direction 0-$3F ($9C62) or $FF, aimed at Wiz. Does nothing while $B1CF or $B281 is set, or unless the alien's Y is at least $40 and its X - 8 is 0 to $9F. Takes the first free record at $0300 (none: sets $B281) at the alien's cell; an aimed bullet gets X speed random 0-15 and Y speed 15 minus that, each signed toward Wiz ($B20D / 2, $B20F); marks it just fired (2), clears its colour counter and draws one random number. Called by the alien behaviours at $A566-$A5A3.
Turns a direction A = 0-$3F (0 up, $10 right, $20 down, $30 left, clockwise) into the bullet's X and Y speeds (+4 and +5 of record X), signed, with |X| + |Y| = 16: 64 directions on a diamond.

Prepares the bonus stage's waves ($64C1): clears the alien table ($9CD5), resets the script's wait counter $BB05 and position $BB06, and copies the wave script $3902-$39FF (254 bytes) to $ED02-$EDFF, because running it counts its loop counters down in place.
Clears the 16 alien bullet records, $0300-$03FF.
Clears the alien table $0200-$02FF (six slots of 42 bytes), zeroes $B1AE and clears bits 2-7 of $E7D9.

The bonus stage's wave interpreter, once a frame ($65C3) until $B1CF is set. Script at $ED02 (copied from $3902), position $BB06. A record whose second byte is $BB04 ($39) is a loop, (target + 2, $39, count): while count is non-zero it is decremented and the script jumps back, then the record is skipped. $FF and $FE set and clear $B1F8, which $6755 uses to speed up or slow down the stage (apparently its scrolling); $FD ends the stage ($B1CF = $36). Any other record is (type, delay): with type bit 7 set it waits for all six alien slots to be empty, otherwise for one free slot; then it counts delay frames ($BB05) and creates alien type (bits 0-6) from the template table $39DC ($9DA1), except type $63, a pause.

Creates an alien in slot X of the table at $0200 from the template at ($62): copies the template's first 23 bytes, zeroes the other 19 of the 42-byte slot, then applies its random fields: byte 23 is their count, each a triple (mask, base, offset) setting slot byte offset to (random AND mask) + base. Called by the wave script ($9D97) and from $AA68.

At the start of play ($63F5): copies the empty cauldron picture $CE00-$CE3F (sprite shape $38) into the four cauldron sprites $EE40-$EF3F (shapes $B9-$BC: red, green, blue and the mix), zeroes their row counters $9EC6-$9EC9 and calls $776D.

Once a frame in play ($6450), and from $AB91 and $AEE5. Caps the red, green and blue cauldron levels $B12B-$B12D at 20 (a signed test); while $B1CF and $B213 are 0 copies a byte of the mix cauldron's top row ($EF01) into $B874, so a full mix cauldron sends the frame loop to the colour-completed sequence ($6414, $646F); sets the mix level $B12E to the sum, over red, green and blue, of the smaller of the cauldron's level and the target recipe ($B2C0 + 3 x $B51A), unless $AC4E is set; compares the new-key code $B254 with 8, 9 and 7 through branches that all land on the next instruction (no effect); then redraws one row of each cauldron ($9E81). Live: with the red cauldron poked to 20 on level 1 (target red), $B874 became $AA 22 frames later and the loop left for $646F.

Redraws one of the 21 rows of cauldron X (0-3; A = its sprite's offset from $EE40). Steps its counter $9EC6+X (0-20), takes row 20 - counter, and copies that row's three bytes from the full picture $CE40 if the cauldron's level ($B12B+X) is at least the counter, else from the empty one $CE00. So a level L shows the bottom L + 1 rows full, and each cauldron is redrawn in 21 frames.
Row counter (0-20) of the red cauldron sprite, and the base of the four counters $9EC6-$9EC9 indexed by cauldron in $9E81; zeroed by $9DE9 and $6AC0.
Row counter of the green cauldron sprite ($9E81); zeroed at $9E00.
Row counter of the blue cauldron sprite ($9E81); zeroed at $9E03.
Row counter of the mix cauldron sprite ($9E81); zeroed at $9E06 and $7776.
Five bytes nothing reads: '00' in PETSCII, $FF, and the word $9ECA, which points at itself; apparently the remains of a text record and its pointer.

Counts the aliens still to shoot on the current landscape ($B128): its list number from $B19D (0: none), the list from $B1A6; entries are two bytes from offset 2 (position, type), a type with bit 7 set is destroyed, $FF ends. Stores the count in $B1AF and falls into $9EFD. Called from $826A, $A254 and $9F5B.

Unless the colour is complete ($B874), prints $B1AF as two digits on row 1 of the play screen at $E000 (column from $71DD by player, $BFD9): the two-digit count on the top line. At 0, if $E7D9 AND $FC is 0 and the landscape is one of the three highest open ($B1CE - $B128 < 3), makes it a new list ($9F9B), calls the sound driver $4553 with Y = $14, calls $710B with 100 (apparently a score award), zeroes $B1AE and counts again.

At the start of play ($63EC) and from $AF0F: clears the list numbers $B19D-$B1A5 (landscapes 0-8), zeroes $B1AE, and makes lists for the three landscapes $B1CE, $B1CE - 1 and $B1CE - 2 ($9F9B). While $B129 is 0 (set so by $6832 when a game starts) the current landscape's list is replaced by the fixed one at $A0EC.
Aliens in a group of a landscape list: 4, 6, 12, 6, picked at random at $9FDE.
List number of each landscape 0-8: 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3 (read at $9FAC and $A0EC), so the three open landscapes always use different lists.
Spacing of the aliens in a group: 1, 2, 3, 1, picked at random at $9FE9.
First of the four alien types a group gets with 4 chances in 16, type 0 (read by index at $A009, compared at $A013); the table is 0, 2, 8, 11.
Second special alien type, 2 (compared at $A018).
Third special alien type, 8 (compared at $A01D).
Fourth special alien type, 11 (compared at $A022).

Makes the alien list of landscape X (0-8), continuing past $A000. If $8959 is set, first clears it and calls $7D1A. The landscape uses list $9F8A[X] (recorded in $B19D+X), at the address in $B1A6. Writes 0, 0, then groups from position 20: each starts 5-20 further on, with 4, 6, 12 or 6 aliens ($9F86) spaced 1, 2, 3 or 1 ($9F93), of a random type 1-16 or, with 4 chances in 16, one of 0, 2, 8, 11 ($9F97); $A070 adjusts the type's record in the $3ECF table for the landscape, and $A027 the special types' byte $0E by level. Entries are (position, type) until position $C8 or 58 entries, then $FF $FF.

Second half of the wave-list builder $9F9B, which falls into $A000 (and branches to $A003 from $9FF5). $A003: for one group in four (a random 12-15 of 16) the group's alien type $5F is a sphere type from $9F97 (0, 2, 8 or 11) instead of a random 1-16. $A00E: $A070 re-randomises that type's record; if the type is 0, 2, 8 or 11 its firing mode (record byte $0E) is then set by the landscape X: 0, no shots, below landscape 4; 1, aimed, from 4; 3, the eight-way burst with the interval (byte $0F) doubled, from 6. $A046: writes up to $67 two-byte entries (landscape column $61, type $5F) from list offset $60, the column advancing by $5E, and jumps to $9FCB for the next group. $A068 ends the list with $FF $FF once the column reaches $C8 or the offset reaches $76.

Called by the wave builder ($A00E) for each group, type in $5F and landscape in X. It edits the type's shared 23-byte record at $3ECF[type] (pointer in $7B/$7C), so every alien of that type on every landscape uses whatever the latest group set. Fire interval (record byte $0F): $A12A[X] frames, or 10 once all eight levels have been completed ($B12A non-zero), doubled when the firing mode (byte $0E) is 3, the eight-way burst. For the falling and rising movers (byte $08 = 0 or 1): half the time it swaps falling for rising and mirrors the start line (byte $02) about line $82 ($104 minus it); 3 times in 16 it picks a new vertical acceleration (byte $09) of 16-79.

Reached by JMP from $9F82 (the end of $9F5F) while no level has been completed ($B129 = 0): gives the current landscape X ($B128) list number $9F8A[X] (kept in $B19D[X]) and fills that list ($B1A6) with the gentle opening wave: the 0,0 header, then eight type-1 aliens (molecules, which always leave a pearl) at landscape columns $32 to $86, 12 apart, then $FF $FF. So the HUD's alien count shows 08 when a game starts (reference/play-level1.png).

Four bytes, 01 02 03 01, that no instruction reads: the same values as the group-spacing table $9F93. Apparently a leftover. Searched: no instruction in the traced code names $A126-$A129, and no indexed table below it reaches that far.

Frames between an alien's shots, by landscape 0-8 (9 bytes): 70, 65, 50, 40, 37, 35, 33, 30, 25. $A084 copies the entry for the landscape a wave list is being built for into the alien type's record (byte $0F); the firing routine $A541 counts to it.

Police ships still to come in a filth raid. The cat's light-blue droplet sets 6 ($8933) and play start clears it ($805D). While it is non-zero, $A135 starts one ship every 16 frames and counts each one off.
Frame counter for a filth raid: $A135 increments it every frame and tries to start a police ship whenever its low four bits are 0, once every 16 frames.

Part of $A14A, placed before its entry and taken while police ships are queued ($A133 non-zero): every 16th frame ($A134) it starts one through $A181 and, if a slot was free (X is not $FC), counts it off $A133. The no-kill timer does not run while a raid is queued.

Once a frame from the frame loop ($645F). With police ships queued it runs $A135 instead. Otherwise $A1B7 counts frames and $A1B8 seconds (50 frames, PAL) since the player last killed an alien. When the seconds reach the level's limit $A1B9[$B128], a police ship is started by $A181, which also restarts the count. On the first frame of the second before, tune 5 starts through $45F1 with $B8F1 = 1: a warning, the same tune as a filth raid ($893D).

Restarts the no-kill timer, then starts a police ship in the first free slot: alien type 17 (record $40B5, frames $46-$49, a round craft with a flashing beacon; colour byte $86, blue with the siren bit). Its fire interval (record byte $0F) is set to $A1C1[$B128] (written at $A1B2) and it has no wave-list entry ($5E/$5F = 0); $A1B4 continues at $AA66. With all six slots busy it returns X = $FC and starts nothing. Called by $A135 (filth raid) and $A16B (no-kill time is up).

Frames (0-49) into the current second of the no-kill timer, counted by $A14A. Zeroed with $A1B8 on a kill ($A79C), on going through a tube ($81E0), at play start ($8054) and when a police ship starts ($A183).
Seconds since the player last killed an alien (police ships do not count), counted by $A14A and compared with $A1B9[$B128] to decide when to send a police ship.

Seconds without a kill before a police ship comes, by level 0-7: 45, 40, 25, 20, 20, 20, 15, 10. Read by $A168, and copied by $A78A into the SBC operand at $A795. Live on level 1 with no kill: the warning tune at 2,200 frames, the police ship at 2,250 (45 seconds).
Frames between a police ship's shots, by level 0-7: 40, 35, 30, 25, 20, 15, 10, 5. $A1AD reads the level's entry and $A1B2 writes it into type 17's record just before each ship starts.

Empties all six alien slots (line byte $02 = 0, the empty mark, and the hit box's Y limits $1F/$20 zeroed) and gives each one's wave-list entry back (bit 7 of its type byte cleared through $28/$29) so it can come again. Resets the list index $B1AE and turns sprites 2-7 off in the $D015 copy $E7D9. Called when a landscape is entered ($8264) and when a colour is complete ($64B9).

Once a frame, from play ($645C) and the bonus stage ($65C6): runs $A258 for each slot in use (line byte $02 non-zero); slot k is sprite k + 2, with the sprite's bit in $74, its inverse in $72, its number in $73 and twice its number in $75. An empty slot's sprite is switched off. Moves the scenery-test turn $B1B3 on one slot, runs the siren $A974, and when no alien sprite is on (bits 2-7 of $E7D9 clear) jumps to $9ECF, which recounts the landscape's aliens and starts a new wave when none are left.

One slot's frame, X = the slot's offset in $0200: hit and death handling $A7F2 (which does not come back here for a hit object), movement $A386, landscape scroll $A346, animation $A5B1, screen limits and scenery $A659, firing $A541, off-screen removal $A274, sprite registers $A29C, hit box $A744.

Frees an alien that has left the screen: X position (2-pixel units, byte $00) in $B6-$F9, 364-499 pixels, which lies off both edges since the 9-bit sprite position wraps. Unless it has been hit, its wave-list entry is given back (bit 7 cleared) so it appears again when the landscape scrolls back. Ends through $A9AF, which returns past the caller.

Copies a slot into its sprite's register copies: the X position in pixels (byte $00 times two plus the top bit of the fraction $01) into $E7C4 + $75 with the ninth bit in $E7D4 ($D010), line into $E7C5 + $75, colour into $E7EB + $73 ($D027 on), frame byte $24 into the pointer copy $B525 + $73, and the sprite's bit into $E7D9 ($D015). Colour: byte $10's low bits, or when they are $10 a cycle through $B87D (light green, light blue, white, yellow) every 5 frames, counted in bytes $09 and $13. Multicolour ($B1B2, the $D01C copy) unless byte $10 has bit 6 and the object is not hit. While byte $14 is 1, a 16-frame fade-in, hi-res: colours $B875 black, dark grey, grey, light grey.

Keeps an alien fixed to the landscape: moves its X by this frame's landscape scroll $B1FB (-2 to 2 pixels), subtracting $B285/$B282[$B1FB] when that is positive and adding $B28A/$B288[$B1FB + 2] when negative (2-pixel units, high byte then fraction). Skipped while the landscape is at an end and not scrolling ($B25D).

Moves an alien by its movement mode, byte $08. 0: falling, the Y speed $06/$07 grows by the acceleration $09 every frame; 1: rising, it shrinks by it; both then add the Y and X speeds ($06/$07, $04/$05) to the position. 2 and up: a pattern at ($0A/$0B), one byte per step, each step lasting $0C frames (counter $1C, index $1B; $FF loops to the start). Mode 2 adds or subtracts the speeds as the step's bits say (bit 0 adds the X speed, bit 1 subtracts it, bit 2 adds the Y speed, bit 3 subtracts it); mode 3 uses $04-$07 as accelerations on the velocity in $17-$1A, which then moves the alien, so it swoops in curves.

Alien firing: counts byte $21 up to the interval in byte $0F (an exact match, so 0 would mean every 256 frames), then fires by mode byte $0E. 0: never. 2: one shot in a direction that turns by 4 of 64 each time (byte $22). 3: eight shots, one every eighth of a turn. Any other (1): one shot aimed at the Wizball (direction $FF). Shots are started by $9BB5 (the alien bullets at $0300), then $A5A6 plays the shot sound.
Sound effect 6 through $4553 for an alien's shot, unless a bonus-stage message is up ($6733 non-zero).

Sets the alien's frame (byte $24), and notes police ships: any slot whose byte $10 has bit 7 sets $A9A7 for the siren. Animation mode, byte $11. 0: the frame is byte $12. 1: the bounce wobble: every 3 frames (5 with bit 7) the index $12 steps one towards 10, and the frame is ($13/$14)[$12]; the bounce routines set the index to 0 or 20, and the spheres' 21-frame table $40D0 squashes and settles back to round at 10. 2 and up: a frame list at ($13/$14), advanced every $12 frames (counter $23); $FF followed by n steps the pointer back n bytes.

Keeps an alien's line within $46-$C7: at $C8 or more it is put back to $C7, below $46 it is put at $47, and when byte $0D is below 2 it also bounces off the bottom ($A70D) or the top ($A707). Then the scenery test, for one slot a frame (the turn in $B1B3), only when byte $0D is non-zero and not in the bonus stage ($B874): $7C1D gives the screen address under the alien, and the eight characters at the offsets in $B3B6 (below, left, right, above, then the four corners) are tried in turn. The first one that is scenery (code $A0 or more) calls the pair of bounce routines for that probe from $B28C, through the JSR at $A6CB and the JMP at $A6DC.
Low byte of the JSR operand at $A6CB (zero in the image), written by $A6C2 from $B28C + 4 x probe: the first bounce routine for the scenery probe that touched, $A70D, $A6DF, $A6E5 or $A707.
High byte of the JSR operand at $A6CB, written by $A6C8 from $B28D + 4 x probe. After that call returns, $A6CE-$A6D9 fetch the second routine of the pair from $B28E/$B28F into the JMP at $A6DC.

Low byte of the JMP operand at $A6DC (zero in the image), written by $A6D3 from $B28E + 4 x probe: the second bounce routine, $A6DF or $A6E5 for a corner probe and $8404 (an RTS) for the four side probes.
High byte of the JMP operand at $A6DC, written by $A6D9 from $B28F + 4 x probe.

Scenery on the alien's left (probe 1 and the two left corners, through the $B28C table): if its X speed (bytes $04/$05) is negative it is reversed at $A6EA (both bytes EOR $FF, a ones' complement), and for the bounce-wobble animation (byte $11 = 1) the wobble restarts at index 0. Reached only through the rewritten JSR/JMP at $A6CB/$A6DC.

Scenery on the alien's right (probe 2 and the two right corners): if its X speed is zero or positive it is reversed as in $A6DF, restarting the wobble at 0. Reached only through the rewritten JSR/JMP at $A6CB/$A6DC.
The top line ($A67F) or scenery above (probe 3 and the top corners): if the alien is moving up (Y speed negative) the Y speed is reversed at $A712; otherwise nothing.

The bottom line ($A66C) or scenery below (probe 0 and the bottom corners): unless the alien is already moving up, $A712 reverses the Y speed (both bytes EOR $FF), and for the bounce-wobble animation restarts the wobble at index 20.

Zeroes movement mode, acceleration and both speeds (bytes $04-$09). Reached from $A6B6 when absolute $020D, slot 0's byte $0D rather than this slot's, is 2 or more; X then holds the probe number (0-7), not the slot, so the writes land in slot 0's bytes $04-$10 and $A258 carries on with the wrong X. No record in $3ECF or $39DC has byte $0D above 1, so the path appears never to be taken.

Sets the slot's hit box from its position: X from x - 3 to x + 7 (2-pixel units, 20 pixels) in bytes $1D/$1E, Y from line - 3 to line + $13 (22 lines) in $1F/$20. Bullets, the Wizball and the cat test points against these boxes in $6FBE.
The special-droplet counter: each colour sphere shot adds $A765[level] ($A7B5), and a threshold match adds 8 more ($A7D9). It wraps at 256.
$A763 with its low three bits cleared ($A7BB), compared with the five thresholds at $A76D-$A771.

How far each colour sphere shot moves the special-droplet counter, by level: 1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 8 for levels 0-6 at $A765-$A76B; level 7's step, 8, is the next byte, $A76C. Special droplets come more often on later levels.

$A76C is level 7's counter step (8); as threshold 0 it is never compared. $A76D-$A770 are thresholds 1-4 and $A771 threshold 5: random multiples of 8 written by $8086 at play start. When a sphere is shot and the counter's band $A764 equals threshold n (tried from 5 down to 1), its droplet takes colour $A771 + n.

$A771 is threshold 5 (random, from $8086); as colour entry 0 it is never used. $A772-$A776 are the colours of special droplets 1-5, each with its effect when the cat collects it ($8902): 1 white, bonus Wizball (a life); $0B dark grey, indestructacat; 0 black, freaky bits; 4 purple, mutant cat; $0E light blue, filth raid.

Hit handler, entered from $A7F2 with A = the state (byte $15). States 0 (alien), 1 (colour sphere), 6 (the bonus stage's Wizball lookalike) and 7 die now: unless it is a police ship (byte $10 = $86), $A787-$A7A5 restart the no-kill timer and count it off the landscape's remaining aliens $B1AF, which $9EFD redraws (at 0 a new wave and 1,000 points). States 2-5 are already dying and go straight on. Then $A7A9 and the dispatch at $A830.

Operand of the SBC #$00 at $A794, rewritten by $A78D with this level's limit $A1B9[$B128]. Unless the no-kill timer $A1B8 stands exactly one second short of the limit (its warning tune already started), $A79A-$A79F restart it; then $A7A2 counts the alien off $B1AF and $A7A5 redraws the count through $9EFD.

For a colour sphere (state 1): advances the special-droplet counter $A763 by $A765[level]; if its band $A764 matches threshold n at $A76D-$A771 (n from 5 down to 1), the droplet's colour (byte $10) becomes $A771 + n and the counter moves 8 on, past that threshold. Every state then goes on to $A830.
State 6, the bonus stage's Wizball lookalike (record 19 at $3BED, green) shot: sound effect $11 and an extra life for the current player ($B277 + $BFD9), then it explodes through $A891.

First step of $A258: nothing unless the hit flag (byte $25, set by $6FBE, or by the smart bomb $7394 for every slot) is on. An object in state $FF (bonus record 7 at $3AC7: grey, frame $71) shrugs it off: the flag is cleared, the landscape band's background flashes ($B25C = $0A, stepped by $8A44), its X speed is made positive and sound effect $0D plays. Any other state goes to $A777; its handler then runs every frame and drops $A258's return address, so a hit object no longer moves, animates or fires.

State 7 shot: lights the seventh icon ($B258 = 7, shields), sound effect $14, then dies like an alien ($A85B). No record in $3ECF or $39DC starts in state 7 and no instruction stores 7 in byte $15, so this appears unused.

Dispatch on the state in A: 6 to $A7E2, 7 to $A823, 4 to $A8AC (exploding), 1 to $A8D2 (sphere to droplet), 2 to $A8EC (droplet falling), 3 to $A925 (droplet splashing), 5 to $A95B (pearl); anything else, state 0, to $A85B (alien killed).

Aliens killed: $A85B counts every kill, stopping at 255, and the bonus-stage setup ($64A8) clears it, so it holds the bonus stage's kills; the score screen $6693 counts its display up to this, 40 points each.

Kills tallied so far on the bonus stage's score screen: $66E9 zeroes it and $6693 counts it up to $A858, one every second frame, each time adding 40 points and one to the displayed count at $B841-$B843.
Frame toggle for the bonus tally: $6693 increments it and tallies a kill only when it is even, every second frame.

An alien (state 0, or 7) dies: the kill count $A858 goes up (stopping at 255); a police ship (byte $10 bit 7) plays sound effect $0E and silences the siren ($A9A7 = 0). The ninth kill since the last pearl ($A9A9 reaching $A9AA), or any alien with bit 5 in byte $10 (type 1, the molecule), leaves a pearl ($A93C); otherwise sound effect 5 and the explosion ($A891).
Starts an explosion: adds the object's points (byte $16 x 10) through $710B, state 4, timer byte $12 = 0, the hit box's Y limits zeroed so nothing collides with it, frame $5F; falls into $A8AC.
State 4, exploding: every fourth frame the frame steps down, $5F, $5E, $5D, $5C (a spreading ring), and when it reaches $5B the slot is freed ($A9AF).

Common end of the hit-state handlers: $A8C3 first refreshes the hit box ($A744), then $A8C6 drops the return address into $A258 and runs only the off-screen check $A274, the scroll $A346 and the sprite update $A29C, returning to $A204's loop.
State 1 shot, a colour sphere: it becomes a droplet (state 2), sound effect 1, its points (byte $16 x 10) added, bytes $12 and $11 zeroed; falls into $A8EC.

State 2, a falling droplet: wobbles through the frames at $A9AB (a step every 4 frames), falls one line a frame and keeps a live hit box, so the cat can collect it ($88B5); the Wizball passes through. At line $CB it lands: state 3, frame $53.
State 3, a droplet splashing on the ground: every fourth frame the next frame, $53 to $5B, and the slot is freed when it reaches $5C. Its last hit box stays, but the cat collects only state 2.

The alien leaves a pearl: sound effect 2, its points (byte $16 x 10) added, the kill count $A9A9 restarted, state 5, frame $78, colour 5 (green, multicolour). The Wizball collects it for 100 points and the next icon ($7E63, $72AA).
State 5, a pearl: it stays where the alien died (only the landscape scroll moves it), drifting left a quarter unit a frame in the bonus stage ($B874 non-zero); its hit box follows it.
