Set by the screens that start a tune (2 at $8F6F, $6911, $6BC5, $6A8C...; 1 in play at $6569, $6974, $8938; 0 at $7DC0 for the explosion) and cleared by $45BD-$45C4, every frame from $6411, once voice 3's part of the tune has stopped ($5522 returns $5B = 0).

Music tempo: 0 = the music runs once a frame (band $B90C only), 1 = twice ($B8FC too), 2 = four times ($B903 and $B8F3 as well). The title, "get ready" and name-entry screens use 2 ($8F72, $690E, $6BC8); play uses 0 ($6979, $ADFC) and the bonus stage 1 or 0 ($6570).

Sound band present in every display list (the last one, raster line $FF, in the play list): re-enables interrupts (CLI) and, when the music tempo $B8F2 is 2, runs the music once more through $B925. With $B90C, $B8FC and $B903 it is the sound driver's clock, not a sprite multiplexer: the music runs 1, 2 or 4 times a frame.
Sound band (raster line $E5 in the play list): CLI, then one more run of the music ($B925) when the tempo $B8F2 is 1 or 2.
Sound band (raster line $3F in the play list): CLI, then one more run of the music ($B925) when the tempo $B8F2 is 2.

Main sound band, run once a frame near the top of every display list (raster line 1 in the play list, $16 on the other screens): CLI so later bands can interrupt it, steps the volume fade ($45D0), writes volume and filter mode ($45CF OR $B94D) to $D418, runs the sound effects on the voices the music leaves free ($B94E for all three when $B8F1 = 0, $B955 for voices 2 and 1 when $B8F1 = 1), then at $B925 the music: voice 3 only ($53D7, $4FD5, $4CB7) when $B8F1 = 1, all three ($50F4, $4D4E, $5269, $4E86 and those three) when 2; and $D418 again.

Filter-mode bits ORed with the volume into $D418 by $B913 and $B946: $70 (low, band and high pass) for the title tune $1A, $10 (low pass) for every other tune ($45F1); 0 once voice 3's part of the tune has stopped ($45C7).
Runs the sound effect of voice 3 (state at $0440, SID registers at $D40E) and falls into $B955 for voices 2 and 1: taken from $B91C when no music is playing ($B8F1 = 0).
Runs the sound effects of voice 2 (state at $0420, SID $D407) and, falling into $B960, voice 1 ($0400, $D400): called from $B922 when the music has voice 3 ($B8F1 = 1).

Plays one frame of the sound effect on one voice; X = the voice's state offset ($00, $20, $40 into $0400-$045F, 24 bytes loaded from an effect record by $4553), Y = its SID register offset (0, 7, $0E). On the first frame ($0406 = 0) it writes 0 to the control register. The frequency ($0407/$0408) and the pulse width ($040D/$040E) each sweep up by a step ($0409/$040A, $040F/$0410) for a number of frames ($040B, $0411) and down for another ($040C, $0412), direction flags $0413/$0415 and counters $0414/$0416. It writes attack/decay ($0405), sustain/release ($0417), frequency and pulse width to the SID, then the control byte $0404 with the gate on while the length $0402 or after it the tail count $0403 runs down, and 0 when both are spent. While $0402 is non-zero the voice is busy: $4592 lets a new effect take it only if the new priority byte is not greater than the playing one's (smaller numbers win).
RTS that ends $B960; its address is also the base of LDA $BA7A,X at $458E, where X is an effect's voice number 1-3, reading the voice offsets that follow.

Offset of each voice's effect state in $0400-$045F for voices 1-3: $00, $20, $40 ($BA7B-$BA7D). $BA7E-$BA80 (0, 7, $0E, the SID register offsets of the three voices) would be read for voice numbers 4-6, which no effect record has; $B94E-$B95E use immediate values instead.

Firing volume, 0-15 ($0A in the image): $BA82 raises it with the up-arrow key and lowers it with =, and writes it times 16 into byte 23 (the sustain level) of the two firing effects, $3C76 (effect 0) and $3DF6 (effect 16).

Firing volume keys, called every frame of play from $7E5D: key code 5 (up-arrow) raises $BA81 up to 15, code 6 (=) lowers it to 0, and the value times 16 goes into the sustain nibble of both firing sound records ($3C76, $3DF6).

Silences the SID: writes 0 to $D400-$D416 (STA $D3FF,X with X = $17 down to 1) and to the length and release counters of the three effect voices ($0402/$0403, $0422/$0423, $0442/$0443). Called before a life ($63AC), "get ready" ($6901) and game over ($6A84).

Sound effect table: the address of each effect's 24-byte record, one word per effect number ($BACA-$BB01), read by $457F/$4584 with Y = 2 x effect. Effects 0-25 point at $3C5F-$3EB7 (10 and 11 are both $3D67); the last two words, $3ECF and $3EE7, continue the spacing into other data and are never requested. A record: voice 1-3, priority, length, release, control, attack/decay, 0, frequency, frequency step, sweep up and down times, pulse width, pulse step, pulse sweep times, direction flags and counters, sustain/release; $4553 copies it (25 bytes) to the voice's state at $0400 if the voice is free (length $0402 = 0) or the new priority byte is not greater than the one playing (smaller numbers win; the firing sound, effect 0, has 14).
High-byte column of $BACA (LDA $BACB,Y at $4584); the span holds the rest of the 28 words.

Effect number last passed to $4553 ($4569); $45A1 retries effect 0 as effect 16 when its voice is busy. The tube arrival at $82B3-$833F borrows it as the byte offset (steps of 3, one sprite row) of the Wizball image sliding into the sprite blocks at $ED00 and $ED80.
Toggles bit 4 on each request of effect 0 ($456E): with no music ($B8F1 = 0) the firing sound alternates between effect 0 on voice 1 and effect 16 on voice 3; with music it is always effect 0.

Constant $39, never written: the byte that marks a loop record in the bonus wave script ($9CF5 compares the record's second byte with it). A loop record is (target, $39, count): while the count is non-zero it is decremented and the script goes on at offset target - 2, so the loop runs count more times.
Frames already waited on the current record of the bonus wave script, counted up to the record's delay byte at $9D66-$9D71.

Offset of the current record in the bonus wave script at $ED02 (copied from $3902 by $9CB2, which clears it); $9CEF-$9D77 step it through spawn records (template, delay), loop records, $FF/$FE (fly on/off, $B1F8) and $FD (end: $B1CF = $36).

The BOREWIZ cheat: $AFBF sets it to 7, and the border to brown (9), when the seven keys B O R E W I Z (codes at $AFCE) are typed in a row on the title or menu screen ($AF85). While it is set, a collision does not end the life ($7EF4), except in the bonus stage. Cleared at game over ($6B6B) and on quitting ($6EDC). $BB08-$BB0A (1, 2, 3) are not read; $BB0B (4) is the column byte of the stale text record below.

Alternates 2 and 0 each time a bonus stage starts ($655F, EOR #2): at 2 the stage plays tune $0C on all three voices at double tempo, at 0 tune $21 on voice 3 only. The Wiz-lab after it has its music (tune $3D) only while it is 2 ($AB66). It sits where the row byte of the stale text record would be.

Stale text that nothing reads: an earlier draft of part of Wiztips page three, left in memory and cut off by the code at $BBA0. From its header at $BB0B (column 4, row byte now the variable $BB0C): "the horizon gives", (7,13) "immunity to alien bullets", (0,15) "after a colour is complete, you can make", (1,16) "a weapon permanent. just select the one", (3,17) "you want, whil". The live page at $4451 reads "hiding beneath the horizon gives" and misspells "permenant". The only pointer-shaped reference, the bytes $0D $BB at $6390 after the entry's JMP $EC00, is never read.

High-score insertion after a game (through $BFD0, from $6BB0): writes side 1's six score digits (+ "0") into the spare entry 8 of its table (the one-player table, or the team table at +$7E when $BFD6 = 2) with the marker "1" as the first name letter, and sorts both tables ($BC23); does the same for side 2 with "2" when two sides played; then sets $BDA5 to the table whose top entry is higher and works out the rank codes $BFF2/$BFF3 ($BC90).

Sorts one high-score table by score, highest first: $67 = 0 for the one-player table (entries 0-8), 9 for the team table (9-17). Compares the six digits of each entry with the next and swaps the two 14-byte entries when the next is higher, restarting from the top after every swap (a bubble sort); equal scores keep their order, so a new entry stays below an old one.

Part of $BC90 (reached from $BCAF): the marker "2" was found at position Y of the team table. Rank code 3 ($BFF3) for position 0 when the team table holds the best score, else 4 for positions 0-6, and for position 7 only when the team table holds the best score.

Finds where the markers "1" and "2" landed in the top eight positions of both tables and sets the rank codes $BFF2 (side 1) and $BFF3 (side 2): 1 = the best score of both tables, in the one-player table; 2 = another place in it; 3 and 4 = the same in the team table; 0 = not placed. Position 0 counts as best only in the table named by $BDA5; position 7 qualifies only when that table is the best one.

Stores a typed name (through $BFD3, from $6CB9, with the marker "1" or "2" in A): finds the entry whose first name letter is the marker, stepping 14 bytes at a time, copies the seven name characters from the buffer $BFF4 over it, then rebuilds the title's score lines: the best score into "1. " ($BD96) and six entries per column into the page $BEB5 ($BD78), each table starting one entry lower when it holds the best score.

Copies six 14-byte entries, from table offset Y, into six rows of one column of the high-score page (X = 0 for the left column at $BEDF, $14 for the right one), skipping the 26 bytes of each row's end, next header and "N. " prefix between them.
Copies the six score digits of the entry at table offset Y into the title's "1. " line at $BFEB-$BFF0.

Which table holds the best score: 1 = the one-player table, 2 = the team table ($BC1C, from comparing the two top entries at $BC05); 0 in the image, where the title page is already built. Decides which top entry is shown as "1." and which tables' ranks start one lower.
Offsets of the 14-byte high-score entries: 0, $0E, $1C ... $FC, nineteen multiples of 14 ($BDA6-$BDB8), indexed by position at $BC29, $BC4D and $BC98 (the last two, $EE and $FC, are not reached).

The two high-score tables, eighteen entries of 14 PETSCII bytes: six score digits, a space, a seven-letter name. Entries 0-8 ($BDB9-$BE34) are the one-player table and 9-17 ($BE37-$BEB4) the team table; entry 8 and entry 17 are the spare slots new scores go into. In the image: "020000 JOP    ", seven "020000 ---    ", "000000 ---    "; then "050000 --- ---", "020000 KRX NIF", six "020000 --- ---", "000000 --- ---". Not saved anywhere. This span: entry 0's score and space.
Entry 0's name ($BDC0-$BDC6, "JOP    "), and the base of $BDC0,X for the name of the entry at offset X: the marker test at $BC9B and $BD36 and the name store at $BD49.
Entries 1-7 of the one-player table ($BDC7-$BE28), and the base of $BDC7,X at $BC31, $BC56 and $BC5D: the entry after the one at offset X, which the sort compares and swaps with it.
Entry 8, the spare slot of the one-player table: $BBB3 writes a new score here (STA $BE29,X, also reaching entry 17 at +$7E) before sorting.
Rest of entry 8, and the base of STA $BE2A,X at $BBBE/$BBF4: with X already advanced by six, that stores the marker in entry 8's (or 17's) first name letter.
Entry 9, the top of the team table ("050000 --- ---" in the image, the best score of both at load): its score and space, compared with entry 0 at $BC0A to set $BDA5.
Entry 9's name and entries 10-17 of the team table ($BE3E-$BEB4); also the base of LDA $BE3E,X at $BCA6, the name of the team entry at offset X, tested for the markers.

Text page of the high-score table, printed in the normal font by $8F95-$8F9D through $BFFE: (14,5) "top  scores", (2,12) "one  plr", (27,12) "two  plrs", then rows 14, 16 ... 24 with the one-player entries at column 0 and the team entries at column 23, each "N. " and a 14-byte entry, ranks 2-7. $BD78 rewrites the entries in place.

The entry part of the first left row ("020000 JOP    ") and the rest of the page to its closing $FF at $BFCA; the base of STA $BEDF,X at $BD83. Rows are 40 bytes apart, the right column 20 bytes on. $BFCB-$BFCF after the page ("00 -0") are not read.
Jump to $BBA0 (insert the scores, sort, rank), called at game over from $6BB0; with $BFD3 a two-entry jump table into the high-score code.
Jump to $BD32 (store a typed name), reached by JMP $BFD3 from $6CB9 with the marker in A.
Low byte ($32) of the JMP at $BFD3, and the base of $BFD4,X at $7113-$71BD with X = 7 or 14 ($71DA by side): the first (100,000s) digit of a side's score, $BFDB or $BFE2.
High byte ($BD) of the JMP at $BFD3, and the base of LDA $BFD5,X/Y (index 1-4) at $68C2, $6980 and $6A29, which reaches the side flags $BFD6-$BFD9.

Side 1 plays alone (1) or as a Wiz-and-cat team (2), from $B2AC at $6889. $BBA2 picks its high-score table and $697D its joystick routing. Also the base of $BFD6,X (the thousands digit) in the score adder $711C.
Side 2 plays alone (1) or as a team (2), from $B2AC. Also the base of $BFD7,X (the hundreds digit) in the score adder $7128/$7146.

Number of sides taking turns, 1 or 2, from $B2AC: $6B2D swaps sides after a lost life only when it is 2, and $BBCF enters side 2's score only then. Also the base of $BFD8,X (the tens digit) in the score adder $7131-$7143.

Side now playing, 1 or 2: set to 1 at $687B, swapped at $6B41 (EOR #3) when the other side still has lives. Indexes the lives ($B277,X), the score ($71D9 -> $BFD4,X), the score row positions ($71DB-$71DF) and the per-player block copies ($6E38, $6E45). Also the base of $BFD9,X/Y: $70D7 clears $BFDA-$BFE7 for a new game, and $714D tests the overflow digit.

Millions digit of side 1's score: $7146 carries into it; when it is non-zero $714D-$715F sets the six digits to 999999 and it back to 0. Also the base of LDA $BFDA,Y at $7192, which shows the score digits.

Side 1's score, six digits 0-9, the 100,000s first ($BFDB-$BFE0); the last digit is never touched, so scores are multiples of 10. $710B adds A x 10 points; a change of the first digit is an extra Wizball ($71BB). $7190 shows it at the top left of the landscape screen; $BBAD enters it in the tables.
Millions digit of side 2's score (see $BFDA), and the base of LDA $BFE1,Y at $719B, which shows side 2's digits.
Side 2's score, six digits, the 100,000s first ($BFE2-$BFE7), shown at the top right ($71A1) and entered in the tables by $BBE3.

String "1. 050000" and $FF, the best score as the title shows it: $8FC7-$8FCF draws it in the normal font into sprite blocks $85-$87 (pointer $B7DC), shown at $B57B's positions; $BD96 rewrites the six digits.
The space of "1. 050000", and the base of LDA $BFEA,Y at $70DF: with Y = 6 down to 1 $70D3 converts the six digits into the HI score shown in play ($71D4-$71D9).
The six digits of the best score in "1. 050000" ($BFEB-$BFF0, PETSCII), written by $BD9B; then the string's $FF.

Side 1's high-score rank code from $BC90: 0 none, 1 best in the one-player table, 2 placed there, 3 best in the team table, 4 placed there. $6BB3 skips the name entry when both codes are 0; an odd code also asks for the "few words" ($6C8D).
Side 2's rank code, as $BFF2; also the base of STA $BFF3,Y at $6C30, $6C4E and $6C70 (index 1-10), which writes the name buffer $BFF4.

Name-entry buffer, ten PETSCII bytes ($BFF4-$BFFD). It holds "POO BAG   " in the loaded image, a leftover that is never shown: $6C2C fills it with spaces before every name entry, the typed initials go to $BFF4-$BFF6 (and a team's cat player's to $BFF8-$BFFA), and only $BD46 reads it, copying seven bytes ("POO BAG" is exactly seven) into a table entry.
Fourth byte of the name buffer (the space between a team's two sets of initials), and the base of STA $BFF7,Y at $6C87 (Y = 3..1): the cat player's initials at $BFF8-$BFFA; $BFFB-$BFFD stay spaces.
Pointer to the high-score page $BEB5, low byte (LDX $BFFE at $8F95).
High byte of the pointer to $BEB5 (LDY $BFFF at $8F98).

Sprite shapes 0-4 (pointers $00-$04 in VIC bank 3, $C000-$C13F), multicolour, icon-bar icons in their boxes: 0 shield (the yin-yang sphere), 1 smart bomb, 2 catelite (the cat's face), 3 anti-grav, 4 double. Matched against the Wiztips page one legend (reference/wiztips-one.png) and borne out by the code: $720B loads the bar's pointers $EFF8-$EFFF from $B4DE (07 0B 02 06 08 01 00 00), taking icon 1 turns 7 into 3 and then 9 ($7379), icon 2 turns $0B into 4 and then 9 ($734B-$7362), icon 3 turns 2 into 9 ($7366).

Sprite shape 5 ($C140-$C17F), all zero in the image: the game's empty sprite. Pointer 5 hides a sprite ($7220, $859D and $AADE put 5 in $B8DE/$B8DF), and $7230 clears it at the start of play ($8F15 with Y = 5). The player menu borrows it for its star field: $9034 clears it, $903D puts a two-pixel dot in it ($C161), and $9055-$905E point all eight sprites at it.

Byte 33 of sprite 5 (row 11, left byte). $903D writes $C0 here, the only write found: a two-pixel dot for the player menu's stars. It stays there until $7230 clears sprite 5 when play starts (yeti-title.vsf has $C0 here, play-start.vsf 0).

Sprite shapes 6-11 ($C180-$C2FF), more icon-bar icons: 6 blazers, 7 thrust, 8 wiz spray, 9 an arrow in a dark box, 10 cat spray, 11 beam. 9 marks a slot that cannot be taken: used up ($738E after anti-grav, $7360 after double) or in use ($736B while the catelite is out, $73CE while a shield is on); the Wiz-lab refuses a slot showing 9 ($B0A7). Icon 5 switches between 8 and 10 as the spray passes between Wiz and Cat ($7325-$734A).
Sprite shape 12 ($C300-$C33F): a ring, drawn in multicolour. The 'get ready!' screen points all eight sprites at it ($68F4-$68FE) for the rings that circle the words.

Sprite shapes 13-15 ($C340-$C3FF): the catelite, a round cat's face with big eyes, in three animation frames. $87E6 sets sprite 1's pointer ($B526) to $0D + $B268, $B268 counting 0-2 every fourth call; sprite 1 is the catelite, hidden while $B234 is 0 ($8640).

Sprite shapes 16-31 ($C400-$C7FF): the Wizball, a patterned ball, in 16 rotation frames. $80DA sets sprite 0's pointer ($B525) to $10 + $B21A, $B21A being the spin frame 0-15; $81E9 copies the frame in use into sprite $B4 ($ED00) when the ball goes down at glyph $BE ($81C9).

Sprite shapes 32-47 ($C800-$CBFF): the first 16 of the 24 frames in which a Wizball appears or vanishes, the ball's pattern thinning into rings that flatten into an ellipse and then a line. $8031 sets $B21A = $10 + $B214, so the pointer is $20 + $B214: $B214 counts down from 23 to 0 as the ball appears ($8008) and up from 0 to 23 as it goes ($8022); sprite 32 is the frame next to the whole ball.

Sprite shapes 48-55 ($CC00-$CDFE): the last 8 of the 24 appear/vanish frames, a short line at eight angles (pointer $20 + $B214 for $B214 = 16-23). 55 is the first frame shown when a Wizball arrives ($8045 sets $B214 = $17) and the last when one leaves.
Padding byte of sprite 55, and the base of LDA $CDFF,Y with Y from $40 down to 1 at $7781 and $9DEB, which copy sprite 56 (the empty cauldron, $CE00-$CE3F) into the cauldron sprites at $EE40-$EF3F.

Sprite shape 56 ($CE00-$CE3F): an empty cauldron, drawn in multicolour. $9DE9 copies it into sprites $B9-$BC ($EE40-$EF3F), the four cauldrons at the bottom of the play screen, and $777F into $BC alone; $9EB3 reads it a row at a time (this is the base of LDA $CE00,Y) to redraw the part of a cauldron above its fill level.
Byte 1 of the empty cauldron's first row; base of LDA $CE01,Y at $9EB9, the middle byte of each cauldron row that $9EB3-$9EC4 copies.
Byte 2 of the empty cauldron's first row, and the rest of that shape to $CE3F; base of LDA $CE02,Y at $9EBF, the right-hand byte of each cauldron row that $9EB3-$9EC4 copies.

Sprite shape 57 ($CE40-$CE7E): the same cauldron full of liquid. $9EB3-$9EC4 takes a cauldron row from here (index + $40) instead of from sprite 56 when the row lies below the fill level, so each cauldron fills from the bottom up. Its top row's middle byte ($CE41 = $AA) is the value $9E26 later finds at $EF01.

Padding byte of sprite 57 (value $12), and the base of LDA $CE7F,X at $831D with X from 0 to $3F: $830A copies $CE7F-$CEBE, this byte and the first 63 of sprite 58, into sprite $B4, so the pipe it draws starts one byte early (see $CE80).

Sprite shape 58 ($CE80-$CEBE): the left half of a curved pipe, blue, white and red. $830A copies it with sprite 59 into sprites $B4 and $B6 ($ED00, $ED80), three bytes (one row) further down on each of 21 calls, so the pipe slides down; its top row is left behind each time and draws a trail above it. The copy reads from $CE7F with X starting at 0, so every byte lands one place late: whether the data was drawn for that or the index is a slip is unknown.
Padding byte of sprite 58 (value $13), and the base of LDA $CEBF,X at $8323 (X 0-$3F), which copies $CEBF-$CEFE into sprite $B6 ($ED80) the same way $CE7F feeds sprite $B4.
Sprite shape 59 ($CEC0-$CEFE): the right half of the curved pipe, continuing sprite 58; $830A copies it into sprite $B6 ($ED80).

Sprite shapes 60-63 ($CF00-$CFFE), multicolour: three arrow-shaped craft pointing right (60-62, small differences between them) and a diamond with an eye in the middle (63). No code was found that points a sprite at 60-63: $85C7 reaches $3E/$3F only for $B8DC = 0, which it never has there, and the aliens' pointers in $0224,X were not traced to these values. Use unknown.

Padding byte of sprite 63, and the base of STA $CFFF,X/Y with the index counting down to 1, which writes the VIC-II sprite position registers $D000-$D00F: $89C0 (X 8-1, from $B4C6), $8B69 (X 6-1, from $B505), $924E (Y 10-1, from $B571), $92DD (Y 6-1, from $B57B). Not a variable.

The 1 KB block $E000-$E3FF, all written at run time. Title: sprites $80-$8E, built by $8F61: $80-$84 the WIZBALL logo in the large font ($8E32), $85-$8B cleared and '1. 050000' drawn into them in the small font ($8DE4), $8C-$8E filled with $FF, solid bars that the band at $9327 shows expanded behind the text. Play: rows 0-1 are the score line, always shown from here (the band at $8A52 sets D018 = $8C), and the rows below are the first of three play-area buffers ($B1FD = 0). $7C54 clears $E000-$E0FF on every pass of the outer cycle ($63A3 calls $63CA before each get-ready screen). The entry image already holds the built title sprites.

Base of STA $E00B,Y (Y 16-1) at $B020 and $B0F0: 16 characters at row 0, columns 12-27 of the score line, 'select permenant' ($B02F) when the Wiz-lab opens and 'all systems go!!' ($B0FC) when it closes.
Base of STA $E027,Y (Y 6-1) at $7198: player 1's six score digits ($BFDB-$BFE0 plus $30) go to row 1, columns 0-5 ($E028-$E02D).

Row 1, column 0 of the score line; base of indexed writes into that row: $7D70 (X 7 or 32 from $71E0/$71E1) puts the lives digit, $2F plus the player's count at $B278/$B279 (capped at 10), next to each score; $9F0C-$9F1E (Y 9 or 29 from $71DE/$71DF) put the tens digit of the count in $B1AF.
Base of STA $E029,Y at $9F28: the units digit of $B1AF, one column right of the tens digit written through $E028 (row 1, columns 10 or 30).

Base of STA $E033,Y (Y 16-1) at $B028 and $B0F5: row 1, columns 12-27 of the score line, 'weapon' centred under 'select permenant' ($B03F-$B04E) for the Wiz-lab, then cleared to glyph 0 (blank) by $B0F5.
Base of STA $E038,Y (Y 6-1) at $71AF: the high score's six digits (from $71D4-$71D9) go to row 1, columns 17-22 ($E039-$E03E); skipped while $AC4E is non-zero.
Base of STA $E049,Y (Y 6-1) at $71A1: player 2's six score digits ($BFE2-$BFE7 plus $30) go to row 1, columns 34-39 ($E04A-$E04F).
Last byte of row 23 of the $E000 buffer; base of the Y 24-1 copies between $B116-$B12D and player 1's save area $E3C0-$E3D7 (STA $E3BF,Y at $6E0D, LDA $E3BF,Y at $6E22).

Player 1's copy of the 24-byte per-player block $B116-$B12D ($E3C0-$E3D7), for games where players take turns: $6E08 saves it (at the start, $686B, and through $6E38 at $63C1 when $BFD9 = 1) and $6E20 restores it (through $6E42 at $63A0, and at $6B5D). It sits in row 24 of the $E000 buffer, which play never shows.
Last byte of player 1's save area, and the base of the Y 24-1 copies for player 2 (STA $E3D7,Y at $6E19, LDA $E3D7,Y at $6E2E).
Player 2's copy of the per-player block $B116-$B12D ($E3D8-$E3EF): $6E14 saves it ($686E, and $6E38 when $BFD9 is not 1), $6E2C restores it ($6B75, and $6E42). $E3F0-$E3F7 after it are not used.

The eight sprite pointers of the screen at $E000 ($E3F8-$E3FF), used while $E000 is the play buffer on show. The play bands write sprite 0's pointer at $8A8E and $8A91 (from $B8DE), $8B18 (from $B525) and $8B3C (from $B8DF), and sprites 1-7's at $8AFE (from $B526-$B52C); $8A5D-$8A6D rewrite those operands' high bytes to $E3, $E7 or $EB for the buffer in use, except $8A91's, which always writes here.

The 1 KB block $E400-$E7FF: the second play-area buffer ($B1FD = $10), written at run time ($7C57 clears $E400-$E4FF on every pass of the outer cycle, the scrolling code draws the landscape rows). Its hidden rows 23-24 and spare bytes hold variables ($E79A-$E7AD, $E7C3-$E7F2) and $E7F8-$E7FF are its sprite pointers. The entry image holds a leftover landscape screen here.

Row 23, column 1 of the $E400 buffer, not used as a screen cell; the base of indexed accesses to the column at $E79A: STA $E799,X at $766F (X 20-1, clears all of it when $B874 is set) and LDA/STA $E799,X at $79C5-$79CB (X 5-1, its first five rows).

The next screen column to scroll in: 20 glyph codes for rows 3-22 in four groups of five ($E79A rows 3-7, $E79F rows 8-12, $E7A4 rows 13-17, $E7A9 rows 18-22). $78CF-$7977 fills it from four 5 x 5 scenery tiles (at $2642 + 25 x tile number, read from the level map through $0460/$0470), $7978-$7A39 puts star-field glyphs into the cells left empty, and $7A3A/$7A40 copy it into column 39 or column 0 of the buffer being drawn ($7A75-$7A95).
Screen row 4 of the scroll column; base of STA $E79B,X at $7951 (the tile byte at offset 5, X = 0, 5, 10 or 15 for the four tiles).
Screen row 5 of the scroll column; base of STA $E79C,X at $7958 (tile offset 10).
Screen row 6 of the scroll column; base of STA $E79D,X at $795F (tile offset 15).
Screen row 7 of the scroll column; base of STA $E79E,X at $7966 (tile offset 20) and of LDA/STA $E79E,X at $79E6-$79EC (X 5-1, the second group, rows 8-12).
Screen row 8, the first of the scroll column's second group ($E79F-$E7A3); LDA $E79F,Y at $7A7B copies the group to the screen.
Screen row 12 of the scroll column; base of LDA/STA $E7A3,X at $7A07-$7A0D (X 5-1, the third group, rows 13-17).
Screen row 13, the first of the scroll column's third group ($E7A4-$E7A8); LDA $E7A4,Y at $7A81 copies it.
Screen row 17 of the scroll column; base of LDA/STA $E7A8,X at $7A28-$7A2E (X 5-1, the fourth group, rows 18-22).
Screen row 18, the first of the scroll column's fourth group ($E7A9-$E7AD, the bottom five rows); LDA $E7A9,Y at $7A87 copies it.

Byte before the VIC-II register shadow at $E7C4; base of STA $E7C3,X/Y with the index counting down to 1: $6A4C and $AE64 (X 8-1, sprite 0-3 positions from $B4E5-$B4EC) and $7CE8 (Y $11-1, clears $E7C4-$E7D4).

Start of a shadow copy of the VIC-II registers $D000-$D02E ($E7C4-$E7F2, same order), kept in the hidden rows of the $E400 buffer: game code writes sprite state here and the play-area bands copy it to the chip ($8A52-$8B21). This byte is sprite 0's X, the Wizball ($D000, copied at $8A73).

Shadow of $D001, sprite 0's Y. The band at $8A52 uses it less 23 for the sprite drawn above the Wizball, $8B0F uses it as is, and $8ABB-$8AD9 derive from it the raster lines of the next two bands ($B3F6 = Y - 2, $B3FA = Y + 20).
Shadow of $D002, sprite 1's X: the catelite ($87C0 writes it).
Shadow of $D003, sprite 1's Y; $8645 sets it to 0 (off screen) while there is no catelite ($B234 = 0).
Shadow of $D004, sprite 2's X.
Shadow of $D005, sprite 2's Y.
Shadow of $D006, sprite 3's X; $82E4 and $ACF4 count it down to move that sprite left.
Shadow of $D007, sprite 3's Y; also the base of $E7CB,X (X 8-1) for sprites 4-7's positions $E7CC-$E7D3: read at $8AE4, written at $6A52 and $AE6A.
Shadow of $D008, sprite 4's X.
Shadow of $D009, sprite 4's Y; sprites 5-7's X and Y follow at $E7CE-$E7D3.
Shadow of $D010, the ninth bit of every sprite's X; copied at $8A7F, updated per sprite at $A29C-$A2B7 and $87C3-$87CA.

Shadow of $D015, which sprites are on; copied to the chip by $8A57 for the play area. The most-written byte of the shadow (about 30 places): 3 for the Wizball and catelite alone, bits set and cleared as aliens come and go.
Shadow of $D017, sprite Y expansion; ORed with $B1B1 and copied at $8AA0.
Shadow of $D01B, sprite priority; copied at $8AB5. $803C sets it to 1, putting sprite 0 behind the landscape while a Wizball appears or vanishes; also written at $7FF1.
Shadow position of $D01C, sprite multicolour. $80D7 writes 1 here, but the play bands take $D01C from $B1B2 instead and nothing was found that reads this byte.
Shadow of $D025, sprite multicolour 0; $6403 sets $0B (dark grey) when play starts; copied at $8A94.

Shadow of $D026, sprite multicolour 1; $6408 sets $0D (light green). Also the base of $E7EA,X/Y (1-8) for the eight sprite colours $E7EB-$E7F2: $8AEA copies them, $6A58 and $AE70 load them from $B4F5, $B151 sets all eight to one colour from $B61C.
Shadow of $D027, sprite 0's colour, the Wizball's (5, green, in play-start.vsf); $8B1B copies it in the band where sprite 0 is the Wizball.
Shadow of $D028, sprite 1's colour, the catelite's: 5 (green), cycling through $B5DF while $B26C is 8 ($87EF-$8807).
Shadow of $D029, sprite 2's colour; $6AAE fills $E7ED-$E7F2 with the colour at $EBD7.
Shadow of $D02A, sprite 3's colour.
Shadow of $D02B, sprite 4's colour; sprites 5-7's colours follow at $E7F0-$E7F2, the end of the shadow.

Sprite $A0 ($E800-$E83F), the level number at the bottom left of the play screen (bottom-band pointer $F7F8 = $A0), in the hidden top rows of the third play buffer ($E800-$EBFF, $B1FD = $20). $776D clears it ($8F15 with Y = $A0) and $770D draws the digit: each pixel of the small font's '1' + level ($F188 + 8 x $B128) becomes three pixels from the table at $76E9, and each row is written twice. $7C5A also clears $E800-$E8FF on every pass of the outer cycle. The entry image holds an 8 drawn this way.
Byte 1 of the level-digit sprite's first row; base of ORA/STA $E801,X at $773B-$773E, the middle byte of each digit row.
Byte 2 of the level-digit sprite's first row; base of ORA/STA $E802,X at $7747-$774A, the right-hand byte of each digit row.
Byte 0 of the level-digit sprite's second row; base of STA $E803,X at $7735, which repeats each left-hand byte one row lower.
Byte 1 of the level-digit sprite's second row; base of STA $E804,X at $7741 (the repeated middle byte).
Byte 2 of the level-digit sprite's second row; base of STA $E805,X at $774D (the repeated right-hand byte).

The player menu's four moving stars, 6 bytes each ($EB9A-$EBB1, X = 0, 6, 12, 18): +0 X, +1 X fraction, +2 Y, +3 Y fraction, +4 X speed, +5 Y speed. $90BD starts a free star at a random X ($24-$A3) on line $91 with random speeds of at least $20; $910A adds twice each speed to the 16-bit position and frees the star (X = 0) when X < $0C or X >= $AC, or Y < $7A or Y >= $FA (CMP and BPL tests at $9146-$9156); $915F and $9163 show each star on sprites mirrored left-right and top-bottom. Lives in the hidden rows of the third play buffer. This byte is star 0's X; 0 means free.
Star 0's X fraction; base of ADC/STA $EB9B,X at $9115-$9118 for every star.
Star 0's Y (a new star starts at $91, $90D0); base of $EB9C,X for every star's Y at $90E6, $913D-$9143, $9151, $9180 and $9189.
Star 0's Y fraction; base of ADC/STA $EB9D,X at $9133-$9136.
Star 0's X speed, random with bit 5 set ($90D8); read by $910E.
Star 0's Y speed, random with bit 5 set ($90E0); read by $912C. Stars 1-3 follow at $EBA0-$EBB1.
Last byte of star 3's record, and the base of STA $EBB1,X at $8FA4 (X $42-1), which clears $EBB2-$EBF3, the title's colour-cycling state, when the title starts.
Frame divider for the logo's colour bar: $9884 counts it to 2, then moves the 16 colours at $EBC1-$EBD0 one place outwards and steps $EBC0.
Frame divider (to 3) for the colour list at $EBD7-$EBE3, which $98BE moves on when it wraps.
Frame divider (to 3) for the colour list at $EBE4-$EBF0, which $98E9 moves on when it wraps.
Frame divider (to 3) for the four colours at $EBD2-$EBD5, which $9916 moves on when it wraps. $EBB6 after it is cleared with the rest and otherwise unused.
Step counter for the list at $EBE4: $98E9 takes the new colour from $B5CB + (counter AND 7) and stores it at $EBF0.
Step counter for the list at $EBD7: $98BE takes the new colour from $B5DF + (counter AND 7); its low two bits also pick the background colours that $9805 and $9812 write (tables at $9821 and $9825).
Step counter whose low two bits pick $EBD1 from $B5EF ($994A) and $EBD6 from $B5F3 ($996A).
Frame divider (to 7) for $EBB9, stepped by $994A; $996A acts only when it is 0.
Step counter 0-7 for the four colours at $EBD2: $9916 takes the new colour from $B5E7 + counter and stores it at $EBD5.
Frame divider (to 4) for $EBBD, stepped by $997D.
Step counter: $997D sets $EBF1 from $B5DF + (counter AND 7).
Frame divider (to 4) for $EBBF, stepped by $999D.
Step counter: $999D sets $EBF2 from $B5CB + (counter AND 7).

Step counter of the logo colour bar ($98AA): bits 1-5 pick the new colour from $B5FB for $EBC9 and $EBCA. Also the base of LDA $EBC0,X at $9271 (X 16-1), which sets the colour of the five logo sprites from the bar, one raster line at a time from line $3E.

The logo's colour bar, 16 colours ($EBC1-$EBD0), one per raster line of the WIZBALL sprites: every other frame $9884 moves each half one place outwards, the new colour entering in the middle ($EBC9-$EBCA). This is the first colour and the base of STA $EBC1,Y at $989B.
Second colour of the logo bar; base of LDA $EBC2,Y at $9898 and STA $EBC2,X at $98A1, the two halves of the move.
Colour 9 of the logo bar, the middle, where $98B7 stores each new colour from $B5FB.
Colour 10 of the logo bar, given the same new colour as $EBC9 at $98BA.

Background colour of the title's logo band: $922C writes it to $D021; also used at $6DF9 and $97D7; $994A sets it from $B5EF. Also the base of LDA $EBD1,X at $9303 (X 4-1) for the four colours that follow.

Four colours ($EBD2-$EBD5) that shift one place every third frame ($9916), the new one from $B5E7 entering at $EBD5: $9303 gives them, a line pair each from line $76, to the '1. 050000' sprites; $EBD2 alone is a background colour at $6DD5, $96AA, $9703, $97B1, $97C2, $97F0 and $97FC.
Second of the four colours at $EBD2; base of LDA $EBD3,Y at $9928 for the shift.
Last of the four colours at $EBD2; $9946 stores each new one here.

A colour that $996A picks from $B5F3; background at $9320, $9419 and $6DEB. Also the base of $EBD6,X/Y for the list that follows: X 4-1 at $938A (sprite colours) and $9408 (backgrounds), Y 12-1 at $98D0 (the shift).

Thirteen colours ($EBD7-$EBE3) that shift one place every third frame ($98BE), the newest from $B5DF entering here: sprite colours at $938A, backgrounds at $9408; this first one alone at $6810, $6922 and $6AA9 (which copies it to sprite colours $E7ED-$E7F2).
Second of the thirteen colours at $EBD7; background colour at $971A.
Third of the thirteen colours at $EBD7; background colour at $9721.
Fourth of the thirteen colours at $EBD7; background colour at $9728.
Last, oldest, of the thirteen colours at $EBD7; base of LDA $EBE3,X at $9393 (X 4-1), the colours of sprites 0 and 2 in the band code at $9374.
Thirteen colours ($EBE4-$EBF0) that shift the other way: every third frame $98E9 moves them down one place and stores the newest, from $B5CB, at $EBF0. Read at $6DF2 and as $EBE4,X at $9742.
Second colour of the list at $EBE4; base of LDA $EBE5,Y at $98FB for the shift.
Last byte of the list at $EBE4, where $9912 stores each new colour.
Background colour that $997D picks from $B5DF on every fourth call; used at $936A, $6DDC and $97CB.
Colour that $999D picks from $B5CB; $92AC writes it into colour RAM at rows 8-9, columns 20-39 (the large 'sensi soft' of the title), and $970C uses it.

The title's clock: $9829 counts it up to $FF and starts each colour effect once the clock passes its threshold: $0A logo bar ($9884), $23 ($994A), $5A ($9916), $69 ($999D), $9B ($98BE), $C3 ($98E9), $FE ($996A, $997D). Cleared with the rest by $8FA0.

The game's start-up, stage one, jumped to from the entry at $6389 once $01 = $35; it runs from what becomes the title screen's memory. Interrupts off; copies 12 bytes from $EC20 to $001D-$0028; switches CIA 1's interrupts off ($DC0D = $7F, then read to acknowledge); sets the stack pointer to $7F; leaves X = $7F and Y = $42 for the indexed CIA 2 addresses of stage two and continues through JMP ($EC91). $EC91-$EC92 are the operand of STA $EC2C,X at $EC90, so the jump goes to $EC2C; stage two overwrites that pointer before it leaves, and wipes most of its own code.
absolute-mode store into zero page $001D-$0028
through the operand of the STA at $EC90: goes to $EC2C

Twelve bytes that stage one copies to $001D-$0028, a routine in zero page: LDA #$35 / STA $4B / STA $29 / STA $8F / STA $00 (the 6510's data-direction register) / PLA / RTI. The copy is intact in every snapshot taken later, but no JSR, JMP, vector or pointer to $001D (or $001C) was found and the self-modified jumps take their targets from tables that do not hold it: what it is for is unknown.

Start-up stage two, reached through JMP ($EC91) from $EC1D with X = $7F and Y = $42; also the first byte that its own wipe at $EC90 replaces (with RTS). It programs CIA 2 for the once-a-frame NMI and a free-running timer B, fills pages 1-3, installs the hardware vectors, wipes $EC2C-$EC8D, selects VIC bank 3, overwrites its jump pointer at $EC91 and jumps to $8F61, the title. Every CIA 2 register is reached through an indexed address that reads as CIA 1: STA $DC8F,X here is $DD0E. The steps are listed at $EC31.
$DC8F+$7F = $DD0E: CIA 2 timer A stopped

Low byte of the operand of STA $DC8F,X at $EC2E, not a variable; also the base of STA $EC2F,X at $ECAE, which with X = $62 writes the new CIA 2 port A value into $EC91, the low byte of the start-up's jump pointer.
High byte of that operand; the base of STA $EC30,X at $ECA3, which with X = $62 writes CIA 2's data-direction value into $EC92, the jump pointer's high byte.

Stage two from $EC31 to $ECB3, its steps in order. CIA 2, all through indexed addresses: timer B stopped ($DC90,X = $DD0F), its interrupts off ($DC8E,X = $DD0D, $7F), timer A = $4CC7 = 19,656 cycles, one PAL frame ($DC86,X = $DD05, $DCC2,Y = $DD04), timer B = $FFFF ($DC87,X = $DD06, $DCC5,Y = $DD07); zero page $86 = $FF. Waits for raster line $0A with bit 8 clear, then line $1E, starts both timers ($DCCC,Y and $DCCD,Y = 1) and enables the timer A NMI ($DD0D = $81), so the NMI comes at the same raster position every frame and timer B runs free for $7533's random numbers. Fills pages 1-3 with A = $81 exclusive-ORed with each index in turn; copies the vectors NMI $7C61, reset $0000, IRQ $7C73 from $B62D to $FFFA-$FFFF; writes $60 (RTS) to $EC2C and, calling $7533 before each further byte, its random values to $EC2D-$EC8D; sets CIA 2 port A bits 0-1 to output and 0 (VIC bank 3, $C000-$FFFF); stores those two port values over the jump pointer at $EC91-$EC92; JMP $8F61.
$DD0F: timer B stopped
$DD0D = $7F: CIA 2 interrupts off
$DD05 = $4C: timer A high
$DCC2+$42 = $DD04 = $C7: timer A low
$DD06 = $FF: timer B low
$DCC5+$42 = $DD07 = $FF: timer B high
$DD0E = 1: timer A runs
$DD0F = 1: timer B runs
$DD0D = $81: timer A NMI on
X = 0: RTS at $EC2C; then $7533's random bytes to $EC8D
X = $62: DDR value into $EC92
X = $62: port value into $EC91

55 bytes ($ECB4-$ECEA) never executed that decode as an older copy of the start-up's tail: EOR $66 / DEY / BNE, the vector copy from $B464 (LDA $B463,X / STA $FFF9,X), the self-wipe with LDA #$60 and JSR $7304 into $EC63-$ECC5, the VIC bank switch, STA $D013 of 2, and JMP $8D5D. The live code uses $B62D, $7533, $EC2C and $8F61 for these, so this is apparently left over from an earlier assembly in which those routines sat elsewhere. The title's screen clear ($8F41) overwrites it.

Three bytes before sprite $B4; base of LDA $ECFD,Y at $8218 (Y $3E-1), which moves sprite $B4's image down one row, each byte taken from three bytes earlier, while the Wizball sinks. The two bytes it reads here ($ECFE-$ECFF) land in $ED01-$ED02 and are zeroed straight after. In the entry image this is leftover screen text.

Sprite $B4 ($ED00-$ED3F), one of the play sprites built at run time in the part of the $EC00 screen that play does not show (sprites $B0-$BF, $EC00-$EFF7; only the top band's pointers at $EFF8 are used as a screen there). When the Wizball reaches glyph $BE (apparently a tube or crater mouth: $81C9 moves $B128 one level up or down) $81E9 copies its current spin frame into this sprite ($C400 + 64 x $B21A) and $8216 sinks it one row per call for 21 calls ($B213 = $15); $830A then draws the left half of the curved pipe into it. Messages are drawn into sprites $B4-$B9: 'game over' and 'player one' or 'team two' ($6A02-$6A3C), 'wot a wizace!' and 'level n completed' ($AE2A-$AE54). The routine at $646F, which the frame loop enters once $B874 is set (apparently the bonus stage), keeps a working copy of the wave script from $3902 in $ED02-$EDFF instead.
Byte 1 of sprite $B4's top row; $8226 zeroes it after each one-row sink.

Byte 2 of sprite $B4's top row, zeroed by $8229 after each sink. Also where $9CB2 (called at $64C1, in the routine at $646F) copies the wave script $3902-$39FF, to $ED02-$EDFF (STA $ED02,X, X 0-$FD); the sequencer at $9CEA reads it in 3-byte steps from $BB06: here the entry's first byte, a wave number or a control ($FD, $FE, $FF), at $9D05, $9D20 and $9D7A.
Byte 0 of sprite $B4's second row; in the wave-script copy the base of LDA $ED03,Y at $9CF2 and $9D63, each entry's second byte (compared with $BB04 and $BB05).

Byte 1 of sprite $B4's second row; in the wave-script copy the base of $ED04,Y at $9CFA-$9D02, each entry's third byte, a repeat count that $9D02 decrements in place, which is why the script is copied out of $3902 first.

Sprite $B5 ($ED40-$ED7F), below $B4 in the pipe sequence: $8334 scrolls it up one row per call (the base of STA $ED40,Y at $8347, Y 0-$3F, each byte from three bytes on) and blanks its last row ($ED7C-$ED7E); $830A's copies run into it as the pipe slides down; $6A3C draws the second line of the game-over message ('player one', 'team two' and so on) into it.
Second row of sprite $B5; base of LDA $ED43,Y at $8344, the source of the upward scroll (Y 0-$3F reads up to $ED82, the top row of sprite $B6).
Last row of sprite $B5, left byte; zeroed by $835A after each upward scroll.
Last row of sprite $B5, middle byte; zeroed by $8360.
Last row of sprite $B5, right byte; zeroed by $8366. $ED7F after it is the padding byte.
Sprite $B6 ($ED80-$EDBF), the right-hand partner of $B4: $830A copies the right half of the pipe (sprite 59, read from $CEBF) into it, the base of STA $ED80,Y at $8326.
Sprite $B7 ($EDC0-$EDFF), the right-hand partner of $B5: $8334 scrolls it up one row per call (the base of STA $EDC0,Y at $834D) and blanks its last row ($EDFC-$EDFE).
Second row of sprite $B7; base of LDA $EDC3,Y at $834A for the upward scroll (Y 0-$3F reads up to $EE02, the top of sprite $B8).
Last row of sprite $B7, left byte; zeroed by $8357.
Last row of sprite $B7, middle byte; zeroed by $835D.
Last row of sprite $B7, right byte; zeroed by $8363.
Padding byte of sprite $B8 ($EE00-$EE3F); base of STA $EE3F,Y at $9DEE (Y $40-1), which copies the empty cauldron (sprite 56) into sprite $B9.

Sprite $B9 ($EE40-$EE7F), the red cauldron at the bottom of the play screen (bottom-band pointer $F7F9, colour $B516 = 2). $9DE9 makes it from sprite 56; $9E0D-$9EC5 redraws it a row at a time for the level in $B12B, rows below the level from sprite 57. Base of STA $EE40,X at $9EB6, X being the row's offset plus $00, $40, $80 or $C0 for the four cauldrons.
Byte 1 of the red cauldron's top row; base of STA $EE41,X at $9EBC, the middle byte of each cauldron row.
Byte 2 of the red cauldron's top row; base of STA $EE42,X at $9EC2, the right-hand byte of each cauldron row.
Padding byte of the red cauldron; base of STA $EE7F,Y at $9DF1, which copies sprite 56 into sprite $BA, the green cauldron ($EE80-$EEBF, pointer $F7FA, colour $B517 = 5).
Padding byte of the green cauldron; base of STA $EEBF,Y at $9DF4, which copies sprite 56 into sprite $BB, the blue cauldron ($EEC0-$EEFF, pointer $F7FC, colour $B519 = 6).

Padding byte of the blue cauldron; base of STA $EEFF,Y at $7784 and $9DF7, which copy sprite 56 into sprite $BC, the fourth cauldron ($EF00-$EF3F, pointer $F7FD) in the colour to be mixed ($B51A, set per level at $77B8; 2, red, in play-start.vsf).

Middle byte of the fourth cauldron's top row. $9E26 copies it to $B874 whenever $B1CF and $B213 are both 0: it is 0 while that row is drawn from the empty cauldron (sprite 56) and $AA once it is drawn from the full one (sprite 57). So $B874 turns non-zero when the target cauldron is full, and the frame loop then leaves for $646F ($6416): apparently the colour is complete and the bonus stage follows.

Byte before the top band's sprite pointers $EFF8-$EFFF (the band at $89BB shows screen $EC00 with D018 = $B0 only for these); base of indexed accesses from 1: $7210 (X 8-1, the starting icons from $B4DE), $68FB (all $0C, the get-ready rings), $905E (all 5, the menu stars), $AFED-$AFF6 and $B05F (Y 6-1: saved, replaced from $B4DE and restored around the Wiz-lab), $72E4 and $B0A7 (the icon picked, $B258).
Icon 1's sprite pointer, thrust then anti-grav: 7 at the start ($7210), 3 once thrust is taken, 9 once both are ($7379-$7390). Title bands write it too ($925D, $92CD, $9358).
Icon 2's sprite pointer, beam then double: $0B at the start, 4 once beam is taken ($734B-$7357), 9 once double is ($7360).
Icon 3's sprite pointer, the catelite: 2, then 9 while the cat is out ($736B); $8665 puts 2 back when $B26C reaches 9.
Icon 4's sprite pointer, blazers: 6 from $7210; the only other write found is the title band's $8C at $9361.
Icon 5's sprite pointer, the sprays: 8 (wiz spray) at the start; $7325-$734A set $0A (cat spray) on the first take and then switch between $0A and 8 as the spray passes between Wiz and Cat.

Icon 7's sprite pointer, the shield: 0; 9 while a shield is on ($73CE, which also starts the shield timer $7F06 at $28); $7EA0 and $7EDC put 0 back when the timer runs out. Icon 6, the smart bomb ($EFFD, 1), has no write of its own found beyond $7210.

The text character set at $F000 (VIC bank 3), part one: glyphs $00-$1F ($F000-$F0FF) of the small font, in screen-code order: glyph 0 blank, the letters a-z at $01-$1A in a lower-case style, then [, pound, ], up-arrow and left-arrow. Shown on the $EC00 screens (D018 = $BC, $BD) and on the score line (D018 = $8C). The whole small font ($F000-$F1FF) is stored exclusive-ORed with $FF, the way the title wants it: there colour RAM is black and $D021 changes per band, so the letters show through in the background colour.

Small font glyphs $20-$33 ($F100-$F19F): space, the punctuation ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + , - . /, then the digits 0-3 in a square block style. The first byte, row 0 of the space, is the font's state flag: 0 when the glyphs are the right way round, $FF when inverted (as stored). $8C84 makes the font normal and $8C8D makes it inverted, each flipping $F000-$F1FF with EOR #$FF only when needed, and both copy the flag to $B276, the mask that $8E0E exclusive-ORs into text it draws into sprites. $770D reads the digits here ($F188 + 8 x level) for the level-number sprite.

Small font glyphs $34-$3F ($F1A0-$F1FF): digits 4-9, then block capitals H, I, U and P for the score line's '1UP', 'HI' and '2UP' ($3A-$3D), a blank ($3E) and '?' ($3F). This address is also the operand of BIT $F1A0 at $49C8 in the music driver, used to skip: $49DC branches to $49C9, where the operand bytes A0 F1 run as LDY #$F1.

Large gothic font, glyphs $40-$7F ($F200-$F3FF): the top halves of the letters a-p, two glyphs each (a = $40/$41 ... p = $5E/$5F), and their bottom halves 32 glyphs on ($60-$7F). A character is drawn 2 x 2 from the table at $B591 (glyph = $40 + entry) by $8D1F on screen and by $8E59 into sprites; i and l use only the left column. Stored the right way round; $8CBE inverts the whole large font ($F200-$F7FF) and $8CB5 restores it.

Large font glyphs $80-$93 ($F400-$F49F): the top halves of q-z (q = $80/$81 ... z = $92/$93); their bottom halves are at $A0-$B3. $F400-$F7FF doubles in play as the screen of the bottom band, which uses only its sprite pointers (see $F7F8).

Large font glyphs $94-$DD ($F4A0-$F6EF): '!' ($94/$95); the tops of the WIZBALL logo's W, I, Z, B and A ($96-$9F, text codes # $ % & '); the bottom halves of q-z, '!' and those logo letters ($A0-$BF); the tops of the digits 0-9 ($C0-$D3); the logo's L ($D4/$D5, code '(', used twice); blank tops ($D6-$DD, the space being $DC/$DD). This address is also the operand of BIT $F4A0 at $4C35, a skip: $4C49 branches to $4C36, where A0 F4 runs as LDY #$F4.

Large font glyphs $DE-$FE ($F6F0-$F7F6): $DE and $DF blank (the get-ready screen is filled with $DE, $68AD); the bottom halves of the digits ($E0-$F3) and of the logo's L ($F4/$F5); $F6, a small mark; $F7-$FE blank (the space's bottom is $FC/$FD). The first byte is the large font's state flag, as $F100 is the small font's: $8CB5 makes the font normal and $8CBE makes it inverted, flipping $F200-$F7FF with EOR #$FF when needed, and both copy the flag to $B277, the mask used by $8E59.
Last byte of glyph $FE; base of STA $F7F7,X at $8B7B (X 6-1), with which the bottom band ($8B46) sets its sprite pointers $F7F8-$F7FD from $B51D-$B522.

Glyph $FF of the $F000 set, used instead as the bottom band's sprite pointers: $8B46 shows the screen at $F400 (D018 = $DC) only to get this eight-byte block; the screen cells there ($F798-$F7E7, rows 23-24) are font data shown black on black. $8B7B writes the pointers for sprites 0-5 each frame: $A0 (the level digit), $B9 and $BA (red and green cauldrons), 0 (sprite 3 is off), $BB (blue), $BC (the target cauldron); $B51E is sometimes $38 or $B9 instead. In the entry image these eight bytes are A0 B9 BA 00 BB BC 45 FF exclusive-ORed with $FF, left there by an earlier run.
The play area's character set, $F800-$FFFF, selected for the landscape rows by $8A25 (D018 = $8E ORed with $B1FD). Glyph 0 ($F800-$F807) is blank: the empty sky.

Star-field glyphs $01-$5A ($F808-$FAD7) are written at run time: on every pass of the outer cycle $7540 clears them (this is the base of its STA $F808,X, which covers $F808-$F907) and plots one random pixel into each of five bands of 18 glyphs (144 bytes from $F808, $F898, $F928, $F9B8 and $FA48), and $747E then moves those five stars sideways a pixel at a time (their state is at $B1B4). The play screens tile the sky with glyphs $01-$5A, 18 across and 5 down, so each band's star recurs every 18 columns.
Star-field glyphs $21-$40 ($F908-$FA07); base of STA $F908,X in the clear loop at $7546.
Star-field glyphs $3B-$5A ($F9D8-$FAD7); base of STA $F9D8,X at $7549, the last of the three overlapping clear loops, which ends the cleared area at $FAD7.

Play-set glyphs $5B-$7F ($FAD8-$FBFF), the same in every snapshot: $5B-$72 a small solid block at four horizontal and six vertical offsets, the last eight cut off by the top or bottom of the cell (pre-shifted copies, as for drawing a small object at any pixel); $73 a two-row block over a dotted bottom row; $74 a nearly solid cell; $75-$76 a vertical bar; $77-$78 two diagonal shapes; $79-$7B a short dash at three heights; $7C-$7E a dotted bar at three heights; $7F a solid cell with a dotted foot. No byte of $2642-$3901, where the scenery tiles are, has a value in $5B-$7F, and none appears on the play screens of the snapshots; what draws them is unknown.

Play-set glyphs $80-$9F ($FC00-$FCFF): dots, speckled and grey textures for ground and rock. The scenery tiles at $2642 use $80-$8C and $8F-$9F; level 1's ground rows are $91, $8F/$90, $92 and $93-$97 (play-start.vsf, rows 18-22).

Play-set glyphs $A0-$FE ($FD00-$FFF7), written at run time: $77C6 copies the level's scenery glyphs here, 760 bytes (95 glyphs) from the word table at $B31C indexed by the level $B128 (blocks $300 apart from $0B42); $6743, in the routine at $646F, copies the small font ($F000-$F1FF) over $FD00-$FEFF instead (this is the base of its STA $FD00,Y). All zero in the entry image.
Play-set glyphs $C0-$DF ($FE00-$FEFF), the level block's second page, or the second half of the small font copied by $6743 (base of STA $FE00,Y at $674E).

Row 0 of play-set glyph $F6, not used as data here; the base of INC $FFB0,X at $93A5 with X = $D5, whose address wraps past $FFFF to $0085: the title band code at $9374 increments zero page $85 this way. $85 is also cleared by the NMI ($7C6B) and written at $8BC5; no read of it was found.

Row 2 of play-set glyph $FC as data; the base of LDA $FFE2,X at $90F8 with X $18-$1D, which reads $FFFA-$FFFF. On every call $90BD (the menu stars, also run by the get-ready loop) compares the hardware vectors with their source at $B62D-$B632 and increments $D021, changing the background colour, if any byte differs: a check against changed NMI, reset or IRQ vectors.
Byte before the hardware vectors (row 1 of play-set glyph $FF); base of STA $FFF9,X at $EC86 (X 6-1), with which the start-up copies the vectors from $B62D-$B632 to $FFFA-$FFFF. $FFF8-$FFF9 stay 0.
The NMI vector, $7C61 (CIA 2's timer A, once a frame), set by the start-up from $B62D; the RAM here is live because $01 = $35.
The reset vector in RAM, $0000, set from $B62F. The CPU reads the reset vector from the KERNAL ROM, which banks in at reset, so this copy is not used by a reset; it is compared with $B62F by $90F8.
The IRQ vector, $7C73, the raster interrupt that runs the display lists; set from $B631 and checked by $90F8.
